Michael Johnson has admitted the fallout from Grand Slam Track (GST) was “the most stress” he had faced for a long time and clarified the financial situation after its controversial demise, including an alleged “secret” payment to himself.

The four-time Olympic champion was at the heart of the league, which had its inaugural season in 2025 with meets in Kingston, Jamaica and in the US cities of Miami and Philadelphia.

The inaugural event in Kingston was in front of a barely third-full stadium, while the fourth and final meet scheduled in Los Angeles in June was cancelled and Grand Slam Track filed for bankruptcy in December 2025.

open image in gallery Grand Slam Track controversially collapsed under Michael Johnson’s watch ( AFP/Getty )

In March 2026, a legal filing by GST’s creditors accused Johnson of “secretly” paying himself $500,000 (£370,000) days before the season collapsed, a claim a GST representative said at the time was “unfounded and false”.

Johnson clarified the payment in an interview with The Telegraph, saying: “I’m happy to clear it up, because it’s the most hurtful thing and the exact opposite of what was reported.

“Our credit card was full at Grand Slam Track, because we were facing significant cash-flow issues. We had 96 athletes, plus companions, whom we needed to fly to Miami and Philadelphia.

“We had 170 people to house in hotels in both cities, and the credit card had no room left. I instructed our travel team to put it on my credit card, and I would be reimbursed for it.

“So, what I received was reimbursement. I also loaned the company 2m dollars (£1.5m) to make sure we took care of the athletes. I decided to forgo my own salary.”

open image in gallery Grand Slam Track failed after its inaugural season ( Getty Images )

Speaking about the stress surrounding the event’s breakdown, Johnson added: “It was 10 (out of 10). In Olympic sprinting, you have to deliver your best performance in seconds, and you get one opportunity every four years – there’s probably nothing more stressful than that. But this was the most stress I had dealt with in a very long time.

“I definitely had nights where I didn’t sleep, where I would be awake thinking, ‘This is on me. This headline just came out – do the athletes believe that?’ Those things weighed on me very heavily, and on my family as well.

“I was asking myself, ‘Are you stupid? Why did you do this? This is not what you need’.”

Johnson was a staple of the BBC’s athletics coverage for many years, and an incredibly popular pundit. He has not worked for the corporation since Grand Slam Track began but suggests there is a chance he could work for them again in the future.

“We’ll see where I am next year,” said Johnson. “It has been 22 years that I’ve worked for the BBC, and I love it. We’re in constant conversation about the future.”

Additional reporting by PA

News.content:

A convicted child rapist has been recaptured after escaping while on escorted community leave.

Cliff Lyons Dobbie, a restricted patient, absconded from Perth city centre in Scotland on Friday.

Dobbie was convicted of raping a 10-year-old girl in Glasgow while on bail for sexually abusing a 12-year-old boy in 1990.

He has been housed in secure units, including State Hospital Carstairs, ever since.

Dobbie was being treated as a missing person by Police Scotland and officers said on Friday that inquiries were ongoing to trace him.

Members of the public were warned not to approach him.

open image in gallery Dobbie was wearing white trainers, light blue ripped jeans, a salmon-coloured golf shirt and a light blue jumper ( Police Scotland )

On Saturday, police said that Dobbie had been caught.

Earlier, Inspector Kris McCall said that Dobbie had links to Glasgow and the surrounding areas, and said police wanted to trace him “as quickly as possible”.

He was described as white, about 5ft 3in, and of stocky and muscular build.

He is bald, has blue eyes, and has a noticeable squint which is more apparent when he is not wearing his glasses.

He was last seen wearing white trainers, light blue ripped jeans, a salmon-coloured golf shirt and a light blue jumper.

He also wore a black cap and thick black-rimmed glasses. Dobbie was carrying a black backpack and a black puffer jacket.

Police said he has distinctive tattoos on both arms, including an image of two blue tiger-like eyes on his right arm and a blue and red Rangers tattoo on his left arm. He speaks with a strong Glaswegian accent.

News.content:

Andy Burnham made a vow upon entering No 10 that he would “rewire” Britain, with a core aspect of his vision to deliver “the biggest council housebuilding drive since the post-war period”.

The prime minister admitted the country is in the grip of a severe housing crisis with millions struggling on unaffordable rents and a social housing backlog that now extends to 1.3million people.

However, the task for Mr Burnham is substantial. The PM’s predecessor Sir Keir Starmer pledged to build 1.5 million houses before the next election, a target that newly reinstated housing secretary Angela Rayner admitted was a “really difficult challenge”.

The government’s target to reach the figure through 300,000 new homes a year is already off pace. Only around 840,000 homes, around half the total target, are expected to be under construction by mid-2029, according to property agent Savills.

The Independent looks at the scale of the challenge ahead and what might need to change to accomplish his goals.

Burnham’s Brexit problem

open image in gallery Andy Burnham has promised a housing revolution, but can he deliver? ( AFP/Getty )

Many point to Britain’s decision to leave the European Union as a key factor in the decline in housebuilding. Brexit is estimated to have reduced the UK construction workforce by more than 200,000 people, a report by training group PfP Thrive found.

At the same time, construction materials in the UK have increased by 60 per cent, according to analysis by the UK Trade and Business Commission, compared to 35 per cent in the EU.

Housebuilding faltering, partially as a fault of Brexit, means that affordable housing is not being delivered. Sir Keir’s government pledged £39bn for the Social and Affordable Homes Programme (SAHP), to deliver around 300,000 properties within the 1.5m target.

And council housing is another matter altogether. This is technically property that is owned by local authorities, and usually offers a much cheaper ‘social rent’ for residents – around 50 per cent of market rates, compared to around 80 per cent for ‘affordable’ homes.

Rooftop Housing Group’s chief executive Boris Worrall told Inside Housing: “It has played out exactly as feared. Brexit has been a key factor in accelerating inequality and deepening the structural challenges the UK faces – including a shortage of affordable housing and a rising and unsustainable welfare bill [because of falling GDP]… We have built fewer homes than we would have done [had we remained in the EU]. It is that simple.”

Construction downturn

One reason Labour has fallen behind on its housebuilding targets has been due to increased costs on the housebuilding sector, says Steve Turner, executive director of the Home Builders Federation.

He told The Independent: “We did a report recently that showed that it's now £76,000 on average more expensive to build a house now than it was 5 years ago, and that's because material costs have gone up.”

Taxes and policy costs like building safety levies, landfill taxes and green initiatives are also all eating into private sector margins, he explained.

“These are probably the right thing to do,” Mr Turner adds, “but because you've layered them on over recent years, including increased affordable housing, it's got to the point now where not everything can be funded through development and sites are no longer viable.”

Continued concerns about the impacts of US president Donald Trump’s war in Iran and the political uncertainties festering over the UK for months meant that output from the construction industry declined at the fastest rate since the height of the Covid-19 pandemic.

The S&P Global UK construction PMI showed a reading of 38.2 in May, down from 39.7 in April and indicating a steep drop in overall business activity.

Any reading above the 50 threshold indicates that activity in the industry is increasing while anything below means it is contracting.

Can more council housing be built?

During the post-war peak in the 1970s, English local authorities built an average of 103,000 homes every year. In the five years leading up to 2025, they managed just 2,000 completions annually.

This is clearly a low point to start from. But there is a way to increase the amount of social housing and still deliver the target of 30,000 affordable homes a year, a new report from the Resolution Foundation has found.

open image in gallery ( Centre for Policy Studies / Onward )

The crucial measure is to ringfence the £39bn SAHP exclusively for social rent, dropping annual completions by 5,000 to 25,000, the think tank says.

Combined with tweaking developer rules and allowing housing associations to access cheap loans, this could be boosted to just over 30,000 affordable homes, 25,000 of which would be for social rent.

But this is still a “far cry” from the promise made by Mr Burnham, author Hannah Aldridge, senior research and policy analyst at the think tank, writes.

“And with the best will in the world, new homes still take years to build,” Ms Aldridge adds, noting that delivering at scale would require far more funding from the government.

To hit 300,000 homes for social rent, the government would need to boost its spending to £47bn by 2036, the report found.

What do local authorities need to make Burnham’s vision happen?

While town halls have welcomed Mr Burnham’s focus on social rent, council leaders warn that the right message cannot overcome longstanding financial barriers.

Councils across England are grappling with historic housing debt, which has risen from £29bn in 2012 to £31bn. This was meant to be paid off beginning in 2012, but has instead risen as Right to Buy proliferated under the Conservative government, meaning less revenue for councils.

Rent freezes and caps during the pandemic – which protected tenants – meant that councils were forced to lose income from their homes, adding more to this debt.

Many council leaders are calling for the historic housing debt burden to be restructured, so that it is more realistic for councils to build new homes.

open image in gallery Housing secretary Angela Rayner has said delivering Labour’s target of 1.5m homes is a ‘really difficult challenge’ ( AFP/Getty )

Several have also advised that the playing field should be levelled for councils and housing associations.

Housing associations will soon be able to access £2.5bn of loans at 0.1 per cent, while local authorities are stuck paying Public Works Loan Board rates which fluctuate between 4 and 5 per cent.

James McAsh, the Green Party leader of Southwark Council, said: “We are straightforwardly paying more to borrow than a housing association building the exact same homes. And I can see no justification for why that should be the case.”

His authority has built 689 council houses in 2024/25, making it the top builder of the past few years. But Mr McAsh warns that the work may have to slow down without more support from the government.

Mr McAsh said: “We're already trying to build as many council houses as we can, we don't need Andy Burnham to tell us to do that. What we need from Andy Burnham is funding to allow us to do it.”

The new prime minister’s pledge represents a clear political shift toward tackling Britain's housing crisis through genuinely affordable homes, which policy experts and council leaders have welcomed.

But delivering a post-war scale building revolution may remain out of reach without serious funding commitments.

Many will be hoping that the new Labour government’s first Budget in October may deliver the answers they are looking for.

Passengers are facing travel chaos at Bristol airport after a runway defect suspended operations for hours leading to cancellations and delays.

Many were left stranded on Friday after the airport’s runway was closed at around 6pm. It remained shut, with no flights coming in or out, until 8am on Saturday, but operations have now resumed.

Though the runway has reopened, passengers are now facing hours of delays, with multiple flights affected.

An updated statement on the airport’s website said: “Flights have resumed at Bristol Airport this morning. There will be some disruption to some flights today and customers are advised to refer to their airlines with any flight queries. We apologise for any inconvenience caused.”

Earlier, the airport said that it had suspended operations to assess and repair a “defect on the runway.”

If you have been affected by the runway closure at Bristol airport, please get in touch by emailing daniel.haygarth@independent.co.uk

Among the many flights to be delayed this morning, according to the airport’s online departures board, are the 5.55am service to Faro, which is scheduled to take off at 10.40am, and the 6.20am flight to Menorca, which is expected to depart at 11.30am.

Cancelled or delayed flights: What are my rights to a refund? Check here

Sophie Brazier-Smith was due to fly from Bristol to Nice on Friday night to see family for the summer and said the “experience has been extremely frustrating and confusing”.

She told The Independent: “I completely understand closing a runway due to a defect, but we were actually boarded onto our easyJet flight between 6.15 and 6.20pm.

“I later found out the airport had decided to suspend all flights at 6.08pm. The decision to board us and keep us on the flight for an hour is baffling.”

Ms Brazier Smith said there was “absolutely no information” once they disembarked the plane and the airport had “descended into chaos.”

She added: “We got home and have a new flight booked for Monday, but I am extremely unhappy with the way this situation was handled on all fronts.”

Paul Smith, who was due to fly to Glasgow on Friday for his son's 20th birthday but had to cancel the holiday, told the BBC: "The communication, advice and support for passengers has been really poor”.

Mr Smith said there were no announcements for more than an hour on Friday and claimed that he was only getting information from EasyJet staff in the departure lounge.

On X, responding to a passenger asking if flights have been cancelled today, airline Jet2 said: “Our flights have not been cancelled. They are currently delayed, and are expected to fly later today when the runway re-opens.”

A Bristol Airport spokesperson told The Independent: “We’re very sorry to all customers who experienced disruption during this busy time. Tannoy announcements were made within the terminal and customers were advised to contact airlines regarding their flights.

“We realise how frustrating this was for all those affected, but the safety of our customers and staff is of paramount importance, which is why runway operations were temporarily suspended. Repairs took place throughout the night to repair the defect.”

EasyJet has been contacted for comment.

News.title: Met Police admit serial sex offender Simon Levy’s murder victim could have been saved
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

A senior Metropolitan police detective has admitted that Simon Levy’s second murder victim could have been saved, as the force faces questions over its handling of the serial sex attacker.

Levy, of Tottenham, north London, was found guilty by a jury at the Old Bailey on Friday for murdering Carmenza Valencia-Trujillo, 53, and Sheryl Wilkins, 39, five months apart last year. The killings came after he subjected a third woman to a brutal sex attack in the same car park where Ms Wilkins’ body was later found.

The timeline of his crimes reveals a string of errors where officials failed to stop a dangerous predator who was already a registered sex offender and was on bail as his attacks on women escalated to double murder.

Questioned on the Met’s approach to the case by the BBC, deputy assistant commissioner Kevin Southworth said: “There were opportunities here to save some of the victims from their fate.”

Regarding the murder of Ms Wilkins and whether her life could have been saved, Mr Southworth said: “I think so”.

Asked if the Met had contributed to her death, he said: “I think we have to wait for the outcome of the [police watchdog] IOPC inquiry, but certainly I’ve apologised to Sheryl Wilkins’ family - to her mother and her sister - wholeheartedly for any role that we’ve played in failing to protect her.”

Levy, 40, fatally suffocated Ms Valencia-Trujillo and Ms Wilkins in sexually motivated attacks, with Ms Valencia-Trujillo found in a largely abandoned block of flats on the Aylesbury estate in south-east London, and Ms Wilkins behind a car park wall near Tottenham High Road, north London.

The jury also found Levy guilty of two counts of rape, grievous bodily harm with intent and the non-fatal smothering of the third woman whose collarbone was broken.

Levy’s crime spree spanned from 2018 to 2025 – the Metropolitan Police, British Transport Police (BTP), and Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) are all facing serious questions over how he was allowed to grope, rape and murder women.

open image in gallery Simon Levy will be sentenced on Wednesday ( Metropolitan Police )

The Met, BTP and Crown Prosecution Service have all admitted failings in how they dealt with Levy.

Levy was previously jailed in 2021 for groping two women in the summer of 2018, one at Notting Hill Carnival and the other at a party in Camden.

He sexually assaulted a prison guard while behind bars in 2022 but was still released the following year, going on to sexually assault a woman on the Tube in October 2023 and allegedly rape another in May 2024, for which he was recalled to prison and released again in August that year.

open image in gallery Simon Levy, 40, has been found guilty at the Old Bailey of murdering two women and raping a third ( Metropolitan Police )

Levy was arrested by BTP in November 2024 for four sexual assaults on the Tube, for which he has since been separately convicted. But delays in organising an identification parade until the following April left him free to carry out the rape and first murder.

When police took details of his Oyster card, BTP officers did not realise that it had been stolen from a bus driver, meaning Levy had a free travel pass that he used on the day he murdered Ms Valencia-Trujillo.

Following her death, he was released on bail at two magistrates’ court hearings in May and June 2025, with the CPS admitting that it had not opposed bail at the first hearing, and the prosecutor had not given the court all the relevant information for consideration at the second hearing.

There were another three crown court hearings that he failed to attend for various reasons, yet no arrest warrant was requested.

Less than two weeks after a hearing on 11 August, he murdered Ms Wilkins.

The murders of Ms Valencia-Trujillo in March and Ms Wilkins in August were interspersed with sexual assaults on six women on the Tube and Overground.

An Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) spokesperson said it was investigating the management of Levy from his first conviction in September 2021 up to his arrest in September 2025.

It said: “Our independent investigation began in January following a voluntary conduct referral from the force, relating to alleged failures by two officers in his management following his prison release on licence in February 2023.

“We are examining whether action could or should have been taken to prevent his reoffending, and if all officers involved in his management followed policies, procedures, and training.

“We are also assessing whether any learning, whether individual, force-wide, or nationally or other changes should be implemented in light of the events under investigation.

“At this stage, we have served a gross misconduct notice on a police constable and a misconduct notice on a detective sergeant, which means that the actions of those officers are under investigation.

“The serving of conduct notices does not necessarily mean disciplinary proceedings will follow.”

Judge Mark Lucraft KC adjourned sentencing until Wednesday 12 August and remanded Levy into custody.

Actor and comedian Jessie Cave says she has made more money from one year of sharing hairbrushing videos on OnlyFans than she has done throughout her “entire acting career”.

The performer, 39, who is best known for her role as Lavender Brown in the Harry Potter films, started to post videos showing herself brushing her long hair on the social media platform last year, after dealing with rejection in the entertainment industry and struggling financially.

OnlyFans is a subscription-based platform best known for its adult content, although it is also home to plenty of creators who share non-sexual content too.

Cave was clear from the start that her account would not be “a sexual one” and would instead focus on “sensual” videos of her hair.

Speaking to The Times, Cave, who shares four children with comedian fiancé Alfie Brown, said that she had reached “a point of complete desperation” after being rejected from an audition.

“I couldn’t go and, say, work in a supermarket because I can’t afford the childcare, and also I don’t want people shouting Harry Potter spells at me as I work at Tesco,” she told the paper.

“I could retrain but I can’t afford to do a degree. I had a breakdown and I thought, that’s it with acting, I give up. But also we have no money. It was a point of complete desperation.”

open image in gallery The actor turned to OnlyFans after struggling to land acting roles ( Getty )

She initially thought that she would be on OnlyFans “for a few months” to “make five grand” and buy herself some “time to work out what we’re going to do”, but instead the income she has made on the platform has "genuinely saved our lives”.

Her subscribers pay $6 each month for access to her content, and she also earns additional income from “paid-for messages”.

Within just one day, she told The Times, she managed to earn back the £15,000 cost of her accommodation at the Edinburgh Fringe the year before, and she has “earned more, easily, than my entire acting career within one year”.

The actor admitted that there is “a stigma” attached to the platform because of its association with adult content, and said that she initially “didn’t really understand the risk of people thinking I’m doing porn”.

open image in gallery Jessie Cave, second from right, with the cast of ‘Harry Potter’ ( PA Archive )

Last year, Cave claimed that she had been left off the line-up at a fan convention because of her account.

“I found out that I didn’t get booked for a Harry Potter convention recently, as I’m now doing OnlyFans,” she wrote in her Substack.

“They explained it was because it’s a ‘family show and OnlyFans is affiliated with porn,’” she added. “This was baffling to me as some actors who do conventions (most actors, actually) have done TV and films in which they’ve done sex scenes and nudity. I’m just playing with my hair!”

OnlyFans has become a popular side gig for celebrities. In 2024, singer Lily Allen used the platform to share photos of her feet to paid subscribers, while musician Kate Nash has also used her account to raise funds for her live tour.

News.title: Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong
News.content:
Aston Villa 1 Bayern Munich 2

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

News.title: Suspected Ebola case on packed Congo river boat sparks testing rush
News.content:
Congolese health authorities have intercepted and detained a river boat on its way to the capital after a suspected Ebola case onboard.

Authorities have set up a mobile clinic to test more than 200 passengers after one of them disembarked and died earlier on the voyage.

The boat travelling from the northeastern commercial hub of Kisangani was stopped and held in Maluku, some 40 miles from Kinshasa.

Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is dealing with its worst ever outbreak of the viral haemorrhagic fever, which has seen nearly 4,000 cases and killed around 1,801 people according to the latest government figures.

Samuel Roger Kamba, the health minister, said a 32-year-old man had disembarked in Pimu in Mongala province, before developing ‌suspected Ebola symptoms and dying.

“We did not say it was Ebola. We said there was a suspected case for which we are being cautious,” the health minister told a press conference, according to MediaCongo, a local news site.

He said there had been no other reports of deaths among travellers.

The virus has so far spread to five provinces, though more than 90 per cent of cases have been recorded in the north eastern Ituri region.

News.title: El Nino could cause explosion of rabid seals, animal health experts warn
News.content:
This year’s El Nino weather event risks propelling an outbreak of rabid seals around the world, the world’s animal health body has warned.

Countries in South America and Australasia are being urged to look for signs the deadly infectious disease has reached their waters, only two years after it was first confirmed in South Africa.

The 2024 discovery of rabies in South Africa’s Cape fur seals was the first significant outbreak ever found in marine mammals and has been described as a “significant shift in rabies ecology”.

More than 100 cases have been confirmed in South Africa and Namibia since then, raising fears that aggressive rabid seals could infect humans, pets and other wildlife.

Changing patterns in fish stocks caused by the El Nino phenomenon now potentially risk widening the spread, as uninfected seal populations migrate for food and come into contact with rabid colleagues.

Scientists believe warming sea temperatures off Antarctica could send seal populations northwards into Southern African waters, where they could be exposed to rabies.

They could then return to their home waters, taking the virus with them and infecting other seal populations.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho introduces three ‘strict’ new rules at Real Madrid as he stamps his authority on squad
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO has reportedly laid down the law with three strict rules to kick off his Real Madrid revamp.

The former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham boss returned for his second stint at the Bernabeu in June – 13 years after he left.



Mourinho will be tasked with getting the best out of Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior this season.

And he has wasted no time tightening up discipline in a group with some big personalities.



According to AS, his new deal-breakers are centred around food, punctuality and recovery.

First off, Real’s nutritionist has been given more authority to instruct the players on what to eat for every meal, every day.

The nutritionist used to take on more of an advisory role, but their recommendations are now compulsory.

And although that takes freedom away from the players, they are said to have reacted positively to the change.

From that alone it is clear that Mourinho means business – and his approach to lateness is just as firm.

Whereas Los Blancos’ super-rich stars used to be fined if they were late to training or team meetings, Mourinho will now make them train separately from the main group.

The idea is to deal with all medical issues in-house so that club staff are across every detail.



Mourinho was a surprise appointment by Florentino Perez, with the veteran manager’s career appearing to tail off during stints in Turkey and Portugal.

Sports.title: Georgina Rodriguez wows fans in green leggings and tank top as she enjoys gym session ahead of Cristiano Ronaldo wedding
Sports.content:
GEORGINA RODRIGUEZ was filmed getting a sweat on at the gym ahead of her and Cristiano Ronaldo’s wedding.

The loved-up pair are set to get hitched on Ronaldo‘s home island of Madeira this weekend.



A cathedral in Funchal has been hired out before a glitzy reception at the five-star Savoy Palace hotel.

And Georgina, 32, has been getting ready for the big day by putting in work at the gym.





The mum-of-six huffed and puffed her way through a set of split squats in a pair of crisp white trainers, green leggings and a tank top.

The footage posted by Mirad Magazine was accompanied by a smattering of supportive comments.

One fan wrote: “Gorgeous.”

And another added: “Beautiful, diva, wonderful.”



Georgina talked up her love of the gym in a recent Instagram post which she used to strike back at body shamers.

She wrote: “I work out because it makes me happy. Because I’m passionate about it. Because that hour at the gym is one of the best moments of my day.

“It gives me health, peace of mind, discipline, energy, and well-being.



“It’s never been a struggle to lose weight; it’s always been a way of taking care of myself.”

Sports.title: Why is Preston vs Huddersfield Carabao Cup game being played at Goodison Park?
Sports.content:
IT has been 15 months since Goodison Park hosted a competitive men’s football match – but Everton’s former ground will be in use this weekend for Preston’s Carabao Cup first round match against Huddersfield.

The iconic stadium has been the home of Everton for 133 years before the men’s side relocated to the Hill Dickinson Stadium during the 2025/26 campaign.

Since then, Goodison has become the primary residence to the women’s team who finished 8th in the Women’s Super League last season.



But this weekend will be like no other as Preston are hosting Huddersfield at the 39,000-seater venue, meaning that there shouldn’t be any Toffees persuasion in the crowd.



And SunSport can reveal the reason why this is happening.

Why is Preston vs Huddersfield at Goodison Park?

Preston have spent £1.5million on a new hybrid pitch at Deepdale – their own historic home turf.

And ground staff want to wait until their first Championship home game of the campaign against Wolves on August 22 before exposing it to match action.

So the club have managed to strike a deal with the Merseyside giants which allows them to host their Carabao Cup first round fixture at Goodison Park.

The club said in a statement: “Preston North End have agreed a deal with Everton to host the club’s first round Carabao Cup tie against Huddersfield Town.

“The Lilywhites applied to the EFL for permission to play at the alternative venue due to the installation of the new hybrid pitch at Deepdale.

“The pitch will be complete in time for the club’s first home league game against Wolverhampton Wanderers on Saturday 22nd August, but to ensure no issues after a significant £1.5m-plus investment, the decision was made to ask permission to play away from PR1 in round one.”



Preston vs Huddersfield will take place TODAY – Saturday, August 8 and it will get underway at 3pm BST.

When was the last men’s football match played at Goodison Park?

Goodison has not hosted men’s football since May last year, when Everton beat Southampton 2-0 in an emotional farewell.

Hill Dickinson Stadium, which cost £800m and took three and a half years to build, sits in a picturesque location at Bramley-Moore Dock and can hold 13,000 more fans.

On August 24, 2025, Everton won the first competitive match that was hosted at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Goals from Iliman Ndiaye and Jack Grealish were enough to seal a 2-0 win over Brighton.



And fans were treated to seeing the first-ever penalty save when Toffees keeper Jordan Pickford saved Danny Welbeck’s effort from the spot.

Sports.title: Liverpool agree shock loan deal for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo to relieve Andoni Iraola’s pre-season injury crisis
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL are set to sign Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo to ease their defensive injury woes.

The shock move for the Uruguayan will start as a season-long loan, but Liverpool will have the option to make it permanent next summer.



Fabrizio Romano claims that Barca have green-lighted the switch, which will be signed off by all parties in the next 24 hours.

Araujo, 27, has made more than 200 appearances for the Catalan giants and helped them win LaLiga in three of the past four seasons.



He also finished last campaign as the most senior member of the club’s captaincy group following the departure of Marc-Andre ter Stegen.

So his signing will go down as a major coup for new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola, who has been left light at the back by injuries.

Jeremy Jacquet is still recovering from a shoulder problem, Giovanni Leoni is not yet back after an ACL tear, while Joe Gomez has suffered a muscle issue in pre-season.

Add in Ibrahima Konate’s free transfer to Real Madrid and the fact Virgil van Dijk has not played since being given an extended break after the World Cup, and it is clear that the Reds desperately need extra cover at the back.

Araujo was a pillar of the Barcelona squad but only made 11 league starts last season.

“I feel different and I’m happy about it, because I’m more at ease, happier. I can enjoy what I love to do, which is playing football, and that helps a lot.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s ‘lover paid off with six-figure sum by Uefa while he ran football body’
Sports.content:
GI WHIZ Gianni Infantino’s ‘lover paid off with six-figure sum by Uefa while he ran football body’

UEFA paid off a six-figure sum to an alleged mistress of Gianni Infantino while he was its general secretary, it has been reported.

The woman received the money after their supposed relationship with the 56-year-old – while he was a top official at European football’s governing body, according to The Telegraph.



She is also alleged to have been promoted by the under-fire Fifa boss during their relationship.

Senior figures at Uefa claim the married dad-of-four ensured the woman left with the pay-off.



And after she left, the football body is understood to have paid for her to do an MBA at a business school.

In a statement on Friday night, Uefa admitted that a payment had been made and that it was aware of the allegations the woman was in a relationship with Infantino.



It said it had since “tightened” its regulations to “reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation”.

Infantino joined Uefa in 2000 and spent 16 years there before leaving to become Fifa president in February 2016.



A Fifa spokesperson said: “Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue.

“Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory.

“No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.

“All company actions related to employees, including any departure and severance packages, have always been approved by the appropriate directors in accordance with all applicable regulations.”

The alleged use of Uefa funds happened while Infantino was its general secretary, sources claimed and the woman was allegedly promoted to a management position while the relationship was taking place.



Uefa’s then president Michel Platini is said to have challenged him over the alleged affair and it was agreed she would leave with a pay-off.

As well as the pay-off it also forked out for the woman to take an MBA course at a business school which charged around £45,000 per year in fees, as part of the deal.

Sources also claimed that when the woman left, Infantino allegedly used his connections to secure a new lucrative post for the woman in a similar field.

A spokesman for Uefa said: “We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school.

“The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time.



“Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all Uefa employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.”

Infantino, it is claimed, promoted his alleged lover, handing her a 30 per cent pay rise and a salary of around £147,000.

Her rapid rise is said to have raised eyebrows among colleagues and concerns he could be abusing his position to advance her.

During his time at Uefa he oversaw a footballing empire which had revenues of around £1.2billion and covered the game in 53 countries.

Infantino met his wife Leena Al Ashqar when she was working for the Lebanese Football Federation.



The pair married in 2001 and have four children.

It is not known if his wife was aware of the alleged relationship.

Matters are said to have come to a head when Platini learned about it, reports say.

A well-placed source told The Telegraph: “He made a huge mistake and it almost cost him his career.

“People [within Uefa] were telling Platini, ‘You have to fire him’.”



Another added: “Platini challenged Gianni, saying something like ‘she or you?’ and Gianni said, ‘She will leave’, and she left.”

Sources also claimed that Platini told Infantino that either he or the woman would have to leave.

The revelations come just a week after the collapse of Infantino’s financing scheme, which he announced nine days after the end of the World Cup.

The plan would have resulted in a group of investors controlling the commercial interests of Fifa’s top competitions for both men and women.

Uefa revolted against the plan, voting 55-0 to boycott the next World Cup, a move which helped defeat the plan.



It accused Fifa of attempting to trade away football’s soul.

The Concacaf nations in North and Central America then followed Uefa’s lead and condemned the plan.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fifa is a non-profit organisation which means in theory money made from the competition is ploughed back into football.

Infantino is said to have told his inner circle he has no plans to quit, having met senior staff in Morocco this week and he has allegedly appealed to US President Donald Trump for support.

Sports.title: Sky Sports legend Chris Kamara reveals cancer scare and urges men to get tested as he prepares for Great North Run
Sports.content:
CHRIS KAMARA revealed he had a prostate cancer scare.

And now he is urging men to bury their pride and embarrassment and get tested.



The Sky Sports legend, 68, has been supporting Prostate Cancer UK’s work for a decade, including ten charity walks with pal Jeff Stelling.

But a health scare after a routine blood test in 2024 sparked alarm bells for the former Swindon and Brentford midfielder – before he was given good news that it was not cancer.



Kammy told the Mirror: “Any man would feel scared about the prospect of getting prostate cancer.

“I’ve been working with the charity for more than a decade, so I know that early diagnosis is absolutely key.



“A routine test I had two years ago flagged up a slightly PSA level raised level.

“That was a scary thing to hear, but thankfully it turned out I didn’t have prostate cancer. After consistent monitoring, my levels remain the same.

“As men, it’s so important we look after ourselves and keep an eye on any changes.

“I do get up in the night to pee more now. But that’s a symptom of other conditions too, so check with your GP.



What is prostate cancer? Prostate cancer affects a small, walnut shaped gland that sits underneath the bladder and surrounds the urethra – the tube carrying pee outside the body. It usually grows bigger as you get older. The prostate’s main job is to help make semen – the fluid that carries sperm. Most men with early prostate cancer don’t have any signs or symptoms – that’s why it’s important to know about your risk. Possible symptoms include: Difficulty starting to urinate or emptying your bladder

A weak flow when you urinate

A feeling that your bladder hasn’t emptied properly

Dribbling urine after you finish urinating

Needing to urinate more often than usual, especially at night

A sudden need to urinate – you may sometimes leak urine before you get to the toilet If you do notice changes in the way you urinate, this is more likely to be a sign of an enlarged prostate, which is very common and non-cancerous. But it’s still a good idea to get it checked out. In the UK, about one in eight men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetime. Some factors may mean you’re more likely to get it. This includes: Getting older – it mainly affects men aged 50 or over

Having a family history of prostate cancer

Being Black If you have any of these risk factors or if you have any symptoms, speak to your GP. They can talk to you about your risk, and about the tests that are used to diagnose prostate cancer. Source: Prostate Cancer UK

“And I know none of us likes going to the doctor about ‘problems below the belt’ – but it’s a mountain you have to climb, so just do it.

“Doing the walks alongside my great mate Jeff and meeting so many affected by prostate cancer, or who were marching in honour of loved ones they had lost, really brought it home to me.

“Those stories are heartbreaking and inspirational at the same time, and having that knowledge of the disease certainly helped me deal with my scare.

“I want to raise as much awareness as I can, particularly for black men, who are at double the risk.



“Prostate Cancer UK have a brilliant risk checker on their website. It takes 30 seconds and may just save your life.

“The problem with prostate checking, it’s your genitals, and you feel embarrassed when you shouldn’t be.

“These doctors and nurses have seen it all before. Get over that problem and go and get yourself checked.”

Rather than climbing a mountain, as he did with Kilimanjaro in 2012, Kamara is preparing to run a half-marathon.

He is set to take on the 13.1-mile challenge at next month’s Great North Run in Newcastle to raise more money for Prostate Cancer UK.



Fittingly, Kammy is doing it alongside son Jack and fellow broadcaster Ben Shephard, who have both supported him through his other major health battle.

Kamara was diagnosed with speech apraxia due to an underactive thyroid – causing him to lose his ability to speak as usual and feeling like a “fraud”.

After various treatments and forms of recovery, Kamara has got the confidence to be back on TV – in large part thanks to Shephard, to whom Kamara went public with his condition in a Good Morning Britain interview in 2023.

Kamara – who is hoping to finish in three hours – added: “Ben has been amazing. He’s part of the reason I came back to do TV.

“He convinced me to do that GMB interview with him. I’m back partly down to his help and encouragement.



“I spent a couple of years feeling sorry for myself and thinking, ‘This is totally beyond me to ever consider getting back to walking, never mind jogging.’

“I wanted to give myself a real challenge to try and get back to somewhere near the person I was.

“I’m helping a lot of charities these days. I thought, ‘What would be the perfect challenge for me?’ To do a half marathon and make it to the finish line with all my problems.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Going down stairs I’m not so good, so going down hills is going to be a massive challenge.

“But Ben and my son Jack will guide me through that. They will make sure I get it done.”

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher admits Liverpool transfer 'worry' and issues Man Utd warning
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher admits Liverpool transfer 'worry' and issues Man Utd warning

Liverpool are pushing to buy Bradley Barcola, who Paris Saint-Germain value at a jaw-dropping £145million, but Jamie Carragher isn't convinced about the Reds' strategy

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher has voiced his concerns (Image: Football Ramble)

Jamie Carragher admits that he's a 'bit worried' about Liverpool's new approach to the transfer window. The Reds have had a relatively quiet summer, although things are beginning to ramp up amid their pursuit of top target Bradley Barcola.

‌



Liverpool are in talks with Paris Saint-Germain over the possibility of signing Barcola, who the French giants value at £145million. However, Carragher isn't convinced that he's the right move.

‌



After pointing out last month that the 23-year-old wouldn't be a like-for-like replacement for the departed Mo Salah, the Liverpool legend now says that his former club's pursuit of Barcola represents a change of strategy at Anfield. Voicing his concerns, Carragher used Manchester United's past troubles to warn Liverpool where they could be about to go wrong.

‌



"The thing that I've probably liked about United this summer is it feels like for years they're always obsessed with this big name, and I worry a little bit about my own club with that," he told the Football Ramble podcast. "What we did last summer - and I said this, and I didn't really like it - it felt like a Real Madrid summer.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool agree shock deal for Barcelona star as Andoni Iraola gets transfer wish READ MORE :

"[Florian] Wirtz, [Alexander] Isak, we're gonna get [Hugo] Ekitike, another striker for £80m even though we've got one for £125m. This summer it's all about Barcola.

‌



"I'm like, 'what about the days we had before when we were building that team under [Jurgen] Klopp, and we were getting players who people weren't quite sure about, and getting great value? I almost wanna go back to that."

Do you agree with Jamie Carragher? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola is Liverpool's top target (Image: Antonio Borga/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

‌



Carragher went on add: "What I would say about United, it doesn't feel like this summer they're on this mission to get this big name... Andrey Santos, who knows how he'll do? [Youri] Tielemans. Sort of what you might think, 'clever, people not expecting that, something a little bit different'.

"It's not about the name, it's about what's right for the team and the club. And it feels like United are going down that road which I think is probably healthy."

Sports.title: Liverpool agree shock deal for Barcelona star as Andoni Iraola gets transfer wish
Sports.content:
Liverpool agree shock deal for Barcelona star as Andoni Iraola gets transfer wish

Andoni Iraola has wanted defensive cover after injuries to Joe Gomez and Conor Bradley, and Liverpool have moved to sign someone who can play both at centre-back and right-back

View 2 Images Ronald Araujo will have a medical with Liverpool (Image: Sergio Ruiz/PRESSINPHOTO)

Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo to remedy their defensive injury crisis. Araujo, 27, will join the Reds on loan with an option to buy.

‌



The defender's move to Anfield has come from nowhere, as he was expected to continue at the Camp Nou after signing a new contract until 2031 last year. But Barcelona boss Hansi Flick sanctioned his exit after Liverpool lodged their interest.

‌



Andoni Iraola has been looking to sign a defender in light of injuries to both Joe Gomez and Conor Bradley. Although Araujo prefers to play as a centre-back, he can play also at right-back, providing cover for both positions which Liverpool lack depth in.

‌



The Uruguay international is now set to have a medical with Liverpool before linking up with his new team-mates which could be as soon as this weekend. Araujo has spent eight years at Barcelona, making 213 appearances and scoring 14 goals.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Why Yan Diomande decided against Liverpool transfer after meeting Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

The 6ft 3in right-footer has also won eight trophies, including three La Liga titles. His career under Flick has been blighted by health problems, struggling to nail down a place in the German's starting line-up.

‌



Araujo missed the first half of the 2024-25 season due to a serious hamstring injury, and last season, he took a month out after being granted a leave of absence to 'take care of himself emotionally'. The decision came after he received a red card against Chelsea in a Champions League fixture.

"I'd been dealing with anxiety for a year and a half that turned into depression, and I was playing like that," Araujo revealed to Mundo Deportivo. "That doesn't help, because on the field you don't really feel like yourself.

Will Ronald Araujo be a good signing for Liverpool? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Ronald Araujo has won three La Liga titles (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

"You know your worth and what you can contribute on the field, and when I wasn't feeling well, I knew something was wrong. That day I realised that was it, that I needed to talk to professionals and the club so they could help me."

Araujo could make his debut for Liverpool when Iraola's side travel to Newcastle in their Premier League opener on Sunday, August 23. Prior to that, Liverpool will face Monaco and Como in pre-season friendlies at Anfield.

Sports.title: What happened to the last West Ham starting XI that were embarrassed in Carabao Cup round one
Sports.content:
What happened to the last West Ham starting XI that were embarrassed in Carabao Cup round one

West Ham are set to play a League Cup first round match for the first time in more than a decade

View 5 Images Sam Allardyce's West Ham were stunned in the League Cup in 2011 (Image: Nicky Hayes/Shutterstock)

West Ham's relegation from the Premier League has brought plenty of upheaval and not just in terms of squad ins and outs. It also means the Hammers will play in the opening round of the Carabao Cup for the first time in more than a decade.

‌



Nuno Espirito Santo's team face Portsmouth this weekend before beginning their Championship campaign eight days later. It is their first time entering the League Cup at this stage since they were last in the second tier, back in 2011.

‌



In fact, so much time has passed since then that it was called the Carling Cup rather than the Carabao Cup when West Ham hosted Aldershot in August 2011. The match was played at Upton Park, the ground the London side left in 2016.

‌



Sam Allardyce was in the dugout for the Aldershot match, with his team falling to a shock 2-1 defeat against the League Two side. Here, we've taken a look at the players who turned out for the Hammers that night.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Carabao Cup draw confirmed as final fixtures announced for round one READ MORE :

Ruud Boffin

Belgian goalkeeper Boffin played just three times for West Ham. The first came in the Premier League, on a snowy day against Blackburn and the last came against Sheffield Wednesday in the 2011/12 FA Cup, a few months after his Aldershot start.

‌



He left West Ham in the summer of 2012 and spent the following decade in Turkey, racking up a century of appearances for both Eskisehirspor and Antalyaspor before retiring in 2022. He scored his only career goal for the former when a free-kick from deep inside his own half flew into the opposition net without bouncing.

Julien Faubert

Faubert was known among fans of other clubs for his unexpected loan stint at Real Madrid but the France international's best West Ham form came after he returned from that stint. Having played as a winger early in his career, he was used as a full-back under Allardyce and predecessor Avram Grant.

View 5 Images Julien Faubert stayed to help West Ham win promotion (Image: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images)

‌

The 2012 play-off final would be his last Hammers game, after which he travelled the world. He had spells in Turkey, France, Scotland, Finland and Borneo - also playing international football for Martinique after switching his FIFA nationality - before retiring in 2020.

Winston Reid

Reid was one of the relegated stars who stayed and helped West Ham return to the Premier League. The New Zealander went on to captain the team and became a fan favourite, even scoring the last ever league goal at Upton Park.

‌



He was blighted by injuries in the latter part of his Hammers career and had loan spells with Sporting Kansas City and Brentford, playing his final club match in 2021. The centre-back was also handed an international farewell the following year, captaining the All Whites against Australia before hanging up his boots.

Callum McNaughton

Homegrown centre-back McNaughton was making his debut against Aldershot but it ended up in a nightmare. After being caught in possession inside his own half, he committed a last-man foul on Danny Hylton and was shown a straight red card.

View 5 Images Callum McNaughton (centre) was sent off on his debut (Image: Graham Chadwick/ANL/Shutterstock)

‌



McNaughton was loaned to AFC Wimbledon the following month and joined the League Two side permanently in January 2012. He spent most of his career in non-league football before heading to the United States for a career in teaching and football coaching,

George McCartney

Northern Ireland international McCartney was in his second Hammers spell, rejoining on loan from Sunderland as one of Allardyce's first signings. He would go on to sign permanently after promotion and finished his career at Upton Park.

Now 45 years old, he has dipped his toe into coaching. He has spent the last few years with Linfield in his home country, working as an assistant to former international team-mate David Healy.

‌



Pablo Barrera

Barrera joined West Ham after impressing for Mexico at the 2010 World Cup but underwhelmed during the relegation campaign. He would end up leaving on loan just days after the Aldershot game, spending the season in Spain with Real Zaragoza.

He would return to Mexico after that year in La Liga, playing more than 300 Liga MX games before retiring in 2025. The 39-year-old finished his career at Queretaro, with whom he racked up a century of league appearances.

Junior Stanislas

View 5 Images Stanislas scored West Ham's goal (Image: Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images)

‌



Academy graduate Stanislas scored West Ham's goal against Aldershot after good pressure from Barrera forced a mistake. However, both men would be gone within a week of the defeat, with the England Under-21 international completing a permanent move to Burnley.

Eddie Howe, the manager who brought him to Turf Moor, would later engineer another reunion at Bournemouth. Stanislas spent the best part of a decade on the south coast before retiring in 2023 and has since moved into coaching, most recently working under Kieran McKenna at Ipswich.

Kevin Nolan

Nolan arrived as a marquee signing, taking the captain's armband after Matt Upson's departure. The former Newcastle and Bolton man linked up well with Allardyce again, helping clinch promotion before top scoring for the Hammers in the 2012/13 Premier League.

‌



He moved into management after leaving East London in 2015, with spells at Leyton Orient (as player-manager) and Notts County. After returning to West Ham as part of David Moyes' coaching staff, he spent time in the England youth set-up before a spell in charge of Northampton Town which ended in March this year.

Freddie Sears

Academy graduate Sears burst onto the scene as a teenage striker but was used more as a wide forward as his career progressed. He played 10 Championship games under Allardyce but joined Colchester on loan before the end of the season and later moved there permanently.

It was at Ipswich where the Essex-born talent established himself, playing more than 200 league games for the Tractor Boys. Now 36, he has returned to his roots as a goal-getter after dropping down to non-league, with his 29 league goals for Maldon & Tiptree last term making him the top scorer in the Isthmian League North.

‌



Frederic Piquionne

View 5 Images Frederic Piquionne briefly spent time on the coaching staff at Everton women (Image: Charlotte Tattersall - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

Piquionne followed former manager Grant from Portsmouth to West Ham and ultimately suffered a second successive Premier League relegation. The striker, who won international caps for both France and Martinique, scored twice in the first half of the Championship season before making a loan switch to Doncaster Rovers.

The 47-year-old rounded off his career with spells in the United States, France and India before moving into coaching. He had a brief stint as assistant manager at Everton women when compatriot Jean-Luc Vasseur was in the dugout.

Article continues below

John Carew

Norwegian striker Carew was making his first Hammers start against Aldershot and would end the season with two league goals. He left at the end of the season and retired a little over a year later after failing to find a new club.

Since quitting football, the former Valencia star has embarked on a career change. He is now a professional actor, featuring in a number of Norwegian and English-language productions including Netflix series Home for Christmas.

Sports.title: Celtic's dream end to transfer window as £17m duo signs and World Cup star stays put
Sports.content:
Celtic's dream end to transfer window as £17m duo signs and World Cup star stays put

Celtic have made two attacking signings so far this window and are continuing their quest to build a Champions League-ready squad

View 5 Images Martin O'Neill plans to lead Celtic to more success this season (Image: Getty)

Celtic have signed the fewest players in the Scottish Premiership so far this summer. But Martin O'Neill has championed "quality over quantity."

‌



It was Camilo Duran who became the first to enter the gates of Parkhead, signing a five-year deal from Qarabag for around £6million. Next up was long-term target Kasper Hogh, who broke the club's transfer record when he arrived for £11m.

‌



The former Bodo/Glimt striker penned a four-year contract with the option of a further year. This duo scored a combined 10 goals in the Champions League last season. But fans will not be satisfied with these two signings to end the window, especially if they are to lose key players.

‌



Arne Engels has been heavily linked with a move to West Ham, with the Hoops bracing themselves for a third bid from the Championship side. Here, Mirror Football details what a perfect ending to the summer could look like for O'Neill's Celtic.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

OPINION Man Utd dream attack as Marcus Rashford exits plus free agent striker and World Cup star join by Abbie Meehan

‌



£17m duo signs

The main transfer target for Celtic is Real Oviedo's Haissem Hassan. The Egyptian winger impressed at the World Cup, assisting once and running the show for a period against Argentina.

Oviedo-based newspaper La Nuevo Espana claims that Celtic are pushing forward for the 24-year-old with a move to Parkhead now extremely likely. Sky Sports reports that an initial bid of £6m has been submitted and it could rise to around £9m if all bonuses are met.

View 5 Images A deal involving Hassan is moving quick (Image: Getty)

‌



Frosinone's Fares Ghedjemis is the other star Celtic are interested in - although they may have to compete with bitter rivals Rangers for the 23-year-old. The Hoops had been keen on the Algeria international in January but were unable to get a deal over the line.

Now, they have reignited this interest and Frosinone reportedly want at least £8m for his signature. It is understood that the Italian outfit rejected a bid of a similar price from the Gers, who have since moved on to target Celta Vigo winger Couhaib Driouech.

View 5 Images Signing Ghedjemis is a tough ask for the Hoops (Image: Getty)

‌



Celtic could now swoop in and stump up the cash for Ghedjemis. This would represent a dreamy £17m outlay for both players, but fans would see this as a reasonable price to pay ahead of their Champions League qualifying match-up with LASK.

World Cup star stays put

Alistair Johnston has been attracting considerable interest following his impressive performances for Canada at the World Cup. He started every game for the host nation and reached the round of 16, where he was eliminated 3-0 by Morocco.

Throughout his Celtic career, the right-back has 21 goal contributions and is beloved by the fanbase for his tough-tackling and positive attitude. Yet Everton have registered an interest in the 27-year-old, with O'Neill confirming that manager David Moyes contacted him regarding Johnston.

‌



View 5 Images Johnston has earned plenty of interest (Image: Getty)

He said: "In fairness, David Moyes did call me last week and say that there would be contact. But I don't know how far that has progressed, if it has at all.

"But yeah, that would be disappointing obviously. But I suppose it's to be expected, you know, players who have done well. Our job is to try and do our best to keep them. If that's not possible, naturally, we'll have to try and get replacements in. To replace those players would be a difficult task."

‌



It seems like O'Neill has kept to his word for the time being as the Toffees' interest in the right-back has cooled off. The Daily Record has confirmed that the Premier League side are working on other options after failing to meet Celtic's £15m asking price. If the club want to end the window in style, keeping Johnston is a must.

Defensive reinforcements arrive

Should Celtic retain Johnston, they may opt to add to their defensive line with another loan move for Brentford's Benjamin Arthur. The 20-year-old arrived at Parkhead last season under the same circumstances, spending the second half of the campaign in Glasgow.

View 5 Images Arthur could return on loan (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

Reports claim that the Hoops have already seen a bid from rejected, with Arthur part of the Bees' long-term plans. The defender only made four appearances in the 2025/26 season, but this was clearly enough to impress O'Neill.

A loan move could be beneficial for all parties, giving Arthur some European experience and allowing Celtic's defensive line to relax knowing they have back-up waiting in the wings.

Sports.title: Man Utd have got go ahead from £255million transfer targets for summer moves
Sports.content:
Man Utd have got go ahead from £255million transfer targets for summer moves

Manchester United still have business to conduct in the summer transfer window, and multiple targets are reportedly open to joining them

View 5 Images Michael Carrick could look to target extra additions in defence and midfield (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United's summer recruitment drive is far from over as they look to bolster the squad ahead of a demanding campaign. Under Michael Carrick, the Red Devils have already secured key signatures - including goalkeeper Karl Darlow and midfield duo Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

‌



Yet, with domestic and European fixtures looming, United club chiefs would do well to add to Carrick's options, especially by targeting players who have reportedly opened the door for a move to Old Trafford.

‌



Front and centre on their defensive wishlist is said to Bologna centre-back Jhon Lucumi. United are currently positioned as the frontrunners to win the race for the 28-year-old before the window shuts. According to Quotidiano Sportivo, the Colombian defender is said to only want to join a 'big club', with United battling for his signature against Juventus, Nottingham Forest and Bournemouth.

‌



Lucumi has just 12 months remaining on his deal and is reportedly willing to move to United, who have already made their approach for the World Cup star, it has been claimed. The report also suggests the Serie A outfit are demanding €25million (£21.4m) plus €3million (£2.6m) in add-ons for his signature, with Juventus and Forest's proposals falling below their asking price.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Lucumi's arrival would reinforce United's defensive options, which were severely weakened last season by injuries to Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt. Carrick has successfully refreshed his midfield choices this summer, but could seek to further bolster his options in the engine room by pursuing a deal for either Carlos Baleba or Alex Scott.

‌



View 5 Images Jhon Lucumi has several suitors across Europe (Image: Getty)

The Brighton midfielder has been closely tracked by United over the past two summers, but a deal had never come to fruition due to the Seagulls placing a £100m price tag on the 22-year-old.

The Cameroonian was reportedly eager for a transfer, but any prospect of a deal being struck this summer was dealt a blow after he suffered an ankle ligament injury. This likely makes Scott a more attractive proposition, with a potential switch certainly aided by the Cherries midfielder reportedly being receptive to a move to Old Trafford.

‌



View 5 Images Carlos Baleba is a doubt for the start of the season (Image: Getty Images)

The 22-year-old is attracting fierce interest from across the Premier League, with Chelsea and Liverpool said to be monitoring his situation closely. The future England star shone brightly as Bournemouth secured European football last season and is believed to be valued at £70m by the club.

However, that figure could rise to £80m should a bidding war break out. Landing Scott therefore might not be straightforward either, which could lead United to pursue a more financially prudent deal in AS Roma midfielder Manu Kone instead.

‌



View 5 Images Alex Scott impressed hugely last season for Bournemouth (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

The Frenchman has reportedly given the green light to a potential switch to Manchester, with reports emerging from Italy suggesting that United have already reached an agreement on personal terms with the 25-year-old. The Italian club are said to be demanding approximately €60m (£51m) should they sanction Kone's departure.

‌



A transfer to United would certainly have the backing of former captain Patrice Evra, who spoke glowingly about his fellow countryman's abilities. The ex-France international told Stake: "I like Manu Kone's profile for the Premier League.
