Sports.title: Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer update as dressing room view on Konsa emerges
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer update as dressing room view on Konsa emerges

Liverpool have received updates on multiple transfer fronts as Andoni Iraola looks to add to his summer business

View 2 Images Liverpool have received a concerning update regarding their pursuit of PSG's Bradley Barcola (Image: FRANCK FIFE, AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool are running out of time to wrap up the business required to put them back in contention for Premier League honours this season. The Reds have already overhauled their coaching staff after Andoni Iraola replaced Arne Slot at the helm but the general consensus is that the Reds require more reinforcements.

‌



Weeks have passed since Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz were confirmed as Liverpool's first signings of the summer.

‌



A top-tier replacement for Mohamed Salah remains a pressing concern for the club entering an important stage of the transfer calendar. Mirror Football provides a breakdown of the latest transfer speculation around Anfield this weekend.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal enter Barcola race

Liverpool's pursuit of Bradley Barcola could become more complicated after Arsenal reportedly entered the race for his services. And it leaves the Reds at further risk of frustration after Real Madrid beat them to the signing of Yan Diomande.

Why Yan Diomande decided against Liverpool transfer after meeting Andoni Iraola READ MORE :

Barcola was tipped as Liverpool's back-up option, with talks reportedly underway to get a deal done. However, Arsenal have also been stumped by Real after Vinicius Jr allegedly considered a move to the Emirates before penning a contract extension.

‌



That's led them to pivot their interests in the search for a left winger, with Barcola seemingly their next top choice. Mikel Arteta has already brought in Christos Tzolis as a replacement for Leandro Trossard but he wants more competition for the role.

The Independent reported Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez and Everton forward Iliman Ndiaye are also being monitored by Arsenal. Alvarez has indicated he'd like to leave Los Rojiblancos but Diego Simeone doesn't want to sell.

That could steer the north Londoners further in Barcola's direction, which won't be welcome news at Anfield. The current Premier League champions are one of the few teams in England that may boast greater appeal than Liverpool in the current market.

The Reds have reportedly agreed personal terms with Barcola and are searching to find an agreement with PSG. The Parisiens were demanding as much as £145million for their player, though a more manageable figure of £109m has since emerged.

Dressing room view on Konsa transfer

View 2 Images Aston Villa players are reportedly 'increasingly concerned' Ezri Konsa will leave the club this summer (Image: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

‌



The Aston Villa squad are reported to be 'increasingly concerned' Ezri Konsa will leave this summer. That's according to the Daily Mail, which has suggested Liverpool target Konsa is edging closer to a move.

Despite already adding Jeremy Jacquet to their ranks this summer, more defensive reinforcements are believed to remain a priority at Anfield. That has perhaps been exacerbated by Joe Gomez's recent injury setback, while Jacquet and fellow youngster Giovanni Leoni are still regaining full fitness following injuries.

A major sticking point in Konsa's case would be Villa's supposed £60million valuation. That figure would be hefty for most centre-backs but particularly one who's set to turn 29 in October and has less than two years left on his contract.

Article continues below

It's frustrating for Liverpool, therefore, that Konsa could fit their requirements so succinctly. The England star can play at centre-back or right-back, the same two areas in which Liverpool's defence is most in need of reinforcements.

Manchester United have less than a month to secure further signings ahead of Michael Carrick's first full season in charge

Michael Carrick is reportedly on the hunt to capture another midfield signing for Manchester United this summer. The United boss already brought in Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos from Aston Villa and Chelsea last month, respectively.

‌



While the Englishman has also secured the youth signings of Tynan Thompson and Cristian Orozco, first-team arrivals have been lacking following the midfield duo. There are just two weeks until United's season-opener against Hull City on August 22, with fans certainly hoping their transfer business speeds up ahead of the new campaign.

‌



One reason for the lack of recent incomings could be disagreements at the executive level at Old Trafford, while a hefty offer for a United target is reportedly set to be submitted. Mirror Football delves into the latest Manchester United transfer headlines.

Midfield offer

Despite signing two midfielders, United have parted ways with Casemiro and will be without the injured Manuel Ugarte for most of the season. Carrick's side could be targeting a third addition in the engine room, with Borussia Dortmund and Germany star Felix Nmecha a reported target.

Sports.title: Gabriel Jesus' agent addresses Arsenal transfer exit after being spotted at rival club
Sports.content:
Gabriel Jesus' agent addresses Arsenal transfer exit after being spotted at rival club

Gabriel Jesus has been made available for a transfer by Arsenal this summer and his agent has now been spotted at the training ground of Napoli amid reported negotiations

View 2 Images Gabriel Jesus could leave Arsenal this summer (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Gabriel Jesus' agent has insisted that he was not at Napoli's training ground on Friday to discuss a potential transfer for the Arsenal striker. Jesus has entered the final year of his contract with Arsenal and, having fallen down the pecking order after injuries, could be let go this summer.

‌



The Gunners have Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz as their first-choice strikers and are in the market for another attacker, with Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez on the wish list after Vinicius Junior decided to stay with Real Madrid.

‌



Mikel Arteta is understood to have green lighted an exit for Jesus, who only made 14 Premier League appearances last season, as well as Gabriel Martinelli. The 29-year-old has been with Arsenal for four years and the club are keen to cash in, rather than lose him for nothing next year.

‌



Napoli are interested in signing Jesus, with Romelu Lukaku and Lorenzo Lucca potentially heading for the exit. Arsenal want a permanent transfer worth €20million (£17m), while the Italian giants are keen to negotiate that fee downwards.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal could break unwanted transfer record as Mikel Arteta green lights two deals READ MORE :

Jesus' agent Giovanni Branchini was spotted at Napoli's training ground in Castel di Sangro on Friday, heightening speculation that a deal could be close. But Branchini has insisted that he was visiting the club to see another of his clients, Napoli boss Massimiliano Allegri.

‌



“Allegri and I have been in touch, I came here today to come and visit him,” Branchini told Videoinformazioni.com. “He’s working hard and he’s happy with everything. He’s always had a good opinion of this team and is satisfied with the work that is being done.”

Quizzed on Jesus, Branchini said: “I haven’t spoken to Allegri about him.” And asked if Lukaku and Lucca would have to be sold for Jesus to join, he added: “In my line of work, the ‘ifs’ count for very little, not as much as they matter for you journalists. From my point of view, it’s better to not talk about speculation.”

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus could both be sold this summer (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

‌



Allegri will build his attack around Rasmus Hojlund in the 2026/27 season after the Danish striker completed a permanent £38m move from Manchester United following a successful loan spell. But there is room for another forward, with Lukaku poised to move on and Lucca facing an uncertain future too.

Arsenal have so far only managed to move on Leandro Trossard (£17m to Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (£14.7m to Porto), Karl Hein (£2.5m to Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (£7m to Everton) this summer. Arteta knows that shifting other fringe players will be key if they are to land a world-class attacker and a centre-back to provide cover for the injured William Saliba.

Jesus has struggled for consistency at Arsenal, with injuries hampering the Brazilian. He has failed to live up to his £45m fee from Manchester City in 2022 and has seen his chances of game time dramatically reduced by the arrival of Gyokeres last summer.

Sports.title: 'I'd rather fight Aaron for world title' - Walsh dismisses Stevie McKenna call-out
Sports.content:
Callum Walsh would entertain a fight against Aaron McKenna over Stephen McKenna, insisting all-Irish clashes only make sense with the world title on the line.

Walsh (16-0, 11 KOs) fights former European champion Tyler Denny on the undercard of Aaron McKenna's IBF world middleweight title showdown with Etinosa Oliha at Dublin's 3Arena this Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

It's the headline act of six middleweight bouts on a stacked card that also sees Stephen McKenna face Owen O'Neill over eight rounds before assuming corner duties for his younger, world title-chasing brother.

Walsh has been identified as a potential future opponent by Stephen McKenna (16-1, 15 KOs), but the unbeaten 25-year-old believes he's already at another level.

Responding to McKenna's challenge, Walsh told Sky Sports: "If there's anyone that I'm looking at, it would be the fella with the world title, not the fella with the loss.

"In my mind, it doesn't make sense unless it's for a world title. There are bigger names than Stevie McKenna calling me out.

"Shane Mosley Jr is a bigger fight than Stevie McKenna. His brother Aaron is fighting for the world title. If I was going to fight either of them, I'd fight Aaron for the world title."

Image: Walsh on the scales ahead of his middleweight fight against Denny (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa Boxing)

'It makes sense for him, not for me'

Walsh believes an all-Irish fight without a world title on the line could needlessly jeopardise the momentum middleweights are currently generating in Ireland.

"It's a big time for Irish boxing," he added. "As an Irish fighter from such a small place, there are three of us now in Zuffa Boxing. Why would we want to eliminate each other unless it's for a world title?

"If it's for a world title, at least you can get paid for it. You're going to be able to sell out an arena and put on a big show for everyone involved. Why have an all-Irish fight on an undercard somewhere when it doesn't make sense?

"It makes sense for him. It makes no sense at all for me. His brother's fighting for the world title. There are bigger names calling me out. I've had bigger fights. It doesn't make any sense."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stevie McKenna is determined to have an all-Ireland clash against Walsh should both of them emerge victorious at Zuffa Boxing 10 this weekend

Walsh believes Stephen McKenna would be better served avenging his sole loss as a professional, a majority-decision defeat to Lee Cutler in 2024.

"He doesn't even want to fight the fella who beat him," he said. "He was asked if he wanted a rematch and he said no.

"Go back and fight the fella who beat you. That's the one I'd be looking at if I was him. He's in the same division, the same league, and he's begging for the rematch."

'I'll fight Aaron or the other fella'

Walsh, who fights in Dublin for the first time since knocking out Przemyslaw Runowski in two rounds in 2024, is confident he can overcome Denny and believes Aaron McKenna will become Ireland's newest world champion.

Victory for both men would set up the mouth-watering prospect of an all-Irish world title fight, and Walsh insists he would have no problem facing Aaron should he emerge as champion.

"I don't know much about his opponent, to be honest," Walsh added. "I'm sure Aaron will win. I presume he will.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Walsh insists he's not complacent ahead of Saturday's fight with Denny, while the former European champion is confident he can cause the upset in Dublin

"It's a big opportunity and a big night for him to go out there, perform and win the world title in Dublin. I think he will.

"If Aaron wins and they want me to fight him, I'll fight him. If he doesn't win, maybe I'll fight the other fella.

"I just fight whoever they tell me to. I'm not out here calling anybody out. It's just the same old habits."

Watch Zuffa Boxing 10, headlined by Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha live on Sky Sports this Saturday.

Sports.title: Bracey shares memories of Lawrence ahead of Sunday's tribute
Sports.content:
When James Bracey thinks of Syd Lawrence, he does not first think of wickets, records or milestones.

He thinks of a man who never stopped giving to Gloucestershire cricket.

This Sunday, Gloucestershire will honour former England fast bowler Syd Lawrence during their Metro Bank One Day Cup fixture against Nottinghamshire, wearing a special commemorative kit and raising funds for the Motor Neurone Disease Association (MNDA).

For Bracey, the occasion is deeply personal.

One memory stands above all others: September 2024, when Gloucestershire won the T20 Blast for the first time in the club's history. Lawrence, already battling motor neurone disease, was there to present the trophy.

"That was very special for me," Bracey tells Sky Sports.

Image: For Bracey, his standout memory of Lawrence comes from that exchange - Photo courtesy of Gloucestershire CCC

"We were obviously delighted that we'd just won the Blast for the first time as a team, but to see how much it meant to him, even at that stage of his life, was really emotional.

"It just showed how much he really loved the club. To see his face when he was able to hold that trophy was really special for me."

Image: Photo courtesy of Gloucestershire CCC

Lawrence, who passed away in June 2025 aged 61, remains one of the most influential figures in Gloucestershire's history. He became the first British-born Black cricketer to play Test cricket for England in 1988 and later became Gloucestershire's first Black president.

Although Bracey never saw Lawrence play, his impact on the club was impossible to miss.

"From my experiences, he was an incredibly kind-hearted person, incredibly personable and cared a hell of a lot about Gloucestershire cricket," Bracey said.

"Any time he was around the ground, he was chatting to everyone. He was larger than life and had a hell of a lot of energy."

Sunday's tribute is also designed to raise awareness of motor neurone disease and highlight the work of the MNDA.

"We've seen how public Syd was with his condition," Bracey said. "But the impact it has on family and friends is just as important.

"That's the amazing thing about what the MNDA do. They support the person with the disease, but they also help those around them."

Image: A pioneering Black cricketer, Lawrence helped open doors for future generations

Lawrence's legacy also extends beyond Gloucestershire. As a pioneering Black cricketer, he helped open doors for future generations.

"There's been a lot of progress," Bracey said. "But there's obviously a lot more work to do in maintaining that progress and increasing it as well."

As Gloucestershire and Nottinghamshire come together to honour Lawrence, Bracey hopes supporters remember the cricketer, the trailblazer and the person behind both.

"When I'm reminded of Syd, it takes me back to that day," he said.

"It was a very special and happy moment for me to see what that meant to him."

This weekend's tribute will celebrate a man whose love for Gloucestershire never faded - and whose legacy continues to inspire the club he loved.

Sports.title: Araujo set for medical ahead of surprise Liverpool loan move
Sports.content:
Liverpool have agreed a surprise deal for Barcelona defender Ronald Araujo to join on loan for the season.

The deal for the 27-year-old, who signed a new Barca contract that runs until 2031 last year, includes an option to buy.

Araujo will arrive in the UK on Sunday to undertake a medical and complete his temporary switch to Liverpool.

The Uruguay international joined Barcelona B in 2018 before being promoted to the first team in 2019.

The 27-year-old centre-back will add to Andoni Iraola's options at the heart of his defence following the departure of Ibrahima Konate to Real Madrid and fitness concerns over relatively inexperienced 21-year-old Jeremy Jacquet.

The summer signing from Rennes has made fewer than 100 senior career appearances and has not featured in pre-season yet after missing the second half of last season following shoulder surgery.

Sports.title: McKenna vs Oliha and Walsh vs Denny big-fight predictions
Sports.content:
Experts have their say ahead of the Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha middleweight world championship clash and Callum Walsh's crucial fight against Tyler Denny, live on Sky Sports from 7pm.

Aaron McKenna vs Etinosa Oliha

Chris Billam-Smith (former cruiserweight champion): McKenna's got so much to his game I think. He's shown he can box a bit but he's got an intensity and a workrate. He punches hard enough to get people's respect. We saw a lot from him in the Liam Smith fight, of what he can do. I will pick him to win, probably on points, but he could overwhelm him as well.

Johnny Nelson (former cruiserweight champion): Aaron McKenna gets an inside-the-distance stoppage win I think. His engine, his pace will be too much.

Oliha can't afford to get hit too easily because McKenna won't leave you alone. It's a good fight, especially for McKenna boxing in Dublin for the first time in his professional career.

I think McKenna in the first half of the fight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McKenna and Oliha were locked in a tense face-off ahead of their IBF world middleweight title clash

Johnny Fisher (heavyweight star): McKenna's been based in America for a little while, this is now his homecoming fight. Tremendous amateur record, hopefully that pedigree comes through. I think this crowd will give him that extra lift. If he uses that crowd and doesn't let it be detrimental to him, that's what's going to carry him over the line.

Callum Walsh (middleweight contender): I presume that Aaron will win. It's a big night, a big opportunity for him to go out there and perform and to win the world title in Dublin. I think he will.

Connor Coyle (middleweight contender): I think McKenna will win, I think he'll win on points. I know McKenna's boxing, I've known him growing up through Irish boxing. That's why I know he's a good boxer.

I think he'll become IBF world champion on Saturday night.

It's kind of a new breed of middleweight coming through.

Patrick O'Connor (cruiserweight prospect): I think Aaron McKenna will win by decision. From what I see, I think Aaron is going to beat him on points, maybe late stoppage. It's going to be great for Irish boxing to have a world champion, it's a big thing.

Owen O'Neill (middleweight fighter): McKenna on points. He's a very technical boxer, he's very smart and he's very good. I've been in there with him [in sparring] and he's tall, he's got big arms and he punches hard too.

He's a good fighter. He's shown it. His first breakout win was Brad Rea, a really good win at the time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Callum Walsh is relishing performing in front of his home fans at the 3Arena in Dublin when he takes on Tyler Denny

He's not affected by his losses. He's been beat, come back and won and he's looked good doing so. So it's a really interesting one. I can't really pick a winner because I know how good Callum is but nothing would surprise me in that fight.

Nelson: On paper you'd lean towards Walsh because of where he's at in his career, but then you look at what Tyler Denny's done, the heads he's snatched because they've looked through him, looked past him. This is going to be a test of Walsh's heart, Walsh's desire. Because Tyler Denny is not one of those guys that folds easily.

I'd lean towards Tyler, but on points.

If he establishes his jab, fights at range, it's Walsh's fight to win. I pick Walsh but I like Tyler Denny, I like his tenacity. He's fought some of the top guys in the division. Although I pick Walsh I wouldn't be surprised if it goes the other way.

Hickey: Tyler Denny's a good fighter, he can make people look average. If you're not on your best night he can make a mess of the fight. Look at his last fight with George Liddard, it was a close one.

That's an interesting fight because Callum Walsh has obviously made his career over in America. You'll really see the level that Walsh is at. It's different because when you move up the levels, fighters can take the power. If Walsh is a serious puncher he can maybe get him out of there but he's moving up the levels so he might end up having to go the rounds and we'll see how good a fighter he is.

Sports.title: Debut Lankshear goal sees Boro past Wrexham as Wolves & Stevenage progress
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear's debut strike ensured Middlesbrough made a winning start to the season as they beat Wrexham 1-0 in the Carabao Cup first round.

Lankshear, a £10m summer signing from Tottenham, scored the only goal of the game in the 61st minute as he hooked home an excellent first-time volley.

Middlesbrough almost claimed a seventh-minute opener, but while Adilson Malanda prodded Sebastian Berhalter's cross goalwards from close range, Danny Ward kept the ball out with a superb point-blank save.

Danny Imray wasted a decent chance for Wrexham when he failed to make a proper connection from Callum Doyle's cross, and the visitors went close again six minutes before the break when Sam Smith fired a low shot into the legs of Sol Brynn after he was rolled into space by Nathan Broadhead.

Lankshear came close with an effort that was curled just over the bar at the start of the second half, but the 21-year-old did not have to wait too much longer for his first goal in a Boro shirt.

Leo Castledine headed Jeremy Sarmiento's cross into Lankshear's path, and the striker swivelled neatly before hooking a superb first-time volley into the far corner.

Boro almost doubled their lead with three minutes remaining, but Morgan Whittaker's low strike rebounded off the post.

Wolves coast past Port Vale as Jimenez makes return

Wolves progressed with a comfortable 3-0 win over Port Vale in which all three goals came in the first half. Adam Armstrong, Andre and Fer Lopez took the game away from the League Two side as Cesar Peixoto marked his first game in charge with a win.

Jon Brady's Port Vale had opportunities. Jordan Lawrence-Gabriel hooked an extraordinary chance away from the Wolves goal before the break, before Mo Faal's low penalty was saved by the legs of Dan Bentley to deny the travelling fans a consolation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Port Vale's Jordan Lawrence-Gabriel misses a chance from six yards out in his side's Carabao Cup clash with Wolves.

The Wolves supporters among the crowd of 21,360 at Molineux were more interested in serenading their returning hero. Raul Jimenez, the club's Premier League top scorer, re-signed this summer after three years at Fulham and came on as a late substitute.

The Mexican centre-forward did fire off one fierce shot on goal but he was unable to mark the occasion with a goal that would have been cruel on a competitive Port Vale side. But it is Wolves who take their place in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

Stevenage strike late to beat Wycombe

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first round Carabao Cup match between Wycombe Wanderers and Stevenage.

New signing Josh Magennis headed the winner in the dying seconds to send Stevenage through to the second round of the Carabao Cup with a 2-1 victory at Wycombe.

It was a fitting start to the Boro's 50th anniversary season as substitute Magennis, a summer capture from Exeter, rose to score from Phoenix Patterson's left-wing corner in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

The visitors had shaken off early pressure to take the lead against the run of play in the 27th minute.

Midfielder Dan Kemp took advantage of hesitancy in the Wycombe defence as he raced through to fire home a low shot.

That stung the home side into action and Ewan Henderson equalised in the 38th minute. Winger Silko Thomas crossed from the left and the Scot slipped through the visiting defence to score right-footed from just outside the six-yard box.

Stevenage scared their Sky Bet League One rivals again on the stroke of half-time when Kemp rattled the bar with a shot from the edge of the box.

Wycombe took control after the break but struggled to break through.

New boy Emre Tezgel, on for Cauley Woodrow, was thwarted by Boro skipper Carl Piergianni as he attempted to force home Thomas' cross from the left in the 77th minute before Magennis settled the issue.

The Carabao Cup is back for the 2026/27 season, with every first-round tie available to watch live on Sky Sports!

West Ham, Burnley and Leicester are among those in action on Saturday - and you can follow the goals as they go in from all 29 ties on Soccer Saturday.

Every match from the opening round will be shown live on Sky Sports, with clubs from the Championship, League One and League Two entering the competition.

Sports.title: New Zealand begin South Africa tour with flattering win over Stormers
Sports.content:
New Zealand's first full-scale tour of South Africa in 30 years began with an underwhelming 38-21 win over the Stormers.

The scoreline flattered a scratch All Blacks side which was favoured to win comfortably.

The makeshift Stormers - in pre-season mode - rallied twice to tie the score, which was knotted at 14-14 until 13 minutes to go.

When the Stormers lost their second scrum-half and had no more reserve backs, the patched-up backline was ruthlessly exposed by New Zealand, who scored three tries in the last eight minutes.

But the result only papered over a performance that was blighted by ill-discipline, three yellow cards, and a struggling set-piece.

They overcame those with six tries to three by the Stormers in front of a 47,130 crowd.

Image: New Zealand started with an unconvincing win on their tour of South Africa

The good news for the All Blacks was they appeared to finish with no major injuries, seven players made their first appearance in the black jersey this year, and two more made their debuts off the bench; prop Siale Lauaki and inside back Josh Jacomb.

But the most impressive players in the stadium were Stormers fly-half Yaqeen Ahmed, who looked comfortably cool in his first-class debut at age 20, and flanker Deon Fourie, the dynamo who will be 40 next month.

"It was a good introduction for us to South African rugby," said New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie. "We started ​very well and it looked like which side had the ball ⁠got rewarded by the referee.

"When we had ⁠the ball we were really dangerous. We knew they would bring line speed [in defence]. We just weren't quite clinical enough ‌to expose them.

"They came at us with their set-piece and we need to be better in those areas. We expected a lot of aerial attacks and we probably did ‌not handle that as well as we could have."

Sports.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino denies claims Uefa paid off alleged ‘lover’
Sports.content:
Uefa has confirmed a “departure payment” was made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Gianni Infantino while he was the organisation’s general secretary, allegations Fifa has dismissed as “categorically untrue”.

The Daily Telegraph reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum following the alleged relationship with Infantino. In a statement, Uefa confirmed a payment was made along with covering the fees for an MBA course, which it said was “in line” with regulations at the time.

However, Fifa has responded to the reports. “Fifa president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue. Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory,” a Fifa spokesman told the Telegraph. “No employee at Uefa and Fifa has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.”

The report comes as pressure mounts on Infantino following his plan to seek private investment in a company which would run Fifa’s competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cups. Infantino worked at Uefa for 16 years and was its general secretary from 2009 before being elected as Fifa president in February 2016.

A Uefa spokesperson said: “We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for a MBA course at a local business school.”

The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time. “Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all Uefa employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.”

Infantino has found himself at the centre of a storm for two weeks following his controversial plan to sell stakes to private investors in a company to run the World Cup. The plan was rejected by Uefa and two other continental confederations. On Wednesday, Infantino was backed by Fifa’s management board following a meeting in Morocco and issued an apology over the process.

Uefa’s threat for its 55 member countries to boycott Fifa competitions until the plan was scrapped remains, with the European confederation saying on Thursday that Wednesday’s announcement “changes nothing”.

Sports.title: Why Super Furry Animals joined music’s dash to cross over football’s vinyl frontier | Emma John
Sports.content:
As someone born on the cusp of the gen X-millennial divide, I am the perfect target for today’s 90s nostalgia. I played my modest, teenage part in the Battle of Britpop (verbal skirmisher, Blur division); I fervently sang – and, God help me, believed – that Things Can Only Get Better. Super Furry Animals were a band I knew only distantly, via the transgressive thrill of that song they had with all the swearing in. And yet the news they’ll be shirt sponsor for a Welsh football club this season has managed to whisk me straight back to a time when things seemed simpler, kinder and more hopeful.

Nearly three decades have passed since Super Furry Animals last had their logo on a football kit. Back in 1999, their frontman Gruff Rhys and bassist Guto Pryce, both Cardiff City fans, persuaded their Bangor-born bandmates to lay down their north Wales allegiances for the duration of the Bluebirds’ Welsh Cup run – which was, incidentally, all they could afford. The cup shirts cost them £2,000 and were, according to Rhys, knock-offs made for ice hockey. This year’s beneficiaries are a more modest outfit: Cwmbran Celtic, just relegated from Wales’s second tier. Cwmbran is the town where the band send their stage props for repair, and given the props in question are giant inflatable bears, you wonder whether they could get one installed in goal.

Super Furry Animals aren’t the only 90s band involved: Scottish post-rockers Mogwai have sponsored the men’s away strip, with 10% of the profits from all shirt sales going to a grassroots music charity.

There has traditionally been an element of patronage when famous musicians do football, from Elton John’s time as chair of Watford, to Robbie Williams’s 2024 elevation to Port Vale club president. The pattern is a repeating one: local lads (they’re usually lads) make good, and want to give back to the team they’ve followed since they were little. Wet Wet Wet were the first to go down the shirt-sponsorship route with Clydebank in 1993. The team’s shirts turned out to be a more timeless design than the loud, oversized suits that Marti Pellow’s crew wore the day they unveiled them.

Slapping your logo on your home side’s shirt was a charitable endeavour, rather than an investment. Nothing underscored this point better than Fatboy Slim’s relationship with Brighton & Hove Albion. The DJ’s record label first sponsored their shirts in the late 90s, back when the team’s financial straits had left them flirting with extinction, and Tony Bloom’s billions were still waiting to be won. It was particularly appropriate back then that Micky Adams’s men should run out on to the field with their chests declaring them SKINT.

View image in fullscreen Bobby Zamora in Brighton’s home kit sponsored by Fatboy Slim. Photograph: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images

Musical match-ups have tended, therefore, towards the endearing, not the cool. Jake Bugg sponsored Notts County not to market his own music, but to evangelise the Midlands team on his global tours. And it’s even cuter when bands have sponsored kids’ teams. The late Lemmy of Motörhead was tickled by the thought of a Lincolnshire under-10s team sporting his Snaggletooth skull mascot on their fronts; unfortunately the resultant all-black kit too closely resembled referees’ uniforms and the children were banned from wearing it in league matches. Still, the idea had an enduring appeal: the Prodigy, Biffy Clyro, Sleaford Mods and Franz Ferdinand have all paid for youth kits.

In the last couple of years, though, the relationship between bands and football teams has turned serious. The move to monetise the “adjacent audiences” of pop and sporting fandom means shirt sponsorship is no longer a way of artists showing their support, but a marketing and merchandising opportunity in its own right.

Spotify’s deal with Barcelona got the ball rolling, with Coldplay, Karol G, Rosalía and Travis Scott each briefly appearing on the shirtfront, and limited-edition replicas costing more than £340 a pop. The footie-kit-as-streetwear trend means bands aren’t “sponsors” any more, they’re “collaborators”. Hence Manchester United’s pre-match shirts don’t bear the name of the Stone Roses, just their album artwork. And while that may have baffled a few younger fans – the club’s website ran a post explaining who the Madchester group were for the gen Z-ers – it still reflects a genuine connection. Ian Brown is a lifelong Red, and the team has walked out to This Is the One since Gary Neville first requested it two decades ago.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Coldplay show off their Barcelona shirts. Photograph: Fc Barcelona Handout/EPA

Whereas a year ago, if you’d been asked at a pub quiz what Paris Saint-Germain had in common with a K-pop band, or what Pink Floyd had to do with a Serie A team, you’d have been within your rights to say “nothing”. The answer, now, is clothing ranges – PSG teamed up with the girl group Blackpink to optimise fan engagement in Asia, while Inter marked the 50th anniversary of the album release of Wish You Were Here.

All this can be confusing for the simple-minded sports lover like me. What is a culture-forward lifestyle capsule, anyway? It sounds like something Musk and Bezos want to blast to Mars in. Creating a sporting look now involves an advanced understanding of fashion arithmetic: at last year’s Euros it was Admiral x Spice Girls, now it’s the Rolling Stones x England Cricket x Castore. These are powerful equations, as when a 2025 Bohemian FC x Fontaines DC shirt (raised to the power of Greta Thunberg when she wore it on her flotilla to Gaza) = £££££ for charity. Maybe Ed Sheeran’s Mathematics tour top for Ipswich was an omen. Or perhaps this is a fad, and the music industry will soon move on to something new. GQ, which has declared “blokecore” over, says we’ll be wearing classic rugby tops by autumn/winter. Sounds delightfully 90s to me.

Sports.title: Will Lankshear starts off in style to see Middlesbrough past Wrexham
Sports.content:
Will Lankshear’s debut strike ensured Middlesbrough made a winning start to the season as they beat Wrexham 1-0 in the Carabao Cup first round. Lankshear, a £10m summer signing from Tottenham, scored the only goal of the game in the 61st minute as he hooked home an excellent first-time volley.

Middlesbrough almost claimed a seventh-minute opener but when Adilson Malanda prodded Sebastian Berhalter’s cross goalwards from close range, Danny Ward kept the ball out with a superb point-blank save.

Danny Imray wasted a decent chance for Wrexham when he failed to make a proper connection from Callum Doyle’s cross and the visitors went close again six minutes before the break when Sam Smith fired a low shot into the legs of Sol Brynn after he was rolled into space by Nathan Broadhead.

Lankshear came close with an effort that was curled just over the bar at the start of the second half, but the 21-year-old did not have to wait too much longer for his first goal in a Boro shirt. Leo Castledine headed Jeremy Sarmiento’s cross into Lankshear’s path, and the striker swivelled neatly before hooking a superb first-time volley into the far corner.

Boro almost doubled their lead with three minutes remaining but Morgan Whittaker’s low strike rebounded off the post.

After the match the Middlesbrough manager, Kim Hellberg, expressed his delight with the instant impact Will Lankshear has made since joining the club. “He was very impressive and the most impressive thing has been seeing how well he has worked on the training ground,” Hellberg said. “How hard he works on the training ground and how much he wants to learn.

“It’s a joy to watch and when you add the person he is to the quality he has as a footballer on the pitch, you have a very good striker. I’m happy to have him here.”

Wrexham’s manager, Phil Parkinson, felt his side had given a decent account of themselves just four days after returning from a pre-season tour of the US. Parkinson said: “I thought we had enough half-chances, particularly in the first half, to have progressed in the competition. The game really separated from one quality finish from their lad. We had some good build-up play, but just didn’t quite have that clinical edge.

Sports.title: Boardroom struggle deepens gloom as West Ham prepare for life on the outside
Sports.content:
There have been 10 summers of West Ham’s London Stadium tenancy and a number of winters of discontent. As the Hammers kick off the new season on Saturday, a Carabao Cup first-round fixture with Portsmouth is a stark reminder of reduced circumstances, further confirmation of last season’s relegation from the Premier League. The summer has been as bleak as any of those winters, with a number of factors colliding to deepen the gloom of relegation.

Certain clubs, including West Ham back in 2011-12 when promotion was achieved at first time of asking under Sam Allardyce, have used the Championship to take a beat, to refresh and replenish. Can this be the case at West Ham 2026? The Hammers are short-odds favourites for promotion but behind the scenes it has been a summer of turbulence, particularly in the boardroom, where a power struggle is being fought.

Portsmouth will bring 9,000 supporters on Saturday but will David Sullivan be present? This week it was revealed the operators of London Stadium had recommended the former joint-chair (but still co-owner) stay away, because of the “potential for demonstrations and anti-social behaviour by some spectators”.

It is expected that Sullivan will turn up, despite a fans’ advisory board statement that his attendance would cause “offence and upset”. It has been suggested that he wants to enjoy the coming season as a fan and is happy to bide his time before any consideration of selling his 38.8% stake. Considering his personal circumstances, his attendance would be a brazenly unpopular act. On 25 May, when relegation was confirmed despite a home win over Leeds, Sullivan was forced to leave the stadium early for his own safety.

View image in fullscreen Daniel Kretinsky wants to increase his shares in West Ham to just under 50.1%. Photograph: David W Černý/Reuters

Sullivan continues to deny allegations of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour towards women over several decades made by the BBC’s Panorama documentary in early June, though he stepped down from his role on the eve of the broadcast “to avoid disruption to the club while he addresses the matter privately”.

Even before those allegations became public, Sullivan was a lightning rod, lambasted for his stewardship of a club in vertiginous decline since winning the Europa Conference League in May 2023. The £100m fee received for Declan Rice that summer was frittered away. Fellow Prague hero Jarrod Bowen, the club captain, has pledged to stay on, tasked with leading the club back up.

Until his defenestration Sullivan had acted as the club’s de facto director of football, often to the frustration of those in the football department. His chief ally, Karren Brady, stepped down in April as storm clouds gathered, severing a working relationship that dated as far back as 1990.

Among the club’s support, 50,000 season tickets have been sold for the attempt at re-entry to the Premier League. The overriding desire among fans is for Sullivan to completely depart the scene. His announced departure had installed a modicum of optimism.

Potential new sheriffs are circling but the picture is complicated, any future direction opaque as a result. As Sullivan stepped down the expectation was that Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire owner of Royal Mail who has owned 27% of West Ham since 2021, would make his move. Instead, this week, he cut that share down to just under 25%, though this was part of a strategy.

Last weekend, the familiar face of Amanda Staveley entered the picture. In July 2024 she departed Newcastle, after her leading role in bringing in the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund, but now Staveley wants to return to football. Last September, she was linked with a takeover at Tottenham, and it is suggested she will use a similar source of funding to engineer her move for West Ham. Among Newcastle fans, with their club faltering this summer, Staveley’s energy is lamented. With her connections, some Hammers fan hope she could have a similar galvanising effect.

View image in fullscreen David Sullivan’s closet ally, Karren Brady, left the club in April. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy

The key is the 25% that belonged to the late David Gold, Sullivan’s former joint-chair. As Staveley loomed, Kretinsky appeared ready to take up his first refusal on purchasing that 25% from Vanessa Gold, David’s daughter and current co-chair. Adding that to his 27% would take him beyond 50.1%, leaving him liable for a formal takeover offer. But shifting 2% to a Czech ally, the entrepreneur Jakub Havrlant, now means he would be short of that obligation should he cut across Staveley’s ambitions by buying Gold’s stake. Sullivan’s shares also hold the balance of power and Staveley’s next move is keenly awaited.

While that plays out, what of football? The arrival of free agent, the former Brighton and Ajax defender, Joël Veltman, was the first addition of a summer where the sales of Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham and Crysencio Summerville to Al-Hilal fetched a collective £140m, commensurate to a year of Premier League TV money. Youth product Freddie Potts’ departure to Club Brugge for £10m disappointed some fans. Needs must if further players are to arrive. There is interest in Ireland’s World Cup playoff hero Troy Parrott, the striker at AZ Alkmaar, though attracting players to the Championship has its difficulties.

View image in fullscreen West Ham have cashed in on key players, such as Mateus Fernandes to Tottenham, to cushion their descent into the Championship. Photograph: Phil Walter/Getty Images

In the dugout remains Nuno Espírito Santo, who stayed when his departure had been expected. Nuno’s zen-like calm is required at a club where panic regularly sets in. The vacuum created by Sullivan’s situation, relegation and lack of transfer business heightens anxieties. A new season has arrived, with uninviting league fixtures against Burnley, Charlton, Watford and Wolves by 1 September. Karim Virani, previously a club employee who departed in 2020, more recently at Glasgow Rangers, has returned as interim chief executive. Attempts are being made to stitch West Ham into a semblance of unity.

This summer, the London Stadium played host to concerts from Take That and Metallica, and staged the Diamond League athletics meet in July, where Josh Kerr broke the world mile record. Thursday saw a bid confirmed to stage the 2029 World Athletics Championships, following an impasse between the club and the stadium owners. Further reminders that West Ham’s home will never be fully their own, 10 years after departing the Boleyn Ground.

Such were the terms Sullivan, Gold Sr and Brady agreed for a stadium that fans continue to resent, where Sullivan is unlikely to be made to feel welcome.

Sports.title: Jay-Z’s Roc Nation Sports making waves in European football transfer market
Sports.content:
In the end there was a clear winner. And Jay-Z’s latest victory came only 24 hours after the first record featuring him actually rapping for four years had been released by his wife, Beyoncé, on an extended remix pack of Morning Dew (Donk).

These days, the man who remains one of the most influential artists in hip-hop has his fingers in many pies, from the streaming service Tidal and his own streetwear brand, to champagne and cognac. But it is Roc Nation Sports – an offshoot of his entertainment company of the same name founded in 2008 – making headlines in the summer transfer window.

Established five years later in partnership with Creative Artists Agency, it began mainly representing players from the NBA, NFL and MLB, including Kevin Durant. Bayern Munich’s Jérôme Boateng was the first football client, in 2015, before Roc Nation Sports International (RNSI) was established four years later with a focus on stars at big European clubs.

Based in London, it now has more than 100 players on its books, including Vinícius Júnior – the Brazil forward who signed a lucrative new contract with Real Madrid this week believed to be worth around €25m. That came after Arsenal had been linked with a blockbuster move for the 26-year-old.

In July 2023 RNSI took over the successful Brazilian agents TFM – who already represented Vinícius, Gabriel Martinelli, and Endrick – and renamed it Roc Nation Sports Brazil.

In negotiations that have lasted two years, it had hoped to persuade Real to increase their star asset’s salary to €30m a year to match Kylian Mbappé, and allowed his contract to enter its final 12 months in an effort to drum up interest elsewhere. While Arsenal – now exploring other attacking options including Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye – are believed to have been willing to pay a big fee for Vinícius, it is understood that they thought signing him on a free transfer next season was more likely.

Nonetheless, Real upped their offer and Vinícius stayed. It is a decision that looks likely to cost them the chance to sign Rodri from Manchester City after Barcelona stole a march on their great rivals.

View image in fullscreen A phonecall from Vinícius Júnior reportedly led to Yan Diomande signing with Roc Nation Sports. Photograph: Kirsty Wigglesworth/AP

On the same day as the new six-year contract for Vinícius was announced, Yan Diomande flew to the Spanish capital to complete his record £115m transfer from RB Leipzig. The 19-year-old – who has made only 46 appearances at senior level for the German club and for Leganés in the Spanish second division but is already the most expensive African player in history – was pictured with his agents, Nathan Campbell and Kareem Gbaja on a private jet. RNSI has been reported to have been paid up to £17m in commission and fees.

A long-running saga that began when Liverpool had a £70m bid rejected by Leipzig in June ended with Diomande signing a seven-year deal at the Bernabéu on Thursday. It has provided a telling insight into the mechanisms of a modern transfer, with every week bringing a fresh twist. Having been told they must pay in excess of £100m to sign Diomande, Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the race at the end of July after releasing a statement that said the European champions “will not engage in the inflationary and manipulative games of certain player agents”.

RNSI has also had to fend off two legal challenges, including one from the former Bournemouth winger Max Gradel who claims that his agency, Maxidel Management, had an existing agreement with Diomande. Gradel has filed a complaint with Fifa, although world football’s governing body did not block the player’s move to Real. Dez Bamba – who is president of Diomande’s first club, AFI Sud Comoé in Côte d’Ivoire – has said that the winger was persuaded to join RNSI after receiving a call from Vinícius. RNSI has not commented on the case.

Meanwhile, the Rainbow World Group instigated proceedings at the high court in London and the British Virgin Islands against Diomande in mid-June “to enforce binding image rights and intellectual property agreements tied to his early career development”. It is claimed Rainbow invested significant resources in the winger, including taking him for trials at Chelsea, Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Newcastle before he was signed by Leganés. RNSI has not commented on the case.

Given Diomande’s meteoric rise, perhaps it is no surprise that clubs are flocking to invest in African academies.

Jeff Luhnow – the former general manager of the Astros and St Louis Cardinals who won three World Series baseball titles and was chief executive of Blue Crow, the ex-owner of Leganes, until the club was sold to 885 capital in June - told the Guardian last year Diomande was expected to be the first of many after they set up recruitment and development programmes in several African countries, including Ghana and Zambia, in the past several years. “We’ve got more players like that in our pipeline,” said Luhnow.

RNSI announced in November that it has signed eight young African stars, including the Ghana Under-17 midfielder Joseph Narbi and Francis Gomez, a Gambian winger currently at AC Horsens in Denmark. “We believe Africa is a hotbed of untapped footballing potential, and our expansion here is a natural progression of our global vision,” said Campbell.

In the dog-eat-dog world of football agents Jay Z’s new kids on the block are certainly making their presence felt.

Sports.title: England striker Ivan Toney charged with assault after Soho nightclub incident
Sports.content:
The England footballer Ivan Toney has been charged with assault after an incident at a nightclub in Soho in December last year.

Scotland Yard said the striker had been charged on 31 July with assault causing actual bodily harm. Toney, who plays for the Saudi Pro League club Al-Ahli, is due to appear at Westminster magistrates court on 24 September.

The Sun newspaper reported in December that Toney had been arrested after an alleged head-butt. It claimed a fan recognised the footballer and grabbed at him while seeking a photograph with him before the incident.

On Friday the Metropolitan police said the charges related to an incident on 6 December at a nightclub on Wardour Street in central London, reportedly the now-closed 100 Wardour Street.

A spokesperson for Toney said: “Ivan acknowledges the charge and although he is naturally shocked, he looks forward to being given the opportunity to clear his name in court.”

Toney was at the centre of one of the most curious transfers on deadline day in August 2024 when he completed a late move from Brentford to Al-Ahli worth a reported £40m. He has also played for Newcastle United and his home town club Northampton Town, as well as several others on loan as he looked to establish himself.

Seen as a late bloomer in football terms, he had made only two Premier League appearances before his 25th birthday, but went on to score 67 goals in 128 appearances over the next three seasons at the top level.

He has played 10 times for England, scoring once in a friendly match against Belgium in 2024, and was part of the 2026 World Cup squad, making appearances against Argentina in the semi-final and in the win over France as England finished third.

Sports.title: Manchester City reject Barcelona’s opening £38.5m bid for Rodri as talks continue
Sports.content:
Manchester City have rejected an offer of £38.5m (€45m) from Barcelona for Rodri and want at least £60m before allowing Spain’s World Cup-winning captain to depart.

Barcelona have emerged as Rodri’s preferred destination after talks with Real Madrid broke down this week. It is understood that the 30-year-old, who is now in the final year of his contract at City, has agreed personal terms with the Spanish champions after indicating that he would like to return to his homeland following the departure of Pep Guardiola.

Rodri moved to the Etihad in 2019 from Atlético Madrid and has turned down the offer of a lucrative extension. Yet City are believed to be adamant that he will not be allowed to leave for less than their asking price. Barcelona are continuing negotiations in the hope of reaching a compromise.

Rodri, who won the World Cup Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player last month, spoke to Barça’s manager, Hansi Flick, and sporting director, Deco, about a potential move on Wednesday.

The Spanish champions will be without Frenkie de Jong for several months after the Netherlands midfielder sustained a knee injury and have targeted Rodri as a replacement. He has had minor surgery on his back and will miss most of City’s pre-season programme.

City have signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m and remain in negotiations with Lille over a deal for Ayyoub Bouaddi. The Morocco midfielder could cost up to £80m but they could be tempted to bring in a more experienced replacement for Rodri should he depart, with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández among those thought to be under consideration. The 25-year-old is also wanted by Real, whose manager, José Mourinho is said to not to have the news of being gazumped by their great rivals well. Reports in Spain have claimed that the 63-year-old is unhappy after making the signing of a central midfielder his priority on returning for a second stint at the Santiago Bernabéu.

Real have already brought in the winger Yan Diomande for £115m and Marc Cucurella, Bernardo Silva, Ibrahima Konaté, Denzel Dumfries and Carlos Espí, so they may have to balance the books by selling either Aurélien Tchouaméni and Eduardo Camavinga if they want to pursue Argentinian Fernández.

Crystal Palace have confirmed the signing of Takehiro Tomiyasu after a successful trial period. The former Arsenal defender has been training with Palace during pre-season and has done enough to earn an initial 12-month deal with the option of extending that by another two years. Tomiyasu becomes new manager Pierre Sage’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Óscar Mingueza on a free transfer. Palace are expected to complete a deal for the USA youth international Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake in MLS.

Sports.title: Tottenham and Atlético in talks over Romero with Van de Ven set to sign new deal
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Atlético Madrid over the sale of Cristian Romero after categorically rejecting Arsenal’s approach for the Argentina defender and are expected to agree a new five-year deal with Micky van de Ven.

Romero has made no secret of his desire to leave Spurs despite signing a new four-year contract at the start of last season and had looked set to join Inter for a fee of around £35m. But Atlético are long-term suitors of the 28-year-old and are thought to be his preferred destination, with Diego Simeone’s side understood to be prepared to match Inter’s bid.

Reports in Spain on Friday suggested that personal terms have already been agreed with Romero, although his move may have to wait for Atlético to free up space in their squad before they can complete the transfer. Nahuel Molina, Romero’s Argentina teammate, is expected to join Roma while Aston Villa are hoping to sign Matteo Ruggeri.

Arsenal had also made their interest known as they search for a replacement for William Saliba, with the Frenchman out for an extended period due to a back issue. However, Tottenham – who have signed defenders Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi this summer – insisted that they did not want to sell to another Premier League club, least of all their north London rivals. Arsenal are also interested in Villa’s Ezri Konsa.

It is understood that Van de Ven had been considering his future in north London at the start of the summer after Tottenham narrowly avoided relegation last season. But the impact of the new manager, Roberto De Zerbi, has persuaded the Netherlands international to commit his future to the club after talks with his representatives.

Tottenham have already spent more than £200m on six new players this summer and are still in the market for a new attacker. Last week, De Zerbi said that they had “completed 60% of our project in the transfer market”.

Sports.title: Chelsea could release entire XI good enough to challenge for Europe before window shuts
Sports.content:
Chelsea could release entire XI good enough to challenge for Europe before window shuts

With 24 days remaining until the transfer window slams shut, Chelsea still have plenty of work to do.

Their summer spending so far is in and around the £300million mark, with a large chunk of this coming via the £117m signing of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

6 Alonso has a number of players at his disposal as Chelsea boss Credit: Getty

Geovany Quenda and Emmanuel Emegha have joined in pre-agreed deals, with Marco Palestra, Maxence Lacroix, Danny Welbeck, Valentin Barco and Jordan Henderson also through the door.

However, the numerous additions mean that the Chelsea first team squad has only increased in size, with 46 players listed in the squad on their website.

It's an eye-opening number for a club void of European football this season, though many of those listed are academy talents who are on their pre-season tour such as Reggie Walsh and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli.

Xabi Alonso has not specified how big he wants his squad to be, but he is unlikely to want a bloated team that could risk squad harmony.

Various players currently on the books have been linked with exits, and talkSPORT.com has selected a hypothetical XI that, on paper, could contend for European qualification in the Premier League.

Filip Jorgensen

Having been the second-choice goalkeeper to Robert Sanchez for much of his Chelsea career, Jorgensen is closing in on a departure.

He left their pre-season tour amid transfer interest, with sister club Strasbourg understood to be an option for the 24-year-old, who was linked with a move in January.

Jorgensen is also a Denmark international who will likely be looking for more consistent minutes in between the sticks.

Axel Disasi

The first half of the 2025/26 season was quiet for Disasi, but he was back on the pitch at West Ham United with a winter loan move.

Although the Hammers were relegated from the Premier League, the French defender made a good impression in east London and is not short of interest as September 1 approaches.

6 Disasi did well on loan at West Ham despite their relegation Credit: Getty

AC Milan and Roma are understood to have shown interest in Disasi, and Crystal Palace is another speculated destination for the centre-back, who can also play as a right-back.

Tosin Adarabioyo

Another defender who could be heading out of Stamford Bridge is Tosin, who could have done better to deny Tottenham Hotspur the winning goal in their pre-season friendly last week.

His appearances last season were sporadic, and many of these came as a substitute amid competition from Wesley Fofana, Trevoh Chalobah and Jorrel Hato.

However, with 116 Premier League outings to his name, the 28-year-old would add a depth of experience to any back line should he leave.

Benoit Badiashile

Chelsea's FA Cup fifth round victory against Wrexham on March 7 is the most recent match that Badiashile has played for the club.

The defender has featured just 13 times over the past two seasons and dealt with various fitness issues that have kept him sidelined.

6 Gusto (right) and Neto (left) are among the targets for City Credit: Getty

Badiashile is only 25, though, and reports have linked him with Serie A runners-up Napoli, a move that could initially see him join on loan before a permanent switch.

Malo Gusto

It was always going to be difficult for Gusto to hold down the right-back spot when club captain Reece James returned to full fitness.

Premier League rivals Manchester City are understood to be keen on the French full-back, who mostly plays on the right-hand side but can feature at left-back if needed.

Chelsea are understood to value Gusto at £75m and, even though a sale is not being actively looked at, it is possible this summer.

Pedro Neto

Enzo Maresca is seemingly eyeing some Chelsea reunions as the new City boss, with Neto another player to be linked with a switch.

With Rogers and Quenda through the door, Cole Palmer hoping to hit the ground running and Estevao Willian remaining an exciting prospect, the competition for places out wide is strong.

Neto could cost City in the region of £70m, while Liverpool have also emerged as a speculated new club for the Portuguese international.

Enzo Fernandez

Completing the hat-trick of Chelsea to City transfer speculation is Fernandez, whose future in west London has been uncertain for a matter of months now.

6 Fernandez could follow Marc Cucurella as a big-name departure Credit: Getty

After fuelling rumours of a move to Real Madrid, they released a statement to shut down any perceived interest by saying they have 'no intention' of signing him.

City interest in 2022 World Cup winner Fernandez was reported by talkSPORT in April and, with Rodri looking set to leave for Barcelona, this could certainly open the door for a transfer.

Dario Essugo

A thigh injury meant Essugo made a limited number of appearances in his debut season at Chelsea.

The 21-year-old ex-Sporting midfielder is a player who would certainly benefit from consistent minutes away from the club with a loan spell which, as per the BBC, he is open to.

Essugo has featured in all three of their pre-season fixtures thus far but with Moises Caicedo, Romeo Lavia, Fernandez and new man Barco all midfield options, a temporary exit may be wise.

Mykhailo Mudryk

The Football Association announced on July 31 that Mudryk can play for Chelsea once again after the resolution of his anti-doping disciplinary proceedings.

Mudryk's last competitive appearance came in November 2024 and, after months of work to maintain his fitness away from the club, he was a late substitute against Juventus earlier this week.

Coventry City, managed by Chelsea legend Frank Lampard, are among the clubs interested in the winger, who remains electric on the wing.

6 Mudryk is back and available for Chelsea, but may need a loan spell Credit: Getty

Liam Delap

Chelsea were unable to see the best of Delap in his first season after his move from Ipswich Town, where he had become an exciting prospect in English football.

He found the back of the net on just one occasion in the league over 28 appearances, with Joao Pedro being the more impressive striker.

Despite his poor campaign, Delap remained a handful for defenders, has a physical presence up front, and Premier League interest in his services.

Nicolas Jackson

Bayern Munich signed Jackson on loan for the 2025/26 season and he was part of their Bundesliga title triumph alongside Harry Kane, scoring 11 goals in 34 appearances throughout the campaign.

He could have joined them permanently for around £56m, but the conditions to activate the obligation to buy were not met and he is back at Chelsea.

Jackson is on the pre-season tour but has been linked with Villa and Spurs, and is under consideration for an exit.

6 Here is how the Chelsea XI could line up

On paper, this team looks as though it would have a real crack at pushing for European qualification if it played in the Premier League.

However, the Champions League would be a real challenge, so it may have more success in reaching the Europa League or Conference League, depending on the number of qualifying spots for each.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino denies claims ‘lover’ was paid off as UEFA release statement on allegations
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino denies claims ‘lover’ was paid off as UEFA release statement on allegations

Gianni Infantino has denied reports that UEFA paid off his alleged mistress while he was European football's general secretary.

The Telegraph has reported that a woman received a six-figure sum after her supposed relationship with the now under-fire FIFA president.

3 Infantino has held onto his role as FIFA president for now Credit: Getty

Infantino, who is married with four children, is also rumoured to have promoted the junior employee to a management role during the affair.

The publication reports that UEFA paid for the woman's MBA degree after she left the organisation.

Senior figures at UEFA claim Infantino - who is now facing calls to quit over his failed plans to launch the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) - ensured the woman left with the pay-off.

He is said to have been challenged by then UEFA president Michel Platini over the alleged relationship, leading to her departure with payment.

Multiple sources claim that Platini told Infantino that either he or the woman would have to leave.

'Regulations have been tightened'

In a statement released on Friday night, European football's governing body admitted a payment had been made to the woman.

It said all payments were in line with regulations at the time, but those regulations have since been tightened and "reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation".

UEFA also confirmed it was aware of the allegations the individual had been in a relationship with Infantino.

The statement read: “We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school.

"The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time.

3 UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin has led the opposition to Infantino's recent failed FFE scheme Credit: Getty

“Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all UEFA employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.”

As well as the pay-off, UEFA's payment for the woman's MBA course at a business school are said to have totalled around £45,000 per year in fees.

Infantino responds

Infantino has since moved to deny the allegations, with a FIFA spokesperson branding them 'categorically untrue'.

The spokesperson said: “FIFA president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue.

"Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory.

“No employee at UEFA and FIFA has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved.

3 Infantino had already been under pressure for his relationship with the Trump administration Credit: Getty

"All company actions related to employees, including any departure and severance packages, have always been approved by the appropriate directors in accordance with all applicable regulations.”

Infantino joined UEFA in 2000 and spent 16 years there before leaving to become FIFA president in February 2016.

Despite his past ties to the organisation, relations have turned sour between the two parties more recently.

The revelations of his alleged affair come just a week after the collapse of Infantino's proposed FFE scheme, which would have seen stakes in FIFA tournaments sold off to private investors.

Despite the plans being aborted, UEFA have maintained their threat to boycott the World Cup, after Infantino refused to resign from his role as FIFA president.

While there has been opposition from several governing bodies, CONMEBOL - the South American confederation - and the Confederation of African Football (CAF) have backed Infantino, as have the Argentine Football Association (AFA).

Sports.title: EFL club chairman warns about new football trend that’s his latest ‘enemy’
Sports.content:
Peterborough United chairman Darragh MacAnthony has admitted that footballers' dads have become his new enemy.

MacAnthony and Posh have become known for their impressive ability to find and develop young stars in the game.



3 MacAnthony and Peterborough know what it takes to sign and develop a young player Credit: Getty

So, the owner has had to deal with a lot of growing players as well as their agents and parents along the way.

It makes him somewhat of an expert at how to find rising talents and where best to find them across the country.

And that led to a football-loving dad messaging in to talkSPORT's White and Jordan to ask the Peterborough chief for some tips.



After being asked how best to go about getting a youngster into an academy, MacAnthony said: "We have scouts at all levels of games.

"Usually there are development centres nearby, parents need to find development centres for a club.



"Peterborough have development centres hundreds of miles from Peterborough, we have five of them, having players in camps, seeing the talent they are and that potentially leads to scholarships.

"Never stop knocking on the door if you want your kid to get into a good academy, but don't push it over the top.



"Your kid's still young, there's plenty of time."

A 'really difficult' new enemy

talkSPORT host Max Scott then asked about the rising influence of agents in football and whether that has rubbed off onto some players' parents at youth level.

And Posh owner MacAnthony strongly admitted that it had, revealing that his new 'enemy' in the game is players' dads.

3 MacAnthony admitted that dealing with players' dads has become an issue Credit: Getty

"I'll tell you, my biggest enemy used to be agents," he began.

"I deal with all the agents, some good, some bad, some brilliant, and some brilliant people recently that are honest and direct.



"But the one that I've noticed is creeping in is you're dealing with more dads and I'm not sure I love that.

"I just think you need a professional...dads are too close."

MacAnthony continued: "If my son was an athlete, I'd want an expert handling his career and I wouldn't want to get in the way.

"It would cause issues between me and my son and I don't want anything to come in between me and my son.

3 Players looking to build a career seem to have their dads involved in talks Credit: Getty



"But the amount of dads I'm now speaking to is really difficult.

"They're telling me how wonderful their kid is, we all think our kids are wonderful, but I tell people the truth about my kids, yes they're wonderful up to a point, but they're a pain in the neck to another.

"They're not perfect...a lot of these players' dads think they're perfect and they get DMac here who tells them the truth and that's probably why I don't sign a couple of them.

"But you've always got to be honest, right?"
