Sports.title: Liverpool in surprise loan deal to sign Barcelona centre-back as Ibrahima Konate replacement
Sports.content:
Liverpool in surprise loan deal to sign Barcelona centre-back as Ibrahima Konate replacement

Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona, talkSPORT understands.

The surprise transfer comes amid the Reds' lack of depth at centre-back, with Ibrahima Konate leaving earlier this summer.

3 Araujo is set to join Liverpool on loan in a surprise transfer Credit: Getty

Konate departed the club for Real Madrid, signing on a free transfer after his contract at Anfield expired.

It means Virgil van Dijk, new signing Jeremy Jacquet, Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni are the only senior centre-backs in the squad.

So, Andoni Iraola has been keen to bring in an experienced head with the new Premier League season just two weeks away.

A verbal agreement is in place between Barcelona and Liverpool, and Araujo is now set to spend the season in England.

It's understood that the deal is a loan without a buy option.

Araujo on the move

Araujo played 38 games in all competitions last season for Barca, helping lead them as captain to the La Liga title.

In total for the Spanish giants, he's played 213 games across a seven-year span in the first team following his arrival in 2018.

During his spell, he has won three league titles, two Copa Del Reys and three Spanish Super Cups.

The 27-year-old has spent the majority of his career in Spain, only playing for Uruguayan teams Boston River and Rentistas before.

Araujo has also picked up 27 Uruguay caps during his six-year international career, being part of their squad at the World Cup this summer.

3 Araujo departs Barcelona after winning eight trophies and playing over 200 games Credit: Getty

Fourth summer signing

Liverpool are now on the brink of securing their fourth signing of the summer transfer window since Iraola's appointment.

They have already confirmed Jacquet's £60m pre-agreed move.

Meanwhile, Spanish winger Victor Munoz has also joined the club for £35m and teenager Ifeanyi Ndukwe has signed too.

Araujo is set to join them in arriving at Anfield, while the Reds have continuously been linked with Bradley Barcola.

Barcola wants to join the club from Paris Saint-Germain this summer, with Liverpool expected to pursue him.

Tottenham and England's Djed Spence has been linked too, but talkSPORT understands Liverpool are not currently in for him.

3 Araujo will be Liverpool's fourth signing of the summer transfer window Credit: Getty

Mental health break

Liverpool-bound Araujo was granted a leave of absence by Barcelona last season to take a break for his mental health.

He began his break at the start of December last year before returning 'stronger' midway through January.

Posting on social media at the time of his return, with Barca lifting the Spanish Supercopa, the defender said: "I learned that stopping at the right time is self-love."

"Taking care of your mind and heart is not giving up, it is trusting that God works even in silence. Stopping renewed me and allowed me to come back stronger.

"The process was not easy, but coming back like this is a privilege.

"Thank you to the club, my teammates and the fans for their treatment, affection and respect. It was beautiful to return lifting this trophy. We continue together."

Sports.title: Newcastle eye former Tottenham midfielder as shock target amid Bruno Guimaraes sale
Sports.content:
Newcastle are interested in signing ex-Tottenham midfielder Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, talkSPORT understands.

Hojbjerg is viewed as a budget option that will add experience to the squad as Bruno Guimaraes nears a switch to Arsenal.

3 Hojbjerg could potentially be a replacement for Guimaraes at Newcastle Credit: Getty

Captain Guimaraes is set to depart the Magpies and join the Gunners after a £75million deal was finally agreed.

He will follow Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon out the door, while manager Eddie Howe also resigned from his post.

Matthias Jaissle has replaced Howe in the dugout, with this summer becoming one of major change for Newcastle.

And to make up for the loss of some of their key stars and boss, they're going to need some renewed leadership.

Eyeing experience

Hojbjerg could be their chosen man, with the former Spurs player said to be available for around £10m to 15m.

The 31-year-old midfielder played 43 games for Marseille last season, scoring five goals and assisting another five.

But it's his Premier League experience that Newcastle will be attracted to most.

Hojbjerg has played 254 top-flight games in his career - last playing in England for Tottenham in the 2023/24 campaign.

He played 145 times for Spurs in the Premier League during his four-year stay, while also featuring 109 times for Southampton between 2016-2020.

In total, the Denmark international has completed eight seasons in the league, so he won't be unfamiliar should he return.

3 Newcastle want experience and Hojbjerg has played over 250 Premier League games Credit: AFP

Guimaraes latest

Guimaraes has not been confirmed to have left for Arsenal yet, but it's understood that the Brazilian is set to be announced imminently.

Mikel Arteta identified him as a priority target this summer, and after a long saga, the deal has now been agreed.

The 28-year-old left Newcastle's training camp earlier this week to undergo a medical ahead of the move.

He will become Arsenal's fourth summer signing, following Christos Tzolis and Illan Meslier through the door.

Piero Hincapie also made his loan from last season permanent.

As for Newcastle, they're going to have more cash to splash once Guimaraes eventually leaves the club.

3 Guimaraes is set to join Arsenal after a £75m deal was agreed this week Credit: Getty

Hojbjerg is a target to use up to £15m on, while they have already spent nearly £150m on signings in the window.

Bazoumana Toure joined from Hoffenheim for £43m, with Aladji Bamba signing for £34m and Lucas Hornicek for £25.7m.

Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen also joined for a combined £41m.

Sports.title: Arsenal player confirms ACL rupture in heartbreaking statement as Declan Rice reacts
Sports.content:
Arsenal youngster Louie Copley has confirmed that he has suffered an ACL rupture during pre-season duty.

Copley was making his second senior outing for the Gunners on Wednesday as he featured in a 3-1 defeat to Spanish side Real Betis.



2 Copley suffered an ACL rupture playing for Arsenal against Real Betis Credit: Getty

But just nine minutes into his substitute appearance, the 19-year-old suffered a horrible injury, receiving lengthy treatment.

He eventually hobbled off the pitch, with manager Mikel Arteta revealing he was concerned about Copley post-match.

Arteta said: "We’re quite worried for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive, the symptoms that he already has.



"So we’re going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. And yeah, touch wood that he’s not that bad."

'Words can’t describe how I’m feeling'

Unfortunately for Arteta and the Gunners though, Copley has revealed some devastating news in a heartbreaking statement.



On Friday, he posted on Instagram: "Words can’t describe how I’m feeling right now, to making my pre-season debut for the team I’ve grown up supporting to finding out I’ve ruptured my ACL.

"The road ahead won’t be easy but I’ll give everything to come back stronger and better."



Plenty of the Arsenal squad have reacted to Copley's emotional post, replying with their support for the teenage starlet.

Declan Rice replied with a love heart emoji, with Ben White, Max Dowman and Tommy Setford all doing the same.

Jurrien Timber also commented with a praying emoji.

2 Arteta's worst fears were realised as Copley confirmed a serious injury Credit: Getty

Devastating blow

Copley will have hoped to make a big step in his professional career this campaign, having been part of Arsenal's pre-season.



He came off the bench against Girona for his maiden first-team appearance earlier in pre-season, playing 20 minutes.

And then he also featured against Betis, but after being brought on at half-time, his injury saw him taken off soon after.

Copley had appeared on the bench in the Champions League for Arsenal' last season for a clash against 's 3-0 league phase victory over Club Brugge.

The academy product then spent the second half of the campaign on loan at Crawley Town, featuring nine times in League Two.



Sadly, he's now expected to be sidelined for a large part of the upcoming season in what is a huge blow.

Sports.title: Man City set to re-sign World Cup winner immediately after selling James Trafford
Sports.content:
Manchester City are set to sign goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli from Marseille following James Trafford's exit, talkSPORT understands.

Trafford became Leeds United's highest-paid player after completing a club-record £40million move to Elland Road on Thursday.

3 Man City are set to bring in World Cup-winning goalkeeper Rulli Credit: Getty

He had struggled for minutes at City and was unable to displace Gianluigi Donnarumma in goal under Pep Guardiola.

So, the England international opted to move on and sign for their Premier League rivals.

And with Donnarumma expected to continue as Enzo Maresca's No.1, City were left needing to bring in a replacement.

But just a day later, they've struck a deal with Marseille to bring in a new No.2 goalkeeper for a fee in the region of £2.5m.

Rulli is expected to sign a two-year contract at the club with the option for an additional year, talkSPORT understands.

He is set to fly for a medical ahead of the move to Manchester.

Immediate replacement

Man City have swooped in to get a deal done for Rulli instantly after losing their back-up in Trafford to Leeds.

And now, the 34-year-old is set to be Donnarumma's understudy, arriving at City for what is actually his second stint.

He was signed by the club in 2016, but never played a game, leaving to return to his old side Real Sociedad almost straight away.

Rulli has spent the last two seasons with Marseille in France, starting 29 Ligue 1 games last campaign, keeping eight clean sheets.

3 Rulli (left), who was back-up to Emi Martinez at the World Cup this summer, will now be Donnarumma's No.2 Credit: Getty

The year prior, he started 34 games and kept five clean sheets.

Before joining Marseille in 2024, he spent a year in the Netherlands with Ajax, whom he joined from Spanish side Villarreal.

The goalkeeper had been in LaLiga for six years before that, having three different spells at Sociedad in his career.

Rulli started his career in Argentina with Estudiantes - and he's picked up eight caps playing for his country since 2016.

World Cup winner

Despite only playing eight games for Argentina over the last decade, he has become a World Cup winner with his nation.

The veteran was part of the successful squad in 2022 as Lionel Messi finally got his hands on the Jules Rimet trophy in Qatar.

3 Rulli replaces Trafford after he joined Leeds for £40m Credit: Getty

Rulli didn't play a game at the tournament, but still managed to taste the success that so many players dream of.

He was also in the 26-man set-up for Argentina again this summer, but they were beaten in the World Cup final by Spain.

Sports.title: Inside Erling Haaland's unlikely friendship with billionaire founder of Pretty Little Thing: Trips abroad with their WAGs, private yacht jaunts in the South of France and why they bonded
Sports.content:
A little yarn for you. Back in the day, Erling Haaland would pay visits to Pretty Little Thing's all-pink Manchester headquarters. Staff would gawp. What's he doing here?

A reasonable question. What business does a fearsome 6'4" Norse Viking have with a brand who sell trendy outfits to young women and girls?

It turns out that Haaland has a close friendship with Umar Kamani, the fashionista who founded Pretty Little Thing (PLT).

And so, Haaland being Haaland, football's chief of playful nonchalance, he would simply amble in to PLT's office for a chat with his mate. To steal one of the Norwegian's quotes: why not?

That attitude has led to a bromance blossoming. This summer, after chewing up the World Cup, Haaland has been holidaying on a yacht in the French Riviera with Kamani. It's not the first luxury trip they've been on - they have been on holidays to Monaco and St Tropez before and partied together in Dubai.

What's more, the Daily Mail can reveal that one of Kamani's close friends brokered the meeting between Haaland and Michael Jordan which recently went viral.

Erling Haaland has a surprise close friendship with Pretty Little Thing founder Umar Kamani

Haaland used to regularly stroll into PLT's Manchester office while Kamani was there

The pair have been enjoying a summer holiday in the south of France after the World Cup

It's another indicator of Haaland's rising status in the celebrity world and a well-deserved link-up after an exhausting season.

The Manchester City star, 26, recently claimed on Snapchat that his brain is 'fried' after playing in 67 games for club and country last season. Norway's first World Cup in 28 years saw them reach the quarter-finals, beating Brazil along the way. If anyone's joints need soothing in the Mediterranean sun, it's probably Haaland's.

The duo have been merrymaking at the Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc, a stunning coastal resort in Antibes where suites break the bank at up to £7,058 per night. Mind you, that's merely a drop in the ocean for Haaland, who nets close to £1million per week, and Kamani, whose net worth is estimated to be around $1billion (£797m). They've been joined by Haaland's partner Isabel Haugsend Johansen, Kamani's wife Nada, and their friends.

Kamani sat with Haaland's family for Norway's World Cup last-16 victory over Brazil - in which the striker scored two - and the pair linked up for their jaunt almost immediately after they were knocked out by England.

Their friendship dates back to 2022, right when Haaland signed for Manchester City in a £51m deal from Borussia Dortmund. It was a proud moment for the young striker - his father, Alf-Inge, had played for the club, and Erling, who was born in Leeds, claimed to have been a fan his whole life.

Umar, himself a City supporter, was close to some of the players, and they introduced the pair. A source explains that they simply hit it off and the pair have got on ever since. Their shared passion for football, luxury watches, and adventure helps.

By the winter of 2022, five months after they met, Haaland was close enough with Kamani that he received an invitation to the couturier's mansion in Dubai.

That was during the Qatar World Cup, a tournament Haaland missed out on as Norway failed to qualify. The Manchester City star took a mid-season break and visited Kamani with sports therapist Mario Pafundi, who remains one of Haaland's closest allies to this day.

Haaland's viral link-up with Michael Jordan was brokered by one of Kamani's close friends

Kamani's wife, Nada, and Haaland's partner Isabel Haugsend Johansen have also joined them on their trip (pictured in 2024)

In the summer of 2023, Haaland and his father joined Kamani on a luxury superyacht with a host of big names. Among them was Tommy Hilfiger - yes, the man behind the eponymous brand. On the same trip, the striker met up with Prince Albert II of Monaco for lunch. As you do.

To welcome in 2024, Haaland and his girlfriend attended an exclusive party hosted by Kamani in Dubai. The likes of Anthony Joshua and Derek Chisora were there. Fortunately no fights broke out. Kamani turned up in a pink suit and a wore a gigantic mascot head, seemingly of himself.

Haaland also visited the Kamani Club, a private gym owned by the businessman in Dubai. They hung out together in side-by-side ice baths, smiling for a photo, and trained with athletes from a range of disciplines including boxing and tennis.

As far as we are aware, Haaland was not at Kamani's £20m, four-day wedding to his wife Nada in 2024. The lovebirds tied the knot across two lavish ceremonies in the south of France after a fairytale proposal involving a £1.45m ring in August 2021.

But in many ways it makes sense that Haaland and Kamani would become friends, because they share similarities. Haaland is a workhorse powered by long hours in the gym, gigantic barbecued steaks, raw milk, and raw honey. A man who endures the ice bath five times a week. No method is too maverick, no sacrifice too large to prevent him from reaching his goal.

That level of industry is shared by Kamani. The 38-year-old's career has taken him global, but at heart he is a Manchester lad.

He grew up in a house of 18 family members in Chorlton, southwest of the city centre. His grandfather, Abdullah, had escaped war-riddled Kenya in the 1960s and made a living selling handbags from a market stall once he had reached the north west.

Kamani was always destined to go into fashion. His father, Mahmud, co-founded Boohoo in 2006 with Carol Kane. Young Umar caught the bug and set up PLT with his brother Adam in 2012.

After a season of 67 games, Haaland has been letting his hair down in the French Riviera

Haaland and Kamani are pictured with fashionista Tommy Hilfiger during a yacht party

'It’s impossible for me not to be working in fashion. I was born into fashion. That’s like saying if you couldn’t breathe what would you do?' he once told Drapers.

Pretty Little Thing revolutionised the fashion retail industry - suddenly, young people could buy dirt-cheap outfits that looked similar to what their favourite celebrities were wearing.

Design teams monitored the social media feeds of celebs, and within days the company could have rolled out a low-cost mimic of the outfit for regular consumers. Clothes went for as little as six pence.

Not everything was sunshine and roses though. The brand was accused of fuelling a throwaway culture - which is bad for the environment - and killing the high street with deals promising 99 per cent reductions.

On a darker note, its parent company, Boohoo, the Kamani family business, was accused in 2020 of paying employees as little as £3.50 an hour and forcing staff to continue working in shoddy conditions, even after some tested positive for coronavirus.

At a factory in Leicester, the 'sweatshop' scandal resulted in National Crime Agency investigation. The revelations caused a crash in the company's share price. Kamani left PLT as CEO in 2023 but returned to the company in September 2024.

Earlier this year, Boohoo, in which Kamani owns a minority stake, was hit with £10m worth of new legal claims from investors who accuse his father, Mahmud, of knowing about the 'sweatshop' conditions which led to the share price collapse of 42 per cent. Mahmud said in 2020 that he 'cannot possibly know everything in this business'.

Whatever the outcome, one thing is for certain: Umar Kamani and Haaland's bromance helps them let their hair down a few times a year alongside their stressful jobs, and gets them opportunities and access they once would have thought unthinkable.

Sports.title: Man United youngster wanted by Southampton, Ruggeri joining Villa could free up Romero switch, Wednesday chase Liverpool star Scanlon: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Saints eye Man United youngster Kamason

Manchester United full-back Jaydan Kamason is wanted by Southampton.

The Championship side would like the 19-year-old England youth international on a permanent transfer and he is also receiving enquiries from others wanting him on loan.

Preston North End, Blackburn Rovers, Bristol City and Sheffield Wednesday have shown interest in the right-back while there are clubs abroad keen to take him.

Kamason though has a lot of admirers at Old Trafford. He was one of the academy players who excelled in the opening games of United's pre-season, particularly in the 5-0 win over Rosenborg.

He was the first player to sign scholarship forms at United after coming through the club's Emerging Talent Programme, which he joined at 10, while playing for grassroots team Stockport Vikings.

United have yet to decide on plans for his development but he looks likely to stay around Michael Carrick's squad until January.

Goalkeeper Radek Vítek has completed his move to Middlesbrough on a permanent transfer from United in a deal worth up to £14m.

Jaydan Kamason has excelled in pre-season games for United and has plenty of admirers

Atletico's Ruggeri to join Villa for £16m

Atletico Madrid left-back Matteo Ruggeri has agreed to join Aston Villa. The 24-year-old Italian will cost £16m plus add-ons.

His transfer will help pave the way for Atletico to bid for Tottenham captain Cristian Romero.

The Argentine centre-back is also among names being considered by Barcelona but Atletico coach Diego Simeone hopes to convince his compatriot if they can agree on terms.

Matteo Ruggeri's move should pave the way for Cristian Romero to join Atletico Madrid

Facundo Buonanotte leaves Brighton for Elche

Brighton midfielder Facundo Buonanotte has joined La Liga side Elche on a season-long loan.

The 21-year-old was on loan at two different Premier League clubs last season, spending the first half with Chelsea before joining Leeds in the second half of the campaign.

Sheffield Wednesday chase Liverpool star Scanlon

Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon is wanted on loan by Sheffield Wednesday.

The 21-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at Cardiff City and they are keen to take him back too.

Scanlon has impressed on Liverpool's pre-season and is attracting a number of enquiries but League One Wednesday, who play Bolton in the Carabao Cup today, are making a concerted effort to take the England U20 international to Hillsborough.

Sports.title: Liverpool agree surprise loan move for Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo as Andoni Iraola looks to bolster injury-hit defence
Sports.content:
Liverpool are close to completing a loan with option to buy for Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo.

The 27-year-old is preparing to travel to link up with Liverpool on Sunday ahead of signing his contract and meeting his new team-mates. He will also undergo a medical on Sunday.

Araujo wanted to go because after talks with coach Hansi Flick it was apparent he would not be guaranteed regular starts and he believes he will find greater opportunity to do so under Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

The Spanish champions are working to offload a couple of players as they look to upgrade their squad. They are focused on signing Rodri from Manchester City and still want to strengthen their own centre-back options and at striker.

Araujo will say farewell to Barcelona team-mates on Saturday prior to heading for Merseyside on Sunday.

The Uruguay international gives Liverpool experience and vital defensive cover as he is able to play at centre back and right-back.

Joe Gomez suffered a muscle injury in Liverpool's opening pre-season game, while teenage centre back Giovanni Leoni is still recovering from an ACL injury, leaving captain Virgil van Dijk as Liverpool's only fully fit senior centre back.

Liverpool have agreed a surprise deal to sign Barcelona captain Ronald Araujo on loan

The Uruguayan led Barcelona to the LaLiga title last term, but is set for a move to Anfield

The Uruguay international joined Barcelona B in 2018 before being promoted to the first team in 2019.

He has made more than 200 appearances for Barcelona but finds himself down the pecking order in Spain, with the likes of Pau Cubarsi and Gerard Martin ahead of him.

Araujo has therefore taken up the opportunity to move to the Premier League, with more than two weeks still to go until Liverpool's first game of the competitive season.

The 6ft 3in central defender was at the World Cup with Uruguay and was sent off when Barcelona lost 3-0 at Stamford Bridge against Chelsea in the Champions League in November.

He didn't play a minute for his country in North America, though, as he was injured in training and didn't recover in time to feature before Marcelo Bielsa's side were knocked out in the group stage.

The Reds will face Monaco on Sunday in pre-season and then Cesc Fabregas's Como a week later, before starting their campaign against Newcastle on August 23.

Araujo will become the third major arrival at Anfield after the signings of Jacquet and winger Victor Munoz.

Liverpool remain in talks for Paris Saint-Germain pair Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

Sports.title: Revealed: 'Three strict measures' Jose Mourinho has imposed at Real Madrid to lay down his authority - after legendary boss was hired to improve discipline at the Bernabeu
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho has wasted little time putting his stamp on Real Madrid after introducing three strict new measures at the Bernabeu, according to reports.

The legendary former Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham manager returned to the Spanish giants this summer to help improve discipline and restore order to the dressing room after Real Madrid endured a disappointing season without a trophy.

Tasked with managing the personalities of Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior, who agreed a new six-year deal at the club this week, Mourinho has reportedly focused on three key areas to improve standards at the Bernabeu.

According to Spanish outlet AS, the Portuguese has implemented new measures over nutrition, punctuality and recovery from injury.

Firstly, players are told exactly what to eat every day by the club's nutritionist, who used to hold an advisory role but now sets menus for all meals, including breakfast and even afternoon snacks.

Before he arrived, there was more freedom over diet and nutrition but Mourinho is determined to have the kitchen structured around performance as opposed to each player's personal preference.

Jose Mourinho has reportedly introduced three strict new measures at Real Madrid

Rules around nutrition, punctuality and injury recovery has changed since his arrival

For now, despite losing their freedom over food, the players have reacted positively to the new measure, according to the newspaper.

Meanwhile, Mourinho has also changed how players will be punished if they turn up late to training or a meeting at Valdebebas.

Before, poor punctuality would result in financial fines, but now players who turn up late are required to train away from the rest of the team, working out alone in the gym.

Mourinho insists on his players arriving one hour before the start of training and has urged that anyone failing to adhere to this rule will be sanctioned, regardless of status, role or hierarchy.

Finally, the Portuguese boss has ordered that all injury recovery sessions and programmes must now exclusively take place at Real Madrid's Valdebebas training complex.

Eager to make rehabilitation more of a collective task rather than an individual one, Mourinho has banned external treatments and urged that every single medical detail must be coordinated through the club and his staff.

Real Madrid, who finished 12 points behind archrivals Barcelona in LaLiga's title race last season, begin the new campaign with a trip to Espanyol on August 22.

Sports.title: Matheus Nunes opens up on Pep Guardiola's emotional Man City exit, adapting to his new role as a right back - and 'p***ing off' John Stones!
Sports.content:
Eighteen hours after a needlessly dramatic last-minute win over Leeds last November, John Stones ambled out at Manchester City's training complex with Matheus Nunes firmly in his sights.

What might appear an unlikely friendship was forged in wanting to make others laugh. Nunes started most of his days by attempting to get under the skin of Stones at breakfast. Or, in his own words, 'p*** John off'.

So when the Portuguese had been severely at fault for a Dominic Calvert-Lewin goal that launched an improbable comeback, rectifying one mistake from full back only to then lose possession inside his own box in dizzying fashion, Stones saw his opportunity to exact some revenge.

Sources say in that warm down session, the centre half mercilessly mocked his great mate for a comical part in the goal. Nunes had to just take it.

Stones felt safe doing that for two reasons: City won the game via Phil Foden in stoppage time and, more importantly, Nunes had felt a sense of belonging at right back for some time prior.

He had not been able to accept being shifted there by Pep Guardiola for six long months in 2025. He could have left the club.

Matheus Nunes has transitioned from a midfielder to a right back at Manchester City

But once the Leeds gaffe came around, the 27-year-old was already comfortable in his new skin – any mental fragility gone - and now he heads into this Premier League as Enzo Maresca's first choice. This comes after those closest to him had to cajole him into believing in a reimagined destiny while at his lowest ebb.

'When I was playing as a winger, Bernardo [Silva] would call me Thierry Henry,' Nunes says. 'Then I played as a full back and he called me Cafu.

'Bernardo and Ruben [Dias] were so annoying all the time, they were in my head constantly: 'You were good there, you were good there. You need to accept it.' And I was like, no, no, no, all the time.

'I always told my friends that I wasn't a full back. At a certain point you just have to see what the people are saying. You can't be denying it for the rest of your life. If you do, maybe you miss your chance. Now I feel like a full back.'

Nunes struggled to countenance the switch from central midfield, where he had excelled at Wolves. During the process of shifting him into defence Pep Guardiola once said that Nunes wasn't 'clever enough' to feature in the middle for City – comments he privately clarified with the player a day later.

The integration was not easy, Nunes in and out, bruised by mistakes during a derby defeat too – one of them glaring, under-hitting a back pass and then barging Amad over to concede a penalty in blind panic.

'Individually I would say this is probably the most difficult game,' he adds. 'In my head after the game… when you do mistakes as a midfielder, you would never affect the game like that one. I did one mistake and it led to a goal, and then you end up losing the game and that's all you think in your head, you know?

'But it was not only that, it was me coming from a place where it was uncomfortable for me, a position where it was uncomfortable for me, not being able to accept it, because I wasn't accepting it. In my head, it was 'I'm not a full-back. I'm not a full-back'. That's all I was thinking about.

'I think in the Club World Cup, my mindset started to change. Oh, I can actually play good. I had maybe three or four games in a row and then the beginning of last season I started playing every single game. Then your head just flips and you can see it through.'

Nunes saw a psychologist during that transition and Guardiola ended up revealing that he observed elite potential in him as a defender. 'If I didn't change my mindset I would never have played good there and he would never have said stuff like that. He probably said that because he started to see what others couldn't see.

'Then actually seeing Pep during training, the way he believed in me, I felt there was a bit of a difference in the way that we interacted with each other. This stuff, you just feel it, it's not something that I can explain. And once you start seeing all of this stuff, it changes the mindset. It was not easy, of course, but I had a decision to make: do I want to play or do I not want to play? And I wanted to play.'

Nunes begins to become emotional when Guardiola's exit is raised. He talks about the video montage shown to players and staff - of Guardiola's speeches and moments with the squad across a decade - when the manager officially announced his departure to the room.

Nunes offered a new insight into Guardiola's departure and said it was still difficult to talk about

Join the discussion Did Pep Guardiola’s position changes for players help City reach new heights or hold back their talents?

'A lot of people were crying,' Nunes says. 'Pep held it together. He just wanted to get it over [quickly]. It became real that he was actually leaving. It's difficult to talk about.

'It's very hard to say goodbye to someone who gave so much to us all. Someone who put the club to a level that seems unreachable again. What he did was unbelievable. A lot of things are going to change. I've never been in the club without him. It's never easy to say goodbye.'

Adding Silva and Stones into that equation has made it a sombre summer for Nunes specifically.

'Huge losses,' he says. 'If you look at it, John was a very important figure in the club. He was always a joker. The three of us were. I'm just being myself, and then I end up being a clown sometimes. What's the point of life if you're not having a laugh?'

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's 'alleged mistress received six-figure pay-off from UEFA following affair while he was in senior position' - as FIFA president faces mounting calls to quit
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's 'alleged mistress received six-figure pay-off from UEFA following affair while he was in senior position' - as FIFA president faces mounting calls to quit

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The pressure on Gianni Infantino to resign as FIFA president has grown after it emerged UEFA paid off his alleged mistress during his time with the European governing body.

The Telegraph reported the woman received a six-figure sum following an alleged affair with Infantino when he was UEFA general secretary.

It is claimed the junior employee was promoted by Infantino and given a 30 per cent pay rise at the time of their relationship. UEFA's then president, Michel Platini, was reportedly aware and raised concerns with Infantino.

The organisation decided she would depart her role with a substantial sum, paid for by UEFA, which also covered the costs for her to do an MBA course at a business school worth £45,000 per year.

UEFA confirmed the payment and its awareness of the relationship between Infantino and the woman in a statement to The Telegraph.

Infantino has been married to Leena Al Ashqar since 2001 and the couple have four daughters.

UEFA paid off a female employee who had an alleged affair with Gianni Infantino during his time at the organisation

Infantino is under pressure to quit following his failed FIFA Forward Enterprise scheme

'We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school,' UEFA said. 'The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time.

'Such regulations have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all UEFA employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.'

The Telegraph also reported there had been complaints about Infantino's behaviour at FIFA, claims strenuously denied by football's worldwide governing body.

Infantino became UEFA secretary general – a position second only to the presidency in terms of power – in 2009. He started in 2000 as a lawyer before working his way up in the organisation.

The now 56-year-old was elected FIFA president in 2016 following the downfall of Sepp Blatter. He was re-elected in 2019 and 2023, and had been expected to secure a fourth term in March.

The revelations cast further doubt on Infantino's position at FIFA with the Swiss-Italian facing widespread calls to quit after he was forced to abandon a widely condemned plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

UEFA are leading the charge to dethrone Infantino as FIFA president in response to the scrapped proposal, pledging to boycott any FIFA tournaments so long as he remains in the role.

But he appears to retain support from Africa, South America and Asia – which is enough to fend off any leadership challenge ahead of the election, scheduled to take place at the FIFA congress in Morocco in March.

Mexico this week broke ranks from CONCACAF's opposition to Infantino, reaffirming their confidence in the FIFA leadership.

UEFA's current refusal to play in FIFA competitions will cause the governing body significant commercial problems, potentially prompting Infantino to reconsider his position at the top of world football.

But the FIFA president has shown no sign of relenting thus far after being supported by the governing body's hierarchy following crisis talks on Wednesday, vowing to fight on despite demands he resign.

Infantino is facing a possible investigation after Norwegian FA president Lise Klaveness said she would report him to FIFA's Ethics Committee.

The complaint will not only challenge the proposed sale of a £3.1billion stake in the World Cup to private investors, but also the decision to award an ad hoc FIFA Peace Prize to President Donald Trump and the suspension of Folarin Balogun's red card at the World Cup following alleged political pressure from Trump.

Sports.title: ANOTHER ex-NBA player says he is now a woman as he declares for the WNBA Draft and promises to give rivals 'nightmares'... following in the footsteps of former Knicks star
Sports.content:
Royce White has become the second former NBA player to declare for next year's WNBA Draft amid the division surrounding transgender inclusion in sports.

It comes after Enes Kanter Freedom, who stands at 6ft 10in and played in the NBA for 11 seasons, also announced his intention to join the WNBA on Friday afternoon.

White, who is a candidate for the Republican Senate nomination in Minnesota, told Fox News Digital that he is now transgender and wants to join the likes of Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham on the court next season.

'I'm transgender. I'm a woman. I identify as sometimes identifying as a woman for purpose of basketball, professional basketball, so I'll be declaring for the WNBA draft in 2027 as well,' he said.

'I think I'd be unstoppable. But I'm a team-first guy. I'm a pass-first kind of player. I do the little things. I led my team in all five major stat categories at Iowa State University, so I do a little bit of everything.

'I'll do whatever the coach needs me to do. I'll do whatever the girls need me to do.'

Royce White has become the second former NBA player to declare for next year's WNBA Draft

Ex-NBA star Enes Kanter Freedom also vowed to officially declare for the WNBA Draft in 2027

White, a former first-round draft pick who only played three games in the NBA for the Sacramento Kings, insisted that only the WNBA releasing 'a definitive statement about guys with a pair of b**** playing in the Women’s Association' could stop him.

'I don’t want to be discriminated against,' he continued. 'I want fair treatment. I’m a young black, hopefully United States Senator, that would like a fair chance to participate as a sometimes-identifying-as-a-transgender-woman athlete.'

He also vowed to wear a wig while he's playing and said WNBA players will have 'nightmares... and they should' about him potentially competing against them.

'I am 260 pounds, 6ft 8, can palm a men's basketball probably as easily as any player in history,' White, 35, continued. 'I think I had the third biggest hands in the history of the modern NBA Draft combine. I really feel like I'm going to be dominant.'

When asked if he would use the women's locker room in the WNBA, he replied: 'Of course. I don't want to be discriminated against. Why wouldn't I use the women's locker room?

'I have great respect for the skill of women's basketball. They have to play a much more skilled game because they don't have some of the physical God-given abilities as the men.

'So I have great respect for the women's game but there is a significant difference between biological men and women and we've blurred that line, like we've blurred many other lines unnecessarily, and I plan to exploit that for my economic and athletic benefit.'

White's declaration comes amid an ongoing culture war within the WNBA, sparked by Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham after she said in an interview with ESPN that she wants to 'protect young girls' from 'biological men' in sports.

White is a former first-round draft pick who only played three games in the NBA for the Kings

Freedom's announcement comes amid the WNBA's bitter culture war after Sophie Cunningham advocated for restrictions to 'protect young girls' from 'biological men' in sports

Cunningham's comments have left fans, players and coaches in the WNBA divided recently

Since making the comments, the sports world has been left divided.

While some, such as Riley Gaines and Stephen A. Smith, have seemingly sided with the Fever star, others have openly criticized her and booed her on the court.

WNBA star Gabby Williams recently claimed she would 'welcome' a transgender teammate

Recently, the bitter culture war deepened after Golden State Valkyries star Gabby Williams claimed she would happily welcome a trans player to her team.

'I think trans rights, right now, is our new battle,' Williams said in a recent interview, adding: 'We see people's trans rights being stripped away from them; there's a lot of discourse around trans athletes and what they can compete in.

'I would welcome a trans athlete on my team or against my team, anytime,' Williams added. 'I don't think it's a problem in the world.'

In the wake of Cunningham's comments, Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve made her feelings on the topic extremely clear on Sunday – after opting to wear a 'Trans Kids Belong' t-shirt on the sidelines of their game against the Fever.

Freedom shared his own declaration for the WNBA Draft with his fans through a post on social media on Friday afternoon.

In a video, the former New York Knicks and Boston Celtics star said: 'After careful consideration and reviewing the current eligibility guidelines, I'm officially declaring myself a @WNBA prospect.

'If simply declaring who you are is all that’s required, then I meet every single requirement necessary to compete in the WNBA.

A number of political commentators were quick to praise Freedom for his announcement

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve recently wore a 'Trans Kids Belong' t-shirt

'My team and I have carefully examined the WNBA’s eligibility criteria and governing framework surrounding self-identification and inclusion. Based on the current guidelines, I can and am officially declaring my eligibility for the upcoming WNBA draft in April 2027.

'I know my presence on the court will stir up strong opinions. I am definitely not here to mock, make fun of, or disrespect any community or personal choices.

'I’m simply asking that the current rules be applied equally to everyone - the rules that represent the very values many WNBA players and coaches have publicly advocated for.

'My team and I are prepared to ensure these guidelines are applied equally, consistently, and without exception, and I look forward to the #WNBA honoring its stated principles. See you at training camp.'

The 34-year-old was previously picked third overall at the 2011 NBA Draft, before enjoying a career that took him to the Jazz, Thunder, Knicks, Trail Blazers and Celtics. He has not played a professional game since 2022.

Freedom's post quickly went viral on social media as a number of political commentators threw their support behind the NBA veteran and his decision.

Riley Gaines was among those to respond to the post, writing: 'Genius. Perfect. Waiting to see which WNBA team recruits'.

Similarly, Piers Morgan wrote on X: 'Brilliant… now let’s see how keen the @WNBA stars are for men to play in their League.'

Clay Travis, meanwhile, who recently offered to pay $10 million to WNBA champions the Las Vegas Aces if they can beat a high school boys basketball team of his choosing, wrote: 'Amazing. Well done.'

Sports.title: Inside Chelsea's summer clear-out: The price tags slapped on Enzo Fernandez, Nicolas Jackson and Liam Delap, latest on Pedro Neto, why Blues aren't panicking about 46-man squad and the two stars set to sign new deals
Sports.content:
Chelsea’s website currently has 46 player profiles listed for their senior squad and soon there should be another addition. That is Pep Chavarria, a 28-year-old Spaniard whom you may not be familiar with.

Chavarria has a nice backstory. He was still slogging away in Spain’s second division until the age of 24. A late bloomer, the left back made the step up to La Liga with Andoni Iraola's Rayo Vallecano. He frustrated Xabi Alonso last season – in a good way – starring in a 0-0 draw against Real Madrid.

Now he is set for Chelsea and the Premier League and to compete with Jorrel Hato on Alonso’s left-hand side once his transfer from Vallecano – for £16.3million plus £1.7million in add-ons – is confirmed.

Sources within Chelsea are not categorically ruling out further arrivals at Stamford Bridge this summer, though internally, the majority of the focus will now turn to sales in the build-up to September.

A ticking clock is unlikely to spark panic stations within Chelsea. They have been here before. This is what they do. They trade to the very end, submitting deal sheets to the Premier League if necessary to buy them an extra two hours to complete paperwork. While routinely ridiculed for spending significantly, it can be overlooked that they are also good sellers. As good as anyone in football.

We can have our opinions on the incomings, the hits and the misses, but they are up there with the Premier League’s slickest salesmen in terms of outgoings. Keeping hold of core players while swiftly selling those considered surplus is at the heart of the Chelsea operation. They will not let you near the Lamborghini, but will allow you to take the Volvo for a spin before you buy if need be.

Chelsea have 46 players listed as senior squad members on their club website - but club insiders aren't ruling out further additions

Experienced striker Danny Welbeck is one of the fresh faces to arrive at Cobham this summer

He will soon by joined by Rayo Vallecano left back Pep Chavarria (pictured with former boss Andoni Iraola)

Alejandro Garnacho had a subpar season, and yet he is now on loan at Aston Villa. That fee, plus the value of his permanent sale via an achievable clause, means Chelsea stand to make a minor profit on their original £40million investment in the 22-year-old.

Renato Veiga was signed by Chelsea for £10.3million and, combining the £4.7million loan fee from Juventus and his £25.3million sale to Villarreal, they are in line to make almost £20million on the Portuguese. Which is not bad for a player who has appeared in just seven league games for the club.

The same could be said for Joao Felix and the loan fee received from AC Milan and his sale to Al-Nassr. And that is only to name a few examples of Chelsea getting their money back, if not more.

Occasional losses on individuals are inevitable, though Chelsea now need to try to repeat those aforementioned achievements in what remains of this window, again, and again, and again.

Xabi Alonso named 21 substitutes in Chelsea's last friendly, a 1-0 loss to Juventus in Hong Kong. That was without Cole Palmer and Levi Colwill, who were both sidelined by small issues, or those left off the tour of Australia and Asia, such as Benoit Badiashile, Axel Disasi, Marc Guiu, David Datro Fofana and Caleb Wiley, or those yet to return from representing their countries at the World Cup, like Enzo Fernandez, Reece James, Jordan Henderson, Maxence Lacroix, Valentin Barco, Malo Gusto or Morgan Rogers.

No European football for next season means Chelsea cannot afford to have such a crowded changing room, for the harmony and the financials, and so there are plenty of players available for sale or loan.

The next month will tell us whether Chelsea are ready to rise to the challenge again, though it might be misleading to tag this as a 'fire sale'. That suggests assets for sale at deeply discounted prices, whereas those within Stamford Bridge tend to try to stick to the valuations they set.

Among the asking prices we have had stood up, they want £120million for Fernandez, £75million for Gusto, and £65million for Nicolas Jackson. They would seek more than the £30million they spent on Liam Delap if he is to be sold permanently this summer. Delap would not be the first player, nor the last, to be moved on after a single season if so. Chelsea, as mentioned, are swift.

Xabi Alonso named 21 substitutes in Chelsea's last friendly, a 1-0 loss to Juventus in Hong Kong, despite being without many players

Chelsea want more for Enzo Fernandez than the £117million they paid for Rogers this summer

But Joao Pedro is believed to be in line for a new deal after Barcelona were told he is 'untouchable' in this window

Pedro Neto’s valuation is not yet publicly known amid interest from several sides including Manchester City, but Chelsea believe wingers are hot property in this window. They have noted how Real Madrid are spending up to £120million to sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig, for example. It would take a significant fee to convince Chelsea to sell Neto, who remains highly rated internally.

Fernandez is a special case after such a noisy summer. City and Real Madrid have continued to be linked to the Argentinian, though we have not yet heard of an official approach being made to open club-to-club negotiations. If that happens, any suitors will be told by Chelsea that they want more for Fernandez than the £117million they paid for Rogers this summer.

Fernandez is scheduled to return to Cobham soon after his World Cup break, and presumably that will coincide with talks between the club, the player and his representative, Javier Pastore.

Joao Pedro is believed to be in line for a new deal after Barcelona were told he is 'untouchable' in this window, and while names have not been provided, he is not the only one expected to commit himself to Chelsea in the near future. We suspect Levi Colwill will be another.

Jackson is among their more sellable strikers. He is liked by Villa, who have a healthy relationship with his club. We also heard how Tottenham asked about his situation after their pre-season friendly with Chelsea in Sydney as they assess striker options. Spurs claim they are not expected to explore a move. Others abroad admire Jackson, too. His situation is one to watch in these coming weeks.

Clearly, Chelsea still have work to do in this window, it never being a dull day around Cobham or Stamford Bridge. Let the selling and loaning commence.

Major update in hunt for child rapist who escaped while on escorted leave in Perth

Cliff Lyons Dobbie absconded on Friday with a major manhunt launched

A convicted child rapist has been caught after he absconded from staff while on leave.

A major manhunt was launched for Cliff Lyons Dobbie on Friday after the restricted patient absconded from Perth, Scotland, while on escorted leave.

The incident saw police launch a widespread manhunt for the paedophile. Police Scotland confirmed Dobbie was later caught on Saturday morning and apprehended.

Sports.title: Inside Mo Salah’s Trabzonspor deal including shirt number gesture and REAL reason for switch
Sports.content:
Inside Mo Salah’s Trabzonspor deal including shirt number gesture and REAL reason for switch

Former Liverpool star Mohamed Salah has chosen his new club - here's how Trabzonspor completed one of the summer's most eye-catching deals

View 3 Images Mohamad Salah has signed for Trabzonspor (Image: Huseyin Yavuz/Dia Photo via AP)

One of the biggest transfer sagas of the summer has been resolved, with Mohamed Salah choosing Trabzonspor. The Egypt international joined the Turkish club after confirming his Liverpool departure months ago.

‌



Salah ended his time in English football after a difficult final season at Anfield, where he often didn't see eye to eye with Liverpool manager Arne Slot. A change of manager didn't prompt a U-turn, with new Reds boss Andoni Iraola continuing without the two-time title winner.

‌



The 34-year-old forward was mobbed by fans as he arrived in Turkey to sign with his new employers. The signing is no doubt a popular one but some eyebrows were raised when Salah opted for a club not in the Champions League.

‌



So, why did Salah choose Trabzonspor? We've taken a closer look at how the deal came about and what to expect now.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

OPINION Mo Salah is taking a step down with Turkey move but it is about more than just money by Andy Dunn

‌



Salah's motivation

When it emerged that Salah would be leaving Liverpool, there was some speculation about him simply moving to the highest bidder. However, according to Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan, that couldn't be further to the case.

"You cannot persuade and bring a player like Salah with money," Dogan said, as reported in the Turkish media. "One of the contract offers he presented to us was four times the amount we offered. His intention was not financial; he wanted to experience the excitement and passionate love here."

Trezeguet's role

Dogan also pointed to the role played by Trezeguet, Salah's international team-mate. The former Aston Villa playmaker made 70 appearances for the Super Lig side, scoring 23 goals, before moving to Al Ahly in 2025.

‌



View 3 Images Salah's fellow Egypt international Trezeguet had a part to play (Image: Maciej Rogowski/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Every subscription now comes with 135 channels alongside free subscriptions to HBO Max, Netflix, Disney+, discovery+ and Hayu.

Trabzonspor's president said the 31-year-old gave Salah a "positive reference" which convinced him to join. Salah's new team-mates include others with Premier League experience as well, such as goalkeeper Andre Onana - on loan from Manchester United for a second season - and former Southampton striker Paul Onuachu.

‌



Squad number help

Salah has made a squad number change of sorts, abandoning the 11 he wore at Liverpool and moving to the No.10 which he also wears for his country. However, this was only made possible by new team-mate Ernest Muci agreeing to sacrifice the number he wore last season.

"I thank Muci regarding the jersey," Dogan said. "Him voluntarily coming and handing over the jersey number to Salah was a very valuable stance. This gesture moved us."

View 3 Images Salah will wear the No.10 shirt at his new club (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Wrapping up the deal

According to Trabzonspor's president, the deal took between four and five days to get over the line. He also shed some light on the finances behind the deal, indicating recent sales made things easier - goalkeeper Ogurcan Cakir left in a club record £23.5m sale last summer while Ivorian international Christ Inao Oulai joined Fiorentina for not much less.

"When Istanbul teams make big transfers, it's not talked about, but when we do it, it becomes a topic of discussion," Dogan said. "We have made player sales exceeding 100 million Euros in the last year. It is quite natural for a club with this financial power to add any player it wants to its squad."

Salah could make his competitive debut for Trabzonspor on August 15 when they begin their Super Lig campaign away to Kasimpasa. Five days later the Turkish side have a huge match in the form of a Europa League play-off first leg against either Ferencvaros or Gornik Zabrze.

Ticket prices for all League One clubs ahead of the 2026/27 campaign have been revealed

Sports.title: 'I signed five-year deal at Arsenal and left after six months – I didn't trust manager's plan'
Sports.content:
'I signed five-year deal at Arsenal and left after six months – I didn't trust manager's plan'

Arsenal have handled plenty of transfers over the years but one five-year contract renewal ended prematurely

View 3 Images David Bentley's Arsenal tenure ended rather abruptly (Image: Getty)

David Bentley left Arsenal just six months after penning a five-year deal. The midfielder cited a lack of trust in Arsene Wenger, who was the last manager to guide the club to a league title before Mikel Arteta's success last season.

‌



The Gunners have earned major credit following their Premier League title win and some big names are being linked with a move to north London this summer. Arteta has secured Piero Hincapie, Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis so far.

‌



But one former player who would have enjoyed more time in north London, in hindsight, is Bentley. The Englishman joined the Gunners at 13 and enjoyed his youth career in north London. He signed his first professional deal in 2001 and debuted under Wenger two years later. However, Bentley went out on loan to Norwich City in 2004 and handed in a transfer request upon his return.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal forced to release short statement after Christos Tzolis debut READ MORE :

Arsenal could still add another blockbuster signing aside from Vinicius Jr or Bruno Guimaraes READ MORE :

He secured a move to Blackburn in January 2006 after impressing on loan and eventually signed for Arsenal's rivals Tottenham for £15million in 2008. But, during an appearance on the Undr The Cosh podcast, Bentley admitted that he should've spent more time with the Gunners but didn't have confidence in Wenger's plans.

View 3 Images Bentley spoke out about his time as a Gunner (Image: Undr The Cosh/YouTube)

‌



He said: "When we were playing, you were under much more pressure than players are nowadays. Much more pressure. Because, if you found yourself out the team, you were criticised more than you are now. Now, you're a squad player. Just having a rest, not in the squad today.

"[I left Arsenal because] I wanted to play. I signed a five-year deal and left after six months! Wenger was like, 'No, do this.' He had a plan, didn't he? But I couldn't see that plan. Didn't trust it.

"Potentially, I could have stayed; I should have stayed. Remember, I saw the young lads come through, Cesc. I made my debut with Fabregas - my full debut.

‌



"Absolutely unbelievable performance from him. We beat Wolves 5-1 at Highbury. He dominated the game at 15 years old. I was only like 17. Eighteen months older, or two years older than him."

After leaving Arsenal, Bentley's time at Blackburn was the peak of his career. The midfielder was named the club's Player of the Year in 2007 as he was linked with a move to Manchester United.

View 3 Images The Englishman would go on to sign for Spurs (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

In 2008, he headed to Spurs and his first goal for his new side was arguably his greatest. Bentley fired in a 43-yard volley during a 4-4 draw with his former club Arsenal.

This incredible goal was not indicative of what was to come, as the ex-England international would go on loan four times while at Spurs. He had stints at Birmingham City, West Ham, FC Rostov and a return to Blackburn before retiring at just 29 after being released by Tottenham.

Sports.title: UEFA ‘paid off’ Gianni Infantino’s alleged lover as pressure grows on FIFA president
Sports.content:
UEFA ‘paid off’ Gianni Infantino’s alleged lover as pressure grows on FIFA president

Gianni Infantino's position as FIFA president could come under fresh scrutiny following allegations of an affair with a junior member of staff while he was general secretary of UEFA

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino is facing allegations about his time at UEFA (Image: Abdelmajid BZIOUAT / AFP via Getty Images)

Gianni Infantino allegedly arranged for his lover to be paid off by UEFA while he was in a position of power at European football’s governing body.

‌



Infantino is now desperately trying to hold onto his position as president of FIFA, but allegations about the 56-year-old’s behaviour at his previous employer, which he denies, have now surfaced.

‌



The Telegraph reports that a female employee of UEFA, who was allegedly in a relationship with Infantino, allegedly received a six-figure pay-off and funds to study an MBA after he was challenged over the situation.

‌



Infantino, who is married with four children, was UEFA’s general secretary at the time of the alleged affair with a junior employee, who was promoted to a management position during the relationship.

Gianni Infantino state of play as 211 nations decide desperate FIFA president's fate READ MORE :

UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement READ MORE :

He is said to have been challenged by Michel Platini, UEFA’s then president, over the alleged relationship, prompting her to leave the organisation with a substantial payment.

A UEFA spokesperson told the newspaper: “We are aware of the allegations and can confirm a departure payment was made to the individual in question, coupled with the payment of fees for an MBA course at a local business school. The payment was in line with the regulations that existed for departing staff at the time.

‌



“Such UEFA have been tightened since 2016 and the current staff regulations – which apply to all UEFA employees at whatever level – reflect those found in a modern, high-profile organisation.” Mirror Football has contacted UEFA.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been married to Leena Al Ashqar for 15 years (Image: Roberto SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images)

The allegations come at a time of increased scrutiny on Infantino, who is fighting to hold onto power at the top of FIFA following a backlash over his secretive plans to sell stakes in tournaments like the World Cup. His former employer, UEFA, are now the organisation leading the attempts to remove him from power.

‌



“FIFA president Gianni Infantino strongly denies these allegations, and they are categorically untrue. Any insinuation of inappropriate conduct or violation of statutes or regulations is defamatory,” a FIFA spokesperson told the Telegraph.

“No employee at UEFA and FIFA has ever raised a complaint regarding Mr Infantino’s behaviour because there never was an incident where he was involved. All company actions related to employees, including any departure and severance packages, have always been approved by the appropriate directors in accordance with all applicable regulations.”

Infantino spent 16 years working for UEFA until leaving to become FIFA president in February 2016, a position he has held ever since.

Article continues below

He married Leena Al Ashqar in 2001 after they met through her work for the Lebanese Football Federation.

Sports.title: Andrew Flintoff releases statement after shock England departure and confirms next job
Sports.content:
Andrew Flintoff releases statement after shock England departure and confirms next job

England cricket legend Andrew Flintoff has confirmed he has left his job with England Lions ahead of moving to a role in Australia later in the year

View 2 Images Andrew Flintoff has stepped down from England Lions (Image: Gareth Copley/Getty Images)

Ashes icon Andrew Flintoff has announced his decision to step away from his coaching role with the England Lions. The England cricket legend is set to join Sydney Thunder later this year in Australia's Big Bash League.

‌



Flintoff, who started his role with the Lions in September 2024, leaves after less than two years in the position. The 48-year-old earned the job after first working with England's one-day team in an informal consultant role as he recovered from significant injuries he suffered in a car crash filming for the television show Top Gear.

‌



The ECB had permitted Flintoff to leave an upcoming tour to South Africa early to coach in the Big Bash, but Flintoff has made the decision to end his time with the international set-up.

‌



He has joked that his replacement has 'big pants to fill'. Mike Yardy will step in as head coach for the four-day Professional County Club Select XI match against Pakistan Men next week.

Posting on Instagram, Flintoff said; "Unfortunately, I’ve made the decision to step away from my role with the Lions. Not only have I enjoyed my time having the opportunity to work with the best young cricketers in the country, but have taken great pride in seeing them develop.

FA announce changes after tragic death of ex-Arsenal footballer aged 21 READ MORE :

UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement READ MORE :

"I’d like to thank the coaches and staff for all their passion, tireless work and support they give everyday.

‌



"In particular Ed Barney who I’ve loved working with and was so lucky to have as a performance director, and obviously Rob for trusting me with one of the most Important roles in English cricket.

"I can’t wait to get started with the Thunder later in the year and see where coaching takes me. Good luck to whoever takes over you have some big pants to fill."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Ed Barney, ECB men's performance director, said: "Fred has helped to transform the Lions environment into a programme that has had a major impact on young players. By creating an environment that both supports and pushes excellence at all times he has helped bring forward a new generation of young players.

"Coaches have also flourished alongside him, whether early in their coaching journey or with decades of experience, and he has consistently maximised the expertise around the group. We wish him the best in the next stage of his coaching career and look forward to a time he returns to the English game."

Flintoff had come under severe scrutiny for his decision to take on the Sydney job while in charge of England's Lions. Managing Director of England Men's Cricket, Rob Key, defended Flintoff, suggesting that his passion should not be doubted, as he could have earned more money doing something different with his career.

‌



"I saw something I thought was unfair, actually, on Andrew Flintoff, where it said he shouldn't have been doing that Lions job because he's not doing this job now, the England head coach's job," Key said.

"I think that's done a complete disservice to one of our greatest cricketers who, for the last three [sic] years, has done that Lions job when he could have done a hell of a lot of other things, earning a lot more money. But his passion [is] to actually try and bring the next generation through, and people like Sonny Baker, Mitch Stanley… so many of these players have come under his wing."

View 2 Images Freddie was involved in a serious crash while filming an unaired series of Top Gear back in 2022 (Image: PA)

‌



Flintoff's return to cricket came after a difficult time recovering from his brutal Top Gear crash. The former all-rounder suffered serious facial and rib injuries after the open-topped three-wheeled vehicle he was driving rolled over.

Speaking on Freddie Flintoff’s Field Of Dreams: Ultimate Test, he said: "It was, what – 18 months ago? And you know, I’ve suffered with things like depression in the past before, but this time was different. I didn’t know if I had it in me to carry on, not that I wanted to die or anything like that, I just didn’t know if I had it in me, and that took a while.

“The one thing, I think, getting quite deep here, but the one thing you just want to be is happy in yourself, and try and be accepting of yourself of what you are. It took me a long time to be like that, and then the crash put me back again, and now it’s like finding myself or finding the person I want to be.”

Sports.title: Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry
Sports.content:
Man Utd contacted by Newcastle after launching Lewis Hall transfer enquiry

Newcastle have sold Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer, with Bruno Guimaraes also set to leave, and attention has now turned to Manchester United target Lewis Hall

View 2 Images Newcastle don't want to sell Lewis Hall (Image: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle have made it clear to Manchester United that Lewis Hall is not for sale this summer at any price. United are keen to sign a left-back in this window and have kept an eye on Hall for some time, but it seems Michael Carrick won't get his man this summer.

‌



United prioritised central midfield in the early stages of the window, with Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos arriving from Aston Villa and Chelsea respectively for a combined £87million.

‌



Left-back is now a position on the agenda, with Carrick wanting competition for Luke Shaw, who impressed last season but has a chequered injury history. Academy graduate Harry Amass would be allowed to leave for the right price, while last summer's signing Diego Leon has failed to kick on so far and Tyrell Malacia left on a free transfer.

‌



Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui can both play left-back if needed, but Patrick Dorgu has shone further forward, convincing United to go back into the market.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

United thought they could take advantage of the turmoil at Newcastle this summer, with Eddie Howe being replaced by Matthias Jaissle. But the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and the pending exit of Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal has worked against them.

‌



Sky Sports reports that Newcastle have told United in no uncertain terms to look elsewhere. The Magpies first communicated their stance two weeks ago and consider the matter to be settled.

Newcastle's hierarchy are under pressure to steady the ship following the exits of Howe, Gordon, Tonali and Guimaraes. Sporting director Ross Wilson has taken the approach of publicly explaining the £75m sale of Guimaraes to Arsenal.

"What we had to weigh up was, very respectfully from Bruno with his behaviour towards us, very emotionally as well, he effectively told us he wanted to leave and move on," he said.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes' exit has strengthened Newcastle's stance on Lewis Hall (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

"That doesn't mean he can go, but it certainly plays a part in what our thinking is when we hit a certain range of number. There's no part in saying it was part of our strategy and was in our thinking this summer - it wasn't. But we have got to be flexible and react to things that happen."

Unlike Guimaraes, Hall is not agitating for a move. The 21-year-old joined Newcastle for £35m from Chelsea three summers ago and has been a regular fixture on the left side of defence.

Article continues below

With Hall appearing to be a dead end, United could turn their attention to Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas, who is considered to be a viable alternative. The 19-year-old is highly rated and has a €16m (£13.7m) release clause, although United could face competition from Barcelona. Bologna's Jhon Lucumi, who is valued at €25m (£21.7m) is another option.

Sports.title: FA announce changes after tragic death of ex-Arsenal footballer aged 21
Sports.content:
FA announce changes after tragic death of ex-Arsenal footballer aged 21

Former Arsenal youngster Billy Vigar suffered a significant brain injury back in September last year, with changes now being put in place by the Football Association

View 2 Images Billy Vigar passed away in September (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The Football Association (FA) have announced that solid walls around the perimeter of pitches have been banned following the tragic death of Billy Vigar. The former Arsenal youth player died from a head injury after colliding with a wall last season.

The incident occurred with Vigar playing for Chichester City against Wingate & Finchley FC back in September. The 21-year-old collided with a concrete wall surrounding the pitch, resulting in a significant brain injury.

Vigar was part of Arsenal’s youth sides before moving to Hastings United in 2024. He signed with Chichester City last summer, a few months before his death.

The wall at Wingate & Finchley FC has now been removed, with the FA confirming a review of pitch surroundings for non-league grounds . The findings of the review have now been released.

It has been confirmed that the FA: "no longer permits solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers around pitches across the National League system for men [steps 1-6], and the Women's National League [tiers 3-4]".

UEFA could boycott 5 tournaments in next 11 months after new Gianni Infantino statement READ MORE :

In a statement, the FA added: "Any existing solid brick, breeze block or concrete barriers must be removed as soon as reasonably practicable, or covered with suitable protection if they cannot be removed for structural reasons. We have informed the clubs at this level that will be required to take action as a result of these changes.

"Matches may continue to be played at affected grounds during this period; however, clubs should assess the safety of their pitch perimeter barriers on an ongoing basis, and where alterations to these structures have been recommended during this review, they should develop a plan to complete any such alterations within a reasonable timeframe."

Non-league clubs will be helped with funding the changes with the money coming from both the FA and the Premier League. The Press Association reports that 160 of the 900 clubs who play at the levels have been contacted over changes that will have to be made to their stadiums.

View 2 Images The FA have announced changes following the youngster's tragic death (Image: Getty Images)

The FA added: "The initial phase of the programme is already underway, and we will continue to provide full support to the clubs involved in this process.”

Following the announcement, a PFA spokesperson said: “Following the tragic death of Billy Vigar last year, we again highlighted these concerns and made clear our view that the lack of progress and leadership on this issue had been unacceptable.

"As part of working groups set up by the FA following Billy's death, we pushed for the FA's Stadium Accreditation criteria to be amended to ban these types of walls so that there is a clear and centralised policy for clubs to follow.

"Given that, it's a welcome step that the FA's regulations have now been changed to reflect that position.

"However, it will now be important for progress on the removal of such walls - and effective mitigation of risks ahead of their removal - to be properly monitored, and for clubs to be given the support they need so that these changes can happen as soon as possible. Player safety must always come first."
