World.title: Clinton compares Trump’s White House to former Iraqi dictator Saddam’s palaces
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Former US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton has compared President Donald Trump’s White House renovations to former Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein’s palaces, remembering her own travels to Baghdad after his ouster.

Clinton, speaking on journalist Kara Swisher’s podcast, compared Trump’s White House decor to meetings she attended in Saddam Hussein’s former palaces while serving as a US senator.

“They were quite reminiscent of what we are seeing in our own White House,” she said.

Her remarks come amid wider criticism of Trump’s renovations and architectural decisions, such as heavy gold décor within the Oval Office, plans for a new White House ballroom, and a projected triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery.

Clinton called the improvements “tacky” and suggested that the president was focusing too much on cosmetic initiatives when the US confronts substantial foreign policy, economic, and technological issues.

She also criticized the process around Trump’s planned ballroom, stating that she was not opposed to the White House having such a facility but was concerned about the architecture and how the project had been handled.

Given Clinton’s past with Iraq, the connection to Saddam was especially relevant.

She was a member of the United States Senate during the 2003 war that deposed Saddam Hussein and subsequently became Secretary of State under President Barack Obama.

During his reign, Saddam was noted for building multiple extravagant presidential palaces around Iraq, many with elaborate interiors and significant use of marble, chandeliers, and gold-colored décor, despite the country’s international sanctions and economic difficulty.

Trump has defended his White House restoration plans, which are part of a larger push to renovate and enhance Washington’s important federal buildings and sites.

Clinton’s parallel brings Iraq and one of Saddam’s most recognizable emblems into the increasingly heated political argument over Trump’s White House moves.

World.title: Apple officially enters Iraq under new digital services framework
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Apple has legally joined Iraq’s regulated digital market, having met the country’s standards for digital platforms and services, according to the Communications and Media Commission (CMC).

According to the regulator, Apple has been categorized as a trusted digital service provider in Iraq, which includes the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, Apple Arcade, and Apple Ads.

The certification means Apple’s digital services may now function under an official Iraqi regulatory framework, having passed the CMC’s technical and legal standards.

Iraqi officials said the decision is anticipated to boost the country’s digital economy and enhance the investment climate for multinational technology firms.

The development also corresponds with a significant step toward Apple’s physical presence in the Iraqi market. Asiacell has reached a direct arrangement with Apple to include iPhones in its retail network across Iraq.

As part of the cooperation, Asiacell will provide real Apple products with valid warranties throughout its network, while retail personnel will undergo Apple-approved training.

The regulatory permission and Asiacell deal represent a substantial change in Apple’s position in Iraq, pushing both digital services and official device distribution further into a market of over 46 million people.

The move is another indication of Iraq’s quickly emerging technology and consumer market, as Baghdad attempts to lure global corporations, legalize digital services, and promote increased investment in the country’s information technology industry.

World.title: Al-Ghodwa deploys Linde warehouse equipment in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Linde Material Handling of Germany has completed a new warehouse technology project in Baghdad with its official Iraqi partner, Al-Ghodwa Group, as modern logistics systems gain traction in Iraq.

The project was completed in early August, and it comprised the installation and commissioning of two Linde Very Narrow Aisle (VNA) trucks built for high-density warehouse operations.

As part of the turnkey project, Al-Ghodwa installed the guiding system, calibrated and tested the equipment, and taught the local operators.

The technology enables firms to store more items in their current warehouse space by running equipment securely in tighter lanes, which increases productivity and reduces space needs.

The project combines Linde’s German warehouse technology with local installation, maintenance, and after-sales services in Iraq.

Linde Material Handling is a subsidiary of Germany’s KION Group, one of the world’s biggest producers of industrial vehicles and a leading supplier of warehouse automation systems.

The Baghdad installation comes as Iraq’s logistics and distribution industry grows, amid investment in manufacturing, retail, transportation, and private-sector growth.

World.title: Saudi renews invitation to Iraq PM as Baghdad, Riyadh seek to repair ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Saudi Arabia has extended an invitation to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to visit Riyadh as the two countries try to regain momentum in ties after a dangerous escalation involving Iran-backed militias operating from Iraqi soil.

Al-Zaidi met with Saudi intelligence head Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan in Baghdad on Friday, with the Saudi official conveying a message from the kingdom’s leadership extending the offer and discussing greater security cooperation, according to the Iraqi government.

The meeting is notable since Al-Zaidi canceled a scheduled visit to Saudi Arabia last month in response to US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq.

These operations followed a series of drone assaults on Saudi Arabia.

Riyadh claimed that Iran-backed militias fired drones from Iraqi territory, attempting to damage oil installations in the Eastern Province and targets near Riyadh, and publicly urged Baghdad to prevent its land from being used as a launchpad for assaults against the country.

Saudi Arabia then launched operations with US troops against Iran-backed militia strongholds in Iraq, increasing pressure on Baghdad to bring armed organizations operating outside of effective official control under its authority.

During Friday’s meeting, Al-Zaidi underlined Iraq’s refusal to allow its land to be used for attacks on Saudi Arabia or any other country, emphasizing Baghdad’s commitment to sovereignty, good neighbor relations, and regional security.

According to the Iraqi statement, the two sides agreed to maintain information sharing and security cooperation, with Baghdad aiming to avoid future assaults that may prompt another military reaction on Iraqi soil.

The outreach coincides with Saudi Arabia’s efforts to deepen regional security relationships.

On Friday, Riyadh, Ankara, and Islamabad signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, which states that any military assault on one of the three nations is considered an attack on all.

Saudi authorities are also apprehensive about additional strikes by Iran-aligned forces.

For Al-Zaidi, the repeated Saudi invitation provides a chance to mend ties with one of Iraq’s most significant Arab neighbors while also displaying Baghdad’s determination to prevent Iran-backed forces from dictating its regional connections.

The implications extend beyond security. Iraq has been pursuing more Saudi and Gulf investment as part of a larger push to diversify its economy, attract foreign money, and enhance trade and infrastructural ties with its Arab neighbors.

As a result, Friday’s meeting constitutes a crucial step in moving Baghdad-Riyadh relations past last month’s dispute. However, continued progress is likely to be strongly dependent on Iraq’s capacity to show that attacks on its neighbors would not be launched from its territory in the future.

World.title: Spain imposes border checks on Italy as migrant showdown grows
World.content:
Madrid – Spain announced on Friday it would introduce temporary border checks on travellers from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass migrant rush into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until September 7, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

Hours earlier, Spain threatened Italy with countermeasures if it did not swiftly lift its own border checks, drawing a rebuff from Rome.

The rare spat between the European Union and NATO allies came after tens of thousands of people crossed from Morocco to Spain’s North African territory on July 30-31 in an unprecedented, deadly rush.

The scenes infuriated EU members that back a hard line on irregular immigration, including Italy which imposed a one-month suspension of its visa free-travel Schengen deal with Spain.

The Spanish government slammed the measure Friday as “unfair, contrary to the EU’s interests and discriminatory for the Spanish population”.

Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares described it as “a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity.”

“We urge the government of Italy to rectify, put an end to the checks and treat Spaniards like other European citizens,” the government said.

He threatened “proportional measures” in response by Sunday if Italy failed to comply.

– ‘Creating rifts’ –

Within hours, the government of Italy’s far-right Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said it “had no intention of revising the decision” before August 15, when it said Spanish authorities “expected a new wave of migration” to hit Ceuta.

“Italy does not accept ultimatums or impositions from abroad regarding national security and border control,” Meloni’s office said in a statement.

“Only when there is certainty that there are no security or terrorism risks to Italy, that no new wave is occurring, and that no irregular migrants are heading toward European territory, will the decision be reconsidered,” it read.

Spain’s interior ministry announced the reciprocal measures within hours.

Spanish police have been monitoring online rumours and social media about possible fresh arrivals in Ceuta in mid-August, according to local media. But authorities have not expressly said they expect a repeat of last week’s rush.

Border authorities would in the meantime “do their utmost to ensure maximum ease of movement for Spanish and European citizens” who are not affected by border checks, the Italian statement added.

Italy, which does not share a land border with Spain, introduced border controls at maritime and air entry points for third-country nationals arriving from the Iberian country.

The move announced on July 31 was an “extraordinary measure” intended to “safeguard national security and prevent possible repercussions for our nation”, Meloni said at the time.

She was among EU leaders who called for Spain to be suspended from the visa-free Schengen travel zone after the Ceuta incident, despite such a move being legally impossible.

Italy’s coalition government has sought to stop the tens of thousands of people who land in small boats on the country’s shores each year.

The Spanish government warned against “creating rifts and sterile conflicts driven by internal electoral motives” and said “we trust that pro-European sentiment, common sense and good faith prevail”.

Of the 72,000 people who entered Ceuta, 70,000 have returned to Morocco, according to official Spanish figures.

Spanish authorities said 80 people died in the crossings.

Moroccan rights groups however estimate the figure to be higher. The Moroccan Association for Human Rights (AMDH) and the European Coordination for Human Rights in Morocco on Friday said at least 141 deaths were recorded and that the toll was likely to rise.

Morocco’s interior ministry has said 11 people died on its side of the border, all but one by drowning.

Those who remain in Ceuta — including hundreds of unaccompanied children — face dire living conditions with little access to food, water, and shelter.

World.title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan sign defence pact amid regional war
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement on Friday amid violence in the region from Houthi attacks and the US-Iran war.

Riyadh is looking to strengthen its security ties against the backdrop of war between the United States and Iran, which has drawn in surrounding nations and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

The war has emboldened Iran and its Houthi allies in Yemen, both of which have attacked Saudi Arabia, while analysts say Washington is now seen as an increasingly unreliable partner.

In a joint statement published by the official Saudi press agency and Pakistan’s foreign ministry, the three countries announced the signing of the “Mecca Joint Defence Agreement”.

They declared a “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security and stability in the region and beyond”.

Pakistan’s foreign ministry said the pact meant an attack on any member would be regarded as an attack on all, adding it was “intended to strengthen collective deterrence”.

Ankara nonetheless said later that the agreement was “not aimed at any particular country”, according to a post on X by the presidency’s communications director.

It added that “the agreement is not in contradiction with the commitments of Turkey’s existing international alliances, including those at the heart of NATO,” according to a post on X by the government’s anti-disinformation service.

Riyadh said “the agreement does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc”.

“Nor is it linked to any nuclear ambitions or arms race, rather it is focused on building sustainable capabilities,” Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly said on X.

The “does not constitute a threat to the security of any country in the region”, he added.

– ‘Layers of security’ –

Since the onset of the regional war, Saudi Arabia has grown closer to Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan, which have been pushing for mediation and a resolution to the conflict.

Umar Karim, an expert on Saudi foreign policy at the University of Birmingham, England, said the alignment “is clearly oriented towards Iran and meant to address Iran’s new strategic approach which is geared towards dominance of the broader Gulf region”.

The fact that Turkey and Pakistan border Iran means they could “exercise a different kind of leverage” on Tehran, he added.

A source close to the Saudi military and government told AFP before the signing that although the agreement had been under discussion for a long time, “the latest developments in the region expedite it”.

Andreas Krieg of King’s College London said the deal showed a clear desire to diversify alliances beyond the United States.

“Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan are not trying to replace the United States,” he said.

“They are building the capacity to protect their interests when Washington cannot or will not do so.”

Riyadh, in particular, he added, “wants several layers of security rather than one American umbrella”, after the shock of the Iran war.

The deal will support Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to become an organiser of regional security and diversify its defence umbrella, said Krieg. Turkey and Pakistan gain political clout and access to potential Saudi investments, he added.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Mecca on Friday, the Turkish presidency said on X, sharing an image of the meeting.

Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir also travelled to the Gulf kingdom for the signing.

– Renewed Houthi attacks –

Saudi Arabia and Pakistan had already announced a mutual defence pact in 2025, a move that drew attention because Pakistan is the Muslim world’s only nuclear-armed state.

The deal also comes as a truce between Riyadh and the Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen has broken down. The Houthis have launched attacks on Saudi soil and declared a maritime blockade against Saudi Arabia, which they have attempted to enforce by attacking Saudi tankers.

The Houthis, backed by Iran, have added pressure to Gulf energy exporters — already under strain from Tehran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz — by threatening Red Sea shipping.

Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition backing Yemen’s internationally recognised government against the Houthis since 2015.

A truce was agreed four years ago which largely held until hostilities broke out again in recent weeks.

On Thursday, the Houthis killed at least 58 Yemeni government troops in missile and drone attacks, a military source said, in one of the conflict’s deadliest days in years.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate continues to rise in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,520.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,530 Iraqi dinars and 1,520 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,525.5 and 1,525 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq to increase production from Kirkuk oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair announced on Thursday plans to increase oil production from the Kirkuk oilfields.

The decision intends to capitalize on a recent agreement with Turkey for exporting oil to the port of Ceyhan.

This move also aims to circumvent the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and increase Iraq’s oil exports via ports on the Mediterranean.

The instruction utilizes the recently expanded Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline deal, with the goal of increasing exports from 180,000 barrels per day to approximately 750,000 barrels per day.

Khudair stated that increasing production lays the groundwork for boosting export volumes through Turkey to 1.5 million barrels per day.

Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) has officially partnered with British Petroleum (BP) to bolster cooperation in oil and natural gas projects in Kirkuk oilfields.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company (NOC) to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s attempts to optimize energy sector investments, increase oil output, and minimize gas flaring.

The enhanced output directly addresses the Iraqi government’s growing deficit as a result of continued maritime restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz.

By producing more petroleum from Kirkuk, Baghdad reduces internal shipping expenses from southern fields while increasing supplies to global markets via outlets on the Mediterranean.

World.title: IT ministry asks Meta to revamp algorithms, submit roadmap to tackle deepfakes
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) has asked Meta to revamp its algorithms and submit a compliance roadmap aimed at curbing deepfakes, propaganda and other manipulated or illegal content on its platforms.

The directive was issued during recent discussions between MeitY officials and Meta, amid growing concerns over the spread of synthetic and manipulated content online, ANI cites.

Meta asked to strengthen content moderation

Officials have asked the social media giant to strengthen its content moderation systems and act faster on takedown requests from authorised government agencies, the sources said.

MeitY also sought greater compliance with data-localisation requirements and asked Meta to work more closely with government agencies to speed up the identification and removal of deepfakes, morphed images and misleading posts.

The government has also pushed for specific algorithmic changes to limit the reach and amplification of propaganda and manipulated media.

Meta outlines technical measures

The directive followed talks in which Meta acknowledged gaps in its existing systems and outlined technical measures it could take to address deepfakes and other synthetic content, the sources said.

During a meeting with MeitY officials on Friday, Meta's technical team explained how the company currently detects and handles harmful content on its platforms.





Officials, however, pressed for more concrete changes to the algorithms governing the spread of such content and sought a clear compliance roadmap from the company.

Both sides agreed to continue discussions on the issue, with another meeting expected next week, ANI reports.

Meta under growing government scrutiny over CSAM

The government's scrutiny of Meta has intensified in recent days over concerns surrounding deepfakes, Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) and other harmful content on its platforms.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg had earlier apologised over errors related to CSAM and deepfake content after concerns were raised by the Indian government.

The latest discussions come as India has tightened its regulatory framework for synthetically generated content, including through amendments to the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules earlier this year. The revised rules introduce additional due-diligence requirements for online intermediaries and seek greater accountability for AI-generated and manipulated content.

World.title: 'Keep your curiosity alive': PM Modi addresses IIT Delhi graduates; highlights rapid tech shift
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday addressed IIT Delhi's 57th Convocation Ceremony, urging graduating students to embrace change, keep learning and remember the mentors who shaped their journey.

Addressing more than 3,000 graduating students, including 587 PhD scholars, as the chief guest, PM Modi congratulated them on completing their studies and asked them to embrace the next phase of their lives. "From orientation to convocation, you must be satisfied with your journey, but also excited about the start of a new chapter," Modi said.

He asked students to "live this moment to the fullest", noting that many were preparing to start their first jobs, move to new cities, launch startups or appear for competitive examinations.

The Prime Minister also urged them not to forget their time at IIT Delhi or the people who supported them. "Carry them as an asset; don't forget them. Before you leave, make sure to meet every member here," he said.

Speaking about the rapidly changing world and technology, the Prime Minister asked students to keep their curiosity and learning instinct alive.

"Today, the world is changing rapidly. Nobody can say what will happen 20-30 years from now.





Keep your curiosity alive in life... Keep your learning instinct alive. Those who learn, win," he said.

He said people who remain open to new situations and challenges can turn difficulties into opportunities. "Challenges become chances for those with courage to find new solutions," Modi said, adding that this was among the things students had learned at IIT Delhi.

"The global power balance is changing every moment and the biggest force behind it is the speed of technology," he said.

The PM also spoke about India's push for self-reliance and the emergence of new sectors for the country's youth. Referring to the semiconductor sector, he said India had begun production at its first semiconductor unit. "I firmly believe that from chips to ships, everything will be made here by your hands," he added.

The Prime Minister also presented IIT Delhi's top honours, including the President's Gold Medal, Director's Gold Medal, Shankar Dayal Sharma Gold Medal and Perfect Ten Gold Medals, to meritorious students.

He said he was proud of the graduating students but that there should have been "more" girls among them. "Just as your families are feeling proud today, I, too, am proud of all of you," he added.

Union Education Minister Prahlad Joshi, who was also present at the ceremony, said PM Modi's vision had made India's education ecosystem "learner-centric, research-driven, and future-ready".

Earlier, the Prime Minister inaugurated Param Pragya, an AI-powered high-performance supercomputing facility at IIT Delhi's Sonipat campus. According to the PMO, the facility will strengthen the institute's capabilities in AI, data science, advanced computing and interdisciplinary research.

World.title: 'Is India truly independent?' Congress targets Centre over US Bill on Russia sanctions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress Rajya Sabha member Pawan Khera on Saturday attacked the PM Modi-led Centre over a US Senate bill proposing tougher sanctions on countries buying Russian oil, questioning whether India is truly free to make its own decisions.

Speaking to news agency ANI in Prayagraj, Khera alleged India was being pressured by other countries over its purchases of Russian oil.

He said, "Does it look like India is truly independent? Anyone who comes blackmails India; anyone who comes along dictates terms, saying you can buy oil from here, you can buy this much, you cannot buy that much. Demand answers from those who go around the country calling themselves 'Vishwaguru' but lack the courage to even enter Parliament.

They lack the courage because all these issues would be raised, and they would be held accountable for everything.

"

His remarks came after the US Senate passed the Russia Sanctions Bill, named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham. The bill could impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five countries, including India and China, that buy Russian crude oil and natural gas.

Khera also backed the protesting students in Jharkhand and said their concerns should be addressed as the agitation over alleged irregularities in the recruitment process continues.





"Can the mistreatment of women at Jantar Mantar, the use of pellet guns, or the firing of AK-47 in Bihar ever be erased from history? Rahul ji spoke about the situation in Jharkhand as well. Our delegation met with the students there, and the local government is also engaging in dialogue, trying to find a way forward," he further said.

The Jharkhand protests began after the results of the 14th JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination were announced on July 5.

Aspirants have alleged irregularities in the recruitment process and have been holding round-the-clock protests and an indefinite sit-in, demanding transparency and accountability.

Khera said both the government and the Opposition have a responsibility to address the students' concerns. His remarks came ahead of

's 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' programme in Prayagraj, where the Congress leader is expected to raise issues affecting students and job aspirants.

"Students have certain demands and concerns. Addressing those concerns is the duty of both the ruling party and the opposition. You can see what the ruling party is doing; the government's actions at Jantar Mantar were evident to all. As for the opposition, Rahul Gandhi's daily actions make their stance clear. The message to the youth is clear: you are not alone. The country's opposition stands firmly with you," he told ANI.

World.title: ‘Should have been more’: PM Modi disappointed over 'just one or two' girls among IIT Delhi medal winners

At the event, PM Modi urged IIT Delhi graduates to encourage greater participation and representation of women in academic and professional achievements, noting that only a few female students had received medals at the ceremony.

PM Modi congratulated the award-winning students but said there should have been "more" girls among them.

"Many students have received medals for their achievements. I extend my heartiest congratulations to all of you.

However, it would have been even better if there were a few more girls among them. Sorry. Why just one or two? There should have been more," PM Modi said.

PM Modi presented IIT Delhiâs most prestigious honours, including the Presidentâs Gold Medal, Directorâs Gold Medal, Shankar Dayal Sharma Gold Medal and Perfect Ten Gold Medals.

PM Modi also inaugurated Param Pragya, an AI-powered high-performance supercomputing facility at the Sonipat campus of IIT Delhi.





The Prime Minsiter addressed more than 3,000 graduating students, including 587 PhD scholars, who were conferred their degrees during IIT Delhiâs 57th convocation ceremony.

IIT Delhi Board of Governors Chairperson Harish Salve and institute director Prof Rangan Banerjee felicitated Prime Minister Modi and Union Minister Pralhad Joshi during the ceremony.

World.title: ‘Honey-trapped’ IAF officer held for allegedly sharing classified defence data
World.content:
The officer was under surveillance by the IAF intelligence wing before he was arrested and handed over to law enforcement agencies.

NEW DELHI: An Indian Air Force (IAF) Wing Commander has been arrested for allegedly leaking sensitive defence information after being honey-trapped through social media by Pakistani intelligence operatives, officials said.According to an ANI report, the officer was under surveillance by the IAF intelligence wing before he was arrested and handed over to law enforcement agencies. Delhi Police sources said he is currently in judicial custody and has been booked under provisions of the Official Secrets Act for allegedly sharing classified information and confidential defence-related documents.IAF officials said, "He was under active surveillance and was handed over to the suitable law enforcement agencies. Due to proactive measures, he was caught. The IAF has zero tolerance for such activities."Sources said the officer allegedly fell victim to a honey trap operated by Pakistani intelligence personnel through social media. He is also accused of installing data-stealing software on a colleague's mobile phone in an alleged attempt to gain access to the device.The arrest followed specific inputs shared by the IAF intelligence wing with the Delhi Police, sources said.Further investigation into the case is underway.The incident comes amid continued concerns over attempts by Pakistani intelligence operatives to target Indian personnel and civilians through social media-based honey traps.Last year, Rajasthan Police arrested an Alwar resident, identified as Mangat Singh, for allegedly spying for Pakistan's intelligence agency ISI. Police said a surveillance operation had been launched in the state following Operation Sindoor, during which Singh's activities in the cantonment area of Alwar were found to be suspicious.According to police, Singh had allegedly been honey-trapped by a female Pakistani handler using the pseudonym Isha Sharma. The handler reportedly offered him money in exchange for cooperation. Police said Singh had remained in contact with Pakistani handlers through social media platforms for around two years.

World.title: Sick teen dies as ambulance gets stuck in mud for hours in J&K's Rajouri
World.content:
J-K's Rajouri landslide

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A 17-year-old girl died while being taken to hospital in Jammu and Kashmir's Rajouri district after the vehicle carrying her remained stuck in mud for nearly three hours. The district administration has suspended a government engineer and ordered an inquiry into the incident.The girl, a resident of remote Methyani village, had fallen seriously ill on Friday and was being taken to Government Medical College (GMC), Rajouri, when the vehicle became stranded following a mudslide at Chak Methyani, officials told news agency PTI.Volunteers later managed to pull the vehicle out, but the girl's condition deteriorated and she died while she was being taken to the hospital, according to officials.The incident occurred on the Chak Methyani-Panglar-Kotecharwal road, which serves as the only road link for several remote villages in the area. The road was washed away near Methyani during last year's monsoon and had subsequently been restored temporarily.The same stretch was hit by another mudslide around two weeks ago, leaving the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) road unmotorable, officials said.According to the report submitted by the Additional Deputy Commissioner (ADC), Kotranka, the girl had been suffering from an illness for nearly a month and had previously been admitted to Government Medical College Hospital, Jammu. She was discharged around two weeks ago, but her condition worsened again, prompting her family to take her to GMC Rajouri.The ADC's report said the blocked road resulted in a delay of nearly two to three hours. It also found that the stretch remained in "extremely poor condition" due to landslides and deep ditches, making it unfit for vehicular movement.The report further noted that residents of Narla Bamble, Kotecharwal and Panglar continued to face difficulties in transporting patients, food grains and fertilisers.The district administration said the executive engineer, PMGSY division Rajouri, had informed officials through an official WhatsApp group that the road had been restored and was "trafficable". However, subsequent verification by the ADC found otherwise.Taking note of the report, district development commissioner (DDC) Rajouri Abhishek Sharma ordered the immediate suspension of the assistant executive engineer (AEE), PMGSY Sub-Division Kalakote, who was in charge of the road project, pending an inquiry.The DDC said the failure to restore the road despite repeated directions indicated "prima facie negligence and non-compliance with official instructions".The executive engineer has also been asked to explain why disciplinary proceedings should not be initiated against him for allegedly misreporting the road's status and failing to ensure its timely restoration. His salary has been withheld pending consideration of his explanation.The additional district development commissioner (ADDC), Rajouri, has been directed to conduct a detailed inquiry and submit a comprehensive report within seven days.

World.title: A love letter to the Nilgiris: Tall Tales & Short Stories celebrates the hills
World.content:
The Nilgiris, where hills, mist, and clouds come together to create a surreal landscape of quiet beauty. These blue mountains have long inspired writers and poets. Joining the list is a group of avid readers from The Coonoor Book Club that gathers to discuss books over tea and varkeys. Members of the book club have recently brought out a collection of short stories, poems and essays titled Tall Tales & Short Stories, published by Ukiyoto. Edited by Nimi Kurian and Nina Varghese both of whom used to be journalists, and Theresa Varghese, the book features the work of 13 writers, all of whom are based in the Nilgiris.

Each piece carries the distinct flavour of the hills: think tea gardens, forest roads, grasslands, dinner parties with roast and pudding, the Toy Train that chugs along winding tracks and of course delicious gossip about neighbours. The idea for the anthology took shape during one of the book club’s meets. “My sister Nina and I started the club the year before last,” says Nimi. “There are lots of readers in Coonoor, we thought we should get together and discuss books.”

Members decide on a book to read, meeting at one of their homes to talk about it. “Each one takes turns to talk about what they like best,” says Nina, adding that their favourites include Perumal Murugan’s One Part Woman and Abraham Verghese’s The Covenant of Water. During one of their meetings, the members hit upon the idea to write stories on the Nilgiris. “People were quite enthusiastic, but most of them are first time writers. So, they were a bit nervous about getting down to writing. But then finally, they did it,” says Nimi. The book has small descriptions about each of the writers towards the end.

Tall Tales & Short Stories has some charming pieces. Nimi’s story Coffee’s Ready, that describes at length a dinner party hosted at The Bungalow by one Mrs Claire Williamson, is absolutely hilarious. She has also written a ghost story: what’s the hills without haunted bungalows with creaking floorboards and overgrown gardens?

Johnny John’s verses titled Nilgiris – Scapes and Scaped is an ode to all things Nilgiris, from the Neelakurinji, walks to Lamb’s Rock and Tenerife Hill, to shuttle games at the Club and warm bread with fish pie. Missy Ma by Shernaz Sethna talks about her life as a new bride in Coonoor’s palatial West Croft, where she moves in from Nagpur after her wedding. In her heartwarming essay, Shernaz recounts how she warmed up to life in the household and her friendship with Devadas, the cook and butler ‘who ruled with an iron fist’. She even shares her Parsi roast chicken recipe, a dish that she first cooked at the bungalow, under the watchful eyes of Devadas.

The stories, Nimi shares, were written last year. “We received most of them in January, and spent three months editing them, followed by some back and forth, and then the design was finalised,” she adds. Nimi left Coonoor in 1978 and moved back recently after a busy life as a journalist in Chennai. How does it feel to be back? “I thought it would be difficult to fit in again, but actually it was like wearing an old shoe,” says the 65-year-old.

Her sister Nina, with whom she started the book club, says that writing about the Nilgiris was a “gratifying process.” She says, “This is because all of us were writing about a place we love very much, one in which we are very invested in.” She adds that a sequel is in the pipeline. “It too will be based on Coonoor,” says the third-generation Coonoorian.

Tall Tales & Short Stories is available online

World.title: Stalled Erode-Karur road widening work causes hardship to motorists
World.content:
The stalled road widening work between Solar and Gatepudhur on the Erode-Karur Road (State Highway 84) has caused considerable inconvenience to motorists, who have urged the State Highways Department to resume and complete the work at the earliest.

The road is one of the busiest arterial routes connecting Erode and Karur and an important link to destinations in the southern districts. Buses, lorries, commercial vehicles, and other traffic use the road throughout the day. In 2019, former Chief Minister Edappadi K. Palaniswami announced a proposal to convert the road into a four-lane carriageway. However, following a change in government, the project was kept in abeyance. The DMK government subsequently announced that the road would be widened in phases.

Foundation stones were laid on February 20, 2026, for widening the stretches between Solar and Gatepudhur and between Solangapalayam and Kangeyampalayam. The works, estimated at ₹55 crore, are being executed under the Integrated Road Development Scheme 2026-27.

The initial phase involved removing trees along both sides of the five-km Solar-Gatepudhur stretch. Though the work progressed at a brisk pace initially, it subsequently slowed down and stopped in June. Motorists said only culverts had been constructed at multiple locations and no further work had been taken up for nearly two months. “Only barricades have been placed near the culvert construction sites,” said P. Anand of Kollukattumedu.

Uneven stretches pose danger

Road users said several portions of the road remained dug up, while gravel was yet to be laid in some places. More than a foot of soil has been excavated along the existing road for the widening work. “The uneven stretches pose a threat to motorists, particularly during the night,” said a resident of Lakkapuram Naal Road.

Erode MP K.E. Prakash has also raised concerns over roads being left unattended after being dug up for infrastructure works. He said roads across Erode district had been left incomplete by contractors, causing hardship to motorists and the public. He urged the authorities to ensure that such works were completed within the stipulated time and roads restored without delay.

Residents said the incomplete work on the busy Erode-Karur route had increased the risk of accidents, particularly as the road handles substantial passenger and freight traffic. They urged the authorities to resume and complete the widening work at the earliest, before the monsoon intensifies, to ensure the safety of road users.

World.title: Kerala should adopt a rights-based approach to children with disabilities, says panel
World.content:
Kerala should become a model State that can ensure equality, dignity, and equal opportunity for all the children with disabilities, the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has said.

The recommendation has been made in a report on challenges — physical, emotional, intellectual, and developmental — faced by disabled children. It was was submitted by the commission to the government earlier this year.

The report, prepared following consultations with functionaries at State and district levels, urges the State to adopt a rights-based approach, calling for viewing them not just as beneficiaries of services but also recognising them as citizens with rights.

The commission has recommended a single-window system to ensure that schemes for children with disabilities and benefits —including social security pension, scholarships, treatment-rehabilitation aid, travel allowance, and distribution of assistive devices— reach them in a transparent and time-bound manner. At present, these are implemented through various departments, leading to lack of coordination, delays, complications in documents, and lack of information.

The report underscores the importance of early detection of disabilities in children to provide comprehensive treatment and rehabilitation. Services of experts such as paediatricians, clinical psychologist, psychiatrist, and therapists should be ensured permanently in taluk hospitals

Mobile screening teams should be formed for direct screening of children in anganwadis and schools in areas that are remote or difficult to access such as hilly regions.

Home care, palliative care, and other services should be ensured at the doorstep of children who have severe disabilities or are bed-ridden.

Disability certificates and UDID (Unique Disability Identification Card) card should be made available to eligible children. Steps should also be taken to organise camps at the panchayat level to avoid delays in this respect, the report adds.

The report calls for appointing special educators in all government, aided, and recognised unaided schools to ensure school participation and social inclusion of differently abled children. Need-based support will prevent them the children from dropping out of school, it says.

It moots an inclusive evaluation system that considers each child’s abilities, individual education goals, and reasonable accommodation.

Another recommendation is setting up of district disability centres in order for services such as early identification, therapies, counselling, educational support, and training for parents can be provided under a single umbrella.

It stresses the need for police stations that have personnel who have received training in accepting complaints related to children with disabilities, taking their statements, and conducting investigations. Steps should also be taken to provide the services of sign language interpreter, special educator, and support persons to help them in investigations related to them, the commission recommends.

World.title: Many aspects of Ayodhya Ram temple donation ‘theft’ probe done: U.P. Police
World.content:
The investigation team in charge of the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya has completed probing various aspects of the case, Senior Superintendent of Police of Ayodhya Gaurav Grover said.

The probe has to be completed in 90 days and the chargesheet has to be filed in court by the end of next month, the SSP said.

Speaking to reporters on Saturday (August 8, 2026), Mr. Grover said the SIT is not conducting any separate investigation and is coordinating in the police investigation in the role of a high-level probe adviser. The chairman of the SIT is Lucknow IGP Kiran S, who has five years of experience in the CBI, he added.

Mr. Grover added that he is continuously keeping a watch on the investigation at the local level and also giving advice.

As per the FIR in the donation theft case registered on June 25 at the Ram Janmabhoomi police station in Ayodhya, police had sent eight accused to jail.

These included former temple trust general secretary Champat Rai’s close aide Tinnu Yadav, counting in-charge Subhash Srivastava, Ramashankar Mishra, Manish Yadav, Karunesh, Lavkush Mishra, Anukalp and Avinash Shukla.

Police took all eight accused on remand and interrogated them.

The Supreme Court on July 27 was informed by the Uttar Pradesh government that it has set up a four-member special investigating team (SIT) headed by IGP Kiran S to probe the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya.

The top court asked the State Government to include a forensic auditor as the fifth member of the SIT, which will submit its first status report within two weeks.

A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana took note of the submissions of Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the State Government, that the SIT was formed through a notification issued on July 25 following the apex court’s suggestion.

The law officer said that besides the IGP, who was part of the team which had investigated whether an FIR was needed to be lodged, the SIT will include a DIG-rank officer, a senior superintendent of police and an additional SP.

On July 20, the Bench had asked the Uttar Pradesh government to apprise it about the possibility of setting up an SIT to probe the alleged embezzlement of donations.

Investigating officer Circle Officer Ayodhya Ashutosh Tiwari said that based on facts that emerged during questioning in the investigation, documentation is being updated and the investigation is being taken forward.

Kalika Mishra, the president of the Faizabad Bar Association, said that the Bar is determined to take action against Champat Rai, Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao.

He said that if the names of the three were not included in the FIR, then soon they are going to move to the court to get the FIR registered against them.

World.title: Environmentalists flag land use changes in Periya-Pakranthalam elephant corridor
World.content:
Environmentalists have raised serious concerns over the alleged land use changes in the Periya-Pakranthalam (Periya-Pannippad) elephant corridor, warning that ongoing excavation and construction activities could obstruct elephant movement, worsen habitat fragmentation, and trigger a rise in human-elephant conflict across north Kerala.

The Animal and Nature Ethics Community Trust has submitted a representation to senior forest department officials seeking immediate intervention to protect the ecologically sensitive corridor. The Trust’s representative T.S. Santosh has urged the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests, the Chief Wildlife Warden, the Chief Conservator of Forests (Northern Circle), the Wildlife Warden of Kottiyur Wildlife Division, and the Divisional Forest Officer (North Wayanad) to halt ongoing land use changes and restore the functional integrity of the corridor.

“The Periya-Pakranthalam corridor is a vital landscape connectivity that ensures elephant movement across the Aralam-Kottiyur-Periya-Kannavam-Pakranthalam-Padinharathara landscape. Any blockage at Pakranthalam will inevitably increase human-elephant conflict in the surrounding areas,” Mr. Santosh said.

The corridor is one of the most important movement routes for Asian elephants within the Wayanad Elephant Reserve, enabling seasonal migration, maintaining genetic exchange between elephant populations, and reducing encounters with human settlements.

The Trust alleged that the Pakranthalam bottleneck is already under considerable pressure due to existing obstructions, including a mobile communication tower and related infrastructure buildings on private land, and the busy Mananthavady-Kuttiyadi road, all of which restrict elephant movement.

Mr. Santosh said express excavation and large-scale earth removal activities were being carried out in the bottleneck area by a private landowner, potentially altering the terrain permanently and encouraging further conversion of land for non-forest purposes.

“If these activities continue unchecked, the effective width of the corridor will be narrowed or completely blocked, forcing elephants into nearby settlements and agricultural lands. This will inevitably result in increased crop damage, destruction of property, threat to human life, and greater risk of elephants being killed or injured in road accidents,“ he said.

The Trust also contended that such alterations could undermine long-term conservation efforts in the Wayanad Elephant Reserve and weaken one of the region’s most critical wildlife corridors.

Citing directions issued by the Supreme Court on elephant corridor protection, including orders relating to the Segur Plateau elephant corridor, Mr. Santosh stated that authorities are under legal obligation to identify, inspect, and remove illegal obstructions from elephant corridors.

The court has also held that no construction should be permitted within such corridors and that the principles apply to functional wildlife movement routes, not merely those formally notified, he said.

Seeking urgent intervention, the ANEC Trust demanded an immediate field inspection of the Pakrandalam bottleneck, verification of the legality of recent excavation and land use changes, and suspension of all activities affecting elephant movement. It also sought action under the Wildlife Protection Act, Forest Conservation Laws, and other applicable statutes wherever violations are detected.

Mr. Santosh further called for a scientific assessment of the corridor, coordination among forest, revenue, and local self-government authorities to prevent further encroachments, and the constitution of a high-level expert committee under Project Elephant to assess the corridor’s ecological status, recommend restoration measures, and prepare an action taken report within 30 days.

B.N. Anjankumar, Chief Conservator of Forest (Northern Circle) told The Hindu that a case had already been registered under the Kerala Promotion of Tree Growth in Non Forest Areas Act for alleged unauthorised felling of trees on private land. “Permission from the Forest department is mandatory before cutting notified trees even on private non-forest land. Action has been initiated under the relevant provision,” he said.

Mr. Anjankumar said the land belongs to private owners but shares its boundary with vested forest. While land use permissions fall under the jurisdiction of the Revenue department, local self government institutions and other statutory authorities, any commercial development or large scale alteration in such a sensitive area could adversly affect elephant movement.

“The area was largely unmanaged agricultural land earlier. If commercial activities or intensive land development come up, it could increase human presence and interfere with its corridor functionality. We have brought the matter to the notice of the district administration, the geologists, and the local authorities. Further action will be reviewed after consultation with the divisional forest officer,” he said.

World.title: Pinarayi Vijayan accuses the UDF government of opening the door for the RSS to indoctrinate school children
World.content:
Leader of the Opposition, Pinarayi Vijayan, on Saturday (August 8, 2026), accused the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government of opening the door for the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to indoctrinate impressionable young children in profoundly divisive nationalistic ideology.

Also read | UDF govt. has surrendered to RSS agenda: Pinarayi Vijayan

Mr. Vijayan told a press conference in Kannur that the UDF government had callously allowed a politically loaded question whitewashing RSS ideologue V.D. Savarkar’s “treacherous role” in the Independence Struggle.

Mr. Vijayan’s latest foray against the government came against the backdrop of a controversial question that figured in the “Freedom Quiz” programme for students in lower primary schools in the Manjeshwar, Kumbla and Kasargod educational sub-districts in North Kerala.

The question ostensibly sought to test the historical knowledge of children by asking “which freedom fighter received the most punishment from the British. The “answer key” identified the “freedom fighter” as V.D. Savarkar.

The question had caused quite an uproar in Kerala with the Students Federation of India (SFI) and Muslim Student Federation (MSF) demanding that the government order an enquiry to find out who approved the question and how it was included in the “Freedom Quiz” in schools in the run-up to the 79th Independence Day Celebrations on August 15.

Mr. Vijayan accused the government of giving a leg-up to the RSS’s Machiavellian attempts to rewrite history in the Sangh Parivar’s Hindu majoritarian perspective.

“Savarkar had betrayed the Independence Movement by siding with the British. He urged youth to stay away from the struggle and secured release from prison by writing clemency petitions that betrayed the national cause. Savarkar met the British Viceroy and declared loyalty”, Mr. Vijayan said.

Mr. Vijayan portrayed Savarkar as a deeply polarising figure who propounded a two-nation theory that depicted Muslims and other minorities, including Christians, as aliens and fifth columnists.

“Surprisingly, the Congress, which loudly claims the legacy of the Independence movement, has no objection to the RSS seeking to subtly inject its us-versus-them communally divisive narrative into Kerala’s progressive and secular school curriculum”, Mr. Vijayan said.

Mr. Vijayan said Congress leadership’s “slow drift to the far right” was on full display at the swearing-in ceremony of the UDF government. “The incumbent disposition sanctioned the full rendering of the Vande Mataram. It gave short shrift to the Constituent Assembly’s enlightened reasoning that only the first two metrical compositions of the song were secular, civic and inclusive, and hence could be rendered at State functions. Nevertheless, the founding fathers reasoned that the subsequent versions had a pronounced Hindu religious tint that risked undermining national unity and should not supplant the national anthem”, Mr. Vijayan added.

World.title: Five arrested for blackmailing, assaulting man in Choolaimedu
World.content:
The Choolaimedu police arrested five people on Saturday (August 8, 2026) for allegedly blackmailing and assaulting a 30-year-old man.

A senior city police official said Sudharsan, a resident of Padmanabha Nagar who works for a pharmaceutical company, had recently married Krishnaveni. He had allegedly contacted a Namitha, who lived near his house, and spoken to her about marrying her.

According to the police, she recorded their conversation and, along with her lawyer friend, Monisha, allegedly demanded ₹5 lakh from Sudharsan to keep the recording secret. The two women allegedly contacted Sudharsan a few days ago and, when he told them that he did not have the money, assaulted him, the police said.

Based on a complaint filed by the Choolaimedu police, a team after conducting an investigation arrested Namitha, 21, Monisha, 26, her husband Balakrishnan, 30, Ganesh, 28, and Sivaranjani, 21.

They were arrested under six sections, including charges of illegal confinement, criminal intimidation, and causing grievous hurt. All five individuals were produced before the Saidapet Court and remanded to judicial custody.

World.title: ‘Don’t behave like Delhi police’: Abhijeet Dipke seeks removal of ‘rude’ cop from security duty at his home
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) convenor Abhijeet Dipke confronted a police sub-inspector (PSI) deployed as part of the security detail at his home in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for allegedly preventing people from meeting him and sought his removal from duty there.

He accused the officer of being “rude” to visitors and trying to restrict and monitor people entering his residence in the Waluj MIDC area of the central Maharashtra city.

Mr. Dipke, who was provided security following threats and to manage the crowd at his home, also alleged that state CID personnel in plainclothes were roaming near his residence and then reporting in a social media group named ‘Hit Spray’.

A couple of videos showing the CJP founder speaking to a senior police official over the phone and a PSI at his residence went viral on social media platforms on Friday (August 7, 2026).

During the conversations, Mr. Dipke is heard reprimanding the PSI and also seeking his removal from the security staff deployed at his home.

‘’What is the problem in allowing people to come into my home when I am asking them to come in? Why are you behaving like the Delhi police? No problem has occurred till today. I am seeing you for the first time. You (police) will not tell me whom I should meet and whom I should not meet,” Mr. Dipke is heard telling the PSI, who is in civil dress, in one of the videos.

‘’You please go out, I don’t want you in my house,’’ the 30-year-old activist told the PSI, whom he identified only as Suresh.

Also read| Force of law: On the Delhi police

In the second video, Mr. Dipke is seen complaining to the senior police official over the phone about the PSI.

“A PSI named Suresh has come here, and he is very rude to people coming to meet me. He is telling people to go out. Is this being done deliberately? I don’t want him; remove him from here,” the CJP founder is heard telling the police official.

On the same call, he alleged state CID personnel were moving around his home.

“A reporter told me some CID people were spotted near my home. When police tried to remove them, they revealed they were from the CID. The reporter also saw that a WhatsApp group was open on the phone of one of the CID personnel and it was named ‘Hit Spray’. The reporter told me they were sending their reports from here,” Dipke claimed.

Despite repeated attempts, DCP Pankaj Atulkar, whose jurisdiction covers the Waluj MIDC area, was not available for comments on claims made by the CJP founder.

World.title: Rana Sanaullah says PML-N will form govt in AJK with two-thirds majority
World.content:
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah said on Saturday that the PML-N would form the government in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) with a two-thirds majority.

He made the remarks while addressing a rally in Bagh ahead of the third phase of elections in the region. The third phase was originally slated to be held in Poonch division, but will now only be held in its Bagh and Haveli districts due to law and order concerns.

Addressing the rally, Sanaullah said that in the first two phases, the PML-N had secured 24 seats. He said that six more seats were required for a two-thirds majority government.

He asserted that four more seats would be added following the August 10 polls, while five more would be added when polls would be held in the rest of Poonch Division.

“The PML-N will form a government with a two-thirds majority. The people of Kashmir have trusted PML-N. They have trusted Mian Nawaz Sharif. They have trusted the development in Punjab,” he said.

He urged supporters to show up and cast their votes on Monday to help PML-N secure a victory, promising that a PML-N government would prioritise development projects.

He also said that the PML-N government would also meet with members of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). The JAAC, which has been demanding the abolishment of 12 seats in the local legislature reserved for refugees from Indian-held Kashmir, has been holding protests in the region for several weeks now.

“When this government will be set up, with a two-thirds majority, they will sit with [JAAC] representatives. Their first task will be to resolve this issue.”

He said that 99 per cent of JAAC protesters were “our brothers”, adding that they were patriotic Kashmiris and Pakistanis.

He added that the remainder were focused on creating divisions within the nation. He urged cooperation between a future PML-N government and the people of AJK in “exposing and defeating” those divisive elements.

“We will defeat them and we will make Kashmir prosperous,” Sanaullah said.

He further added that in the past, all large-scale development projects in AJK were only completed when the PML-N was in power in the Centre and in the region.

He urged the people of Bagh to go out and vote on Monday, stressing that “all of Bagh should be involved in the government”.

He added that PML-N founder Nawaz Sharif would fulfil his promises to the people of AJK by nominating one of the three PML-N candidates in Bagh as the future prime minister of AJK.

Sanaullah added that Nawaz has already mentioned that he would sit down with the future AJK prime minister to discuss development projects in the region.

World.title: Mir Raza Ali's body exhumed following restoration of original medical board
World.content:
The body of Institute of Business Administration (IBA) graduate and businessman Mir Raza Ali was exhumed on Saturday, his father’s lawyer said after the Sindh government restored the original medical board.

“The investigation officer was present when the body was exhumed and the examination was carried out. All eight people of the medical team were present; the parents were also nearby. And most importantly, a judicial magistrate … was present,” he told the media in Karachi.

Medical board controversy

The exhumation, which was scheduled for Friday morning, was postponed after the deceased’s family objected to the abrupt reconstitution of the medical board and inclusion of members from outside Karachi division.

On Thursday, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Raza’s father, Mir Hussain Ali, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation.

The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed as the convener. Prof Dr Naseem Ahmed of Dow University of Health Sciences, Dr Farah Waseem of Jinnah Sindh Medical University, Amir Hassan Khan of Citizens Police Liaison Committee, Additional Police Surgeon Dr Sirichand, Dr Kamran Khan and Dr Daniyal Mirza of Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre and Dr Mohammed Yaseen, the admin in-charge of the police surgeon office, were the other members of the board.

However, in the small hours of Friday morning, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department.

While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed to Prof Dr Zakiuddin from DUHS, Prof Dr Kazi Akbar and Prof Dr Abid Hussain Chang from Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences and Hyderabad Police Surgeon Dr Waseem Khan.

On Friday morning, Raza’s family was present at the Tariq Road graveyard for the exhumation. Standing alongside Raza’s father, Nasir had accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts and held the police, health department and the Sindh government responsible for the delay.

More to follow

World.title: OIC welcomes Pak-Saudi-Turkiye joint defence pact, calls it 'important strategic step'
World.content:
The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) has welcomed the signing of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, terming it an “important strategic step”.

The pact aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers the three states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

In a statement posted on X, OIC Secretary General Hissein Brahim Taha expressed his “strong appreciation and support” for the agreement, describing it as an “important strategic step” that reflected the three countries’ commitment to strengthening regional and international cooperation.

Taha said the agreement constitutes “a fundamental pillar for supporting security and stability in the region and across the Muslim world”.

He added that it embodies a “shared resolve to address growing security challenges and strengthen solidarity and constructive partnerships” among the OIC member states.

The OIC is the second largest organisation after the United Nations, with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye among its 57 members.

The OIC chief also praised the “tireless efforts and wise leadership” of the three countries that culminated in the signing of the “historic agreement”.

He expressed hope that the pact would contribute to achieving peace and prosperity in the region and the wider international community.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed on Friday at a trilateral summit in Makkah, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed the pact during the “Makkah Al-Mukarramah Summit for Joint Defence”.

Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif were also present at the signing ceremony.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

Saudi Arabia’s Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Rayed Krimly has said the new tripartite agreement “does not supersede or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between these countries”.

Meanwhile, the Turkish president said the pact targets no country and remains open to participation of other friendly nations seeking peace.

PM Shehbaz undertook a three-day visit to Saudi Arabia from August 6 to 8, while Erdogan made a one-day trip to attend the summit.

On Saturday morning, the prime minister paid a visit to Masjid-i-Nabvi in Madina.

He then departed for Pakistan from the Madina airport, where he was seen off by Madina Governor Prince Salman bin Sultan Al Saud.

PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, also a former foreign minister, hailed the agreement as a “significant milestone” in the country’s history.

In a post on X, he noted that the pact was a “historic development that will further strengthen our defence capabilities”.

“This agreement is not only a guarantee of a stable and secure future for Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye, but also a historic document for regional and global peace,” he emphasised.

The PPP chairman also praised the roles of PM Shehbaz and CDF Munir “in making the agreement possible”.

Bahrain, Somalia welcome pact

In a statement issued by its foreign ministry, Bahrain welcomed the agreement as a “key addition to the broader regional defence architecture”.

Bahrain said it viewed the pact as a “strategic partnership between equal partners, driven by a shared commitment to safeguard regional and global stability while bolstering credible deterrence”.

The foreign ministry “highlighted the formidable defence capabilities and military expertise of the three nations, noting their proven track record in serving regional security, stability, and honouring international commitments”.

The pact “complements and enhances the collective defence systems of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) through solidarity and strategic integration”, Bahrain noted.

“Reaffirming that Saudi Arabia’s security is integral to its own, Bahrain expressed full support for all initiatives that protect national sovereignty, safeguard territorial integrity, and advance political solutions to regional issues,” the statement read.

Somalia, whose defence minister paid a visit to Pakistan earlier this week, also congratulated the three signatories.

In a statement, Somalia’s defence ministry termed the signing “a historic milestone in strengthening collective security, advancing defence cooperation, and building a strategic partnership capable of addressing shared security challenges”.

The ministry expressed confidence that the agreement “will make a significant contribution to enhancing regional peace and stability”.

While the signing of the agreement comes in the backdrop of heightened tensions in the Middle East arising from the US-Israel war on Iran, the pact was under deliberation months before the conflict began.

World.title: Captain martyred, 7 terrorists killed in intelligence-based operation in Hangu: ISPR
World.content:
The military’s media affairs wing said on Saturday that a captain was martyred while seven terrorists were killed during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Hangu district.

In a statement, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said security forces conducted an IBO in Hangu on Friday following reports about the presence of terrorists belonging to Fitna al Khawarij — a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

During the operation, troops effectively engaged the terrorists, it said.

“In desperation, the khawarij took refuge inside a mosque, blatantly disregarding the sanctity of the place of worship. In ensuing fire exchange, seven khawarij belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khawarij were sent to hell,” it said.

The statement went on to say that during the exchange of fire, 27-year-old Captain Hamza Akram, a resident of Punjab’s Narowal district who was “leading his troops from front and relentlessly pursuing” the terrorists, embraced martyrdom.

“Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed khawarij, who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities against the security forces and law enforcement agencies as well as killing of innocent civilians,” it said.

ISPR said that a sanitisation operation was being conducted to eliminate any other Indian-sponsored terrorists in the area.

President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the martyred captain, saying, “The motherland pays its profound tribute to the great sacrifice of its brave son.”

“The entire nation is indebted to the eternal sacrifices of these brave sons for the motherland,” the president added, offering prayers for the bereaved family.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed deep grief over Captain Akram’s martyrdom while hailing his courage and devotion, state-run APP reported.

In a statement issued by his office, PM Shehbaz lauded the security forces for eliminating seven terrorists “operating under the Indian patronage”.

“The nation will never forget the sacrifices of its brave sons,” the press release quoted him as saying. He prayed for the captain’s elevated ranks and for patience for his family.

The prime minister reiterated that operations against Fitna al Khawarij would continue till complete elimination of terrorism.

“The sacrifices rendered by our brave armed forces and law-enforcement agencies for the defence, peace and security of the country and nation will not go in vain,” he asserted.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also paid tribute to the martyred captain and offered his condolences to the bereaved family. He said that the officer had paid the ultimate sacrifice for the homeland and would remain alive in our hearts.

A day earlier, ISPR said 10 terrorists were killed in two separate engagements in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. It said that in the first encounter, a group of terrorists attempted to attack security forces’ checkposts in Azam Warsak area in South Waziristan, which was effectively thwarted, resulting in the deaths of eight terrorists.

“In another encounter that took place in Dir district, own troops successfully neutralised two more khawarij,” it added.

Terrorist commander killed in Bannu

Separately, security forces killed a key terrorist commander, identified as Jamidullah, during an operation in Jani Khel area of KP’s Bannu district, a security official said.

The official said that the terrorist commander was involved in terrorist activities and was considered a quadcopter expert.

The official said that security forces conducted the operation in Jani Khel on the basis of intelligence reports, during which Jamidullah was targeted and killed.

World.title: Trump administration to invest $3 billion in minerals projects to boost US defence supply chains
World.content:
The US government will invest $3 billion in critical minerals and battery projects as part of a push to increase domestic production and boost national security and industrial policy, US President Donald Trump said on Friday.

“We’re reclaiming America’s rightful place as the minerals superpower of the world,” Trump told more than 200 mining executives, educators, investors and fellow politicians at a roundtable at the State Department aimed at supporting the industry, which he said had not received enough attention from Washington in recent years.

He announced a slew of investments during his speech, including a $1.4bn conditional loan from the Defence Department’s Office of Strategic Capital for Sila Nanotechnologies, which makes lithium-ion battery parts.

The OSC also extended a $400 million conditional loan to scandium miner Sunrise Energy Metals and a $150m conditional loan to magnet developer Niron Magnetics.

The US Export-Import Bank will lend $58m to Westwater Resources, Global Advanced Metals and 5E Advanced Materials, which Reuters reported earlier on Friday.

“Critical minerals are the raw materials of American strength that power everything from advanced weaponry to automobiles, and we want these essential products to be mined, refined and made right here in the USA,” Trump said.

Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and National Security Council official David Copley attended the announcement.

Weapons stockpiles drive mineral demand

The White House needs critical minerals to replenish weapons stockpiles depleted during the Iran conflict and reduce US dependence on Chinese supply chains.

Several executives came with gifts for Trump. Tom Albanese, chairman of deep-sea mining firm American Ocean Minerals, gave Trump a gold replica of a nodule that the company hopes to mine from the Pacific seabed. Trump last year said he may bypass the UN-backed International Seabed Authority and issue international seabed mining licenses.

Jim Litinsky, CEO of rare earths firm MP Materials, which is financially supported by the Pentagon, gave Trump magnets that had been produced for General Motors in the company’s Texas plant.

Other attendees included executives from Lithium Americas , which is building the largest US lithium mine, NioCorp, which is building a scandium mine to supply defence contractor Lockheed Martin, and Energy Fuels , which received a $725m OSC conditional loan in June.

US forces have burned through large numbers of precision-guided missiles and air-defence interceptors during the five-month-old US- Iran war. Defence officials and lawmakers have warned that replenishing some inventories could take years given existing production constraints. The Trump administration has disputed reports of significant shortages.

Supplies of minerals including rare earths, tungsten, germanium and scandium are essential for manufacturing precision-guided missiles, fighter aircraft, armored vehicles, infrared sensors and other advanced weapons systems, according to Pentagon officials and defence companies.

Mining schools receive funding boost

The Department of Energy on Friday hosted representatives from all 14 accredited US mining schools to promote mining careers and encourage more students to enter the field.

The department announced $100m in grants to help boost educational programs and set a goal of doubling the number of mining-related graduates at the nation’s universities within two years.

“We need to work on some systemic changes to how we as a nation want to offer our brightest students an opportunity to participate in this industry,” said Assistant Energy Secretary Audrey Robertson.

The Pentagon also said it would fund $80m in projects at three US mining schools.

Officials have pointed to China’s extensive network of mining universities as a key advantage in its dominance of global mineral production.

Since returning to office, Trump has launched a $12bn strategic minerals stockpile, backed equity investments in companies developing US mines and processing facilities, and sought to limit defence contractors’ reliance on supplies from China.

The administration says government support is needed to counter decades of Chinese investment that left Beijing dominant in the mining and processing of many strategic minerals.

Australia’s government on Saturday welcomed the Trump administration’s loan to Sunrise Energy Metals, which is developing a scandium mine in the country’s New South Wales state.

“The Sunrise Scandium Project hosts the world’s largest and highest-grade known scandium resource, which has a range of vital aerospace, defence and clean energy applications,” Resources Minister Madeleine King said in a statement.

World.title: Senate, NA leadership pledge closer cooperation for stable parliamentary system
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The leadership of the Senate and National Assembly on Saturday agreed to enhance institutional cooperation and coordination for a stable parliamentary democratic system.

According to a statement issued by the Senate Secretariat, Senate Chairman Yousuf Raza Gilani met National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq and Deputy Speaker Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah at his residence.

The meeting focused on parliamentary affairs, matters of national importance and inter-institutional coordination, it said.

The Senate chairman said close coordination between the two Houses was indispensable for upholding “strong democratic traditions and an effective parliamentary system”.

He added that, “mutual cooperation and effective liaison between the Senate and the National Assembly were essential for the stability of the parliamentary system”.
